verses.english: And fear took hold of all, and they were giving glory to God, saying, "A great prophet has been raised among us," and, "God has visited his people."
verses.greek: ἔλαβεν δὲ φόβος πάντας, καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεὸν λέγοντες ὅτι Προφήτης μέγας ἠγέρθη ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ὅτι Ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And this word about him went out in all Judea and all the surrounding region.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάσῃ τῇ περιχώρῳ.

verses.english: And his learners reported to John about all these things. And calling two of his learners to him, John
verses.greek: Καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν Ἰωάννῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ περὶ πάντων τούτων. καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος δύο τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης

verses.english: sent them to the lord, saying, "Are you the one who is coming, or are we to wait for another?"
verses.greek: ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν κύριον λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;

verses.english: And when the men had come to him, they said, "John the baptiser sent us to you, saying, 'Are you the one who is coming, or are we to wait for another?'"
verses.greek: παραγενόμενοι δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς ἀπέστειλεν ἡμᾶς πρὸς σὲ λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;

verses.english: In that hour he healed many of diseases and scourges and evil spirits, and to many blind people he granted sight.
verses.greek: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς ἀπὸ νόσων καὶ μαστίγων καὶ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν, καὶ τυφλοῖς πολλοῖς ἐχαρίσατο βλέπειν.

verses.english: And answering, he said to them, "Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: blind people see again, lame people walk about, the leprous are being cleansed and deaf people hear, dead people are being raised, the destitute are being given the good news.
verses.greek: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ εἴδετε καὶ ἠκούσατε· τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν, χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν, λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται, πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται·

verses.english: And fortunate is whoever is not tripped up by me."
verses.greek: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί.

verses.english: When John's messengers had gone away, he began to say to the crowds about John, "What did you go out into the desert to gaze at? A reed shaken by wind?
verses.greek: Ἀπελθόντων δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων Ἰωάννου ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς ὄχλους περὶ Ἰωάννου· Τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι; κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον;

verses.english: But what did you go out to see? A person dressed in soft garments? Look, those in splendid clothing and luxury are in royal houses.
verses.greek: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἱματίοις ἠμφιεσμένον; ἰδοὺ οἱ ἐν ἱματισμῷ ἐνδόξῳ καὶ τρυφῇ ὑπάρχοντες ἐν τοῖς βασιλείοις εἰσίν.

verses.english: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
verses.greek: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; προφήτην; ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου.

verses.english: This is the one about whom it is written, 'Look, I send my messenger before your face, who will make ready your way before you.'
verses.greek: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.

verses.english: I tell you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; but the lesser one in the kingdom of God is greater than he."
verses.greek: λέγω ὑμῖν, μείζων ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν Ἰωάννου οὐδείς ἐστιν· ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.

verses.english: And one of the Pharisees was asking him to eat with him; and going into the house of the Pharisee, he reclined at table.
verses.greek: Ἠρώτα δέ τις αὐτὸν τῶν Φαρισαίων ἵνα φάγῃ μετ’ αὐτοῦ· καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Φαρισαίου κατεκλίθη.

verses.english: And look, a woman who was a sinner in the city, learning that he was reclining at table in the house of the Pharisee, brought an alabaster flask of perfumed oil,
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ ἥτις ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἁμαρτωλός, καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα ὅτι κατάκειται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Φαρισαίου, κομίσασα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου

verses.english: and standing behind at his feet, weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and she was wiping them with the hairs of her head, and kissing his feet again and again, and anointing them with the perfumed oil.
verses.greek: καὶ στᾶσα ὀπίσω παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ κλαίουσα, τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἤρξατο βρέχειν τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς ἐξέμασσεν, καὶ κατεφίλει τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλειφεν τῷ μύρῳ.

verses.english: But seeing it, the Pharisee who had invited him said within himself, "This man, if he were a prophet, would know who and what sort of woman it is who is touching him, that she is a sinner."
verses.greek: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Φαρισαῖος ὁ καλέσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Οὗτος εἰ ἦν προφήτης, ἐγίνωσκεν ἂν τίς καὶ ποταπὴ ἡ γυνὴ ἥτις ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.

verses.english: And answering, Jesus said to him, "Simon, I have something to say to you." And he says, "Teacher, say it."
verses.greek: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σίμων, ἔχω σοί τι εἰπεῖν. ὁ δέ· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπέ, φησίν.

verses.english: "There were two debtors to a certain moneylender. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
verses.greek: δύο χρεοφειλέται ἦσαν δανιστῇ τινι· ὁ εἷς ὤφειλεν δηνάρια πεντακόσια, ὁ δὲ ἕτερος πεντήκοντα.

verses.english: When they had nothing to pay back, he freely granted it to both. Which of them, then, will love him more?"
verses.greek: μὴ ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι ἀμφοτέροις ἐχαρίσατο. τίς οὖν αὐτῶν πλεῖον ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν;

verses.english: Simon answered and said, "I suppose the one to whom he freely granted the more." And he said to him, "You have judged rightly."
verses.greek: ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν· Ὑπολαμβάνω ὅτι ᾧ τὸ πλεῖον ἐχαρίσατο. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἔκρινας.

verses.english: And turning to the woman, he said to Simon, "Do you see this woman? I came into your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hairs.
verses.greek: καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα τῷ Σίμωνι ἔφη· Βλέπεις ταύτην τὴν γυναῖκα; εἰσῆλθόν σου εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, ὕδωρ μοι ἐπὶ πόδας οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἔβρεξέν μου τοὺς πόδας καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἐξέμαξεν.

verses.english: You gave me no kiss; but she, from the time I came in, has not stopped kissing my feet.
verses.greek: φίλημά μοι οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ ἀφ’ ἧς εἰσῆλθον οὐ διέλιπεν καταφιλοῦσά μου τοὺς πόδας.

verses.english: You did not anoint my head with olive oil; but she has anointed my feet with perfumed oil.
verses.greek: ἐλαίῳ τὴν κεφαλήν μου οὐκ ἤλειψας· αὕτη δὲ μύρῳ ἤλειψεν τοὺς πόδας μου.

verses.english: For this reason, I tell you, her sins, which are many, have been let go, because she loved much; but the one to whom little is let go loves little."
verses.greek: οὗ χάριν, λέγω σοι, ἀφέωνται αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῆς αἱ πολλαί, ὅτι ἠγάπησεν πολύ· ᾧ δὲ ὀλίγον ἀφίεται, ὀλίγον ἀγαπᾷ.

verses.english: And he said to her, "Your sins have been let go."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ· Ἀφέωνταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.

verses.english: And those reclining at table with him began to say within themselves, "Who is this, who even lets sins go?"
verses.greek: καὶ ἤρξαντο οἱ συνανακείμενοι λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Τίς οὗτός ἐστιν ὃς καὶ ἁμαρτίας ἀφίησιν;

verses.english: And he said to the woman, "Your trust has saved you; journey into peace."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα· Ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.18.1, discusses only the centurion and the saying about faith in Israel; Epiphanius, sch. 7 quotes the saying: »λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, τοσαύτην πίστιν οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ εὗρον«. Its word order ("such trust" first) is printed with NA27's words; Roth rates the words secure. The embassy of the Jewish elders, the friends and the centurion's speech (7:3–8) and the return of the messengers (7:10) are not cited and are printed in grey.

notes.term: "A great prophet has been raised among us" (7:16)
notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.18.3 quotes the acclamation, "Magnus prophetes prodiit in nobis, et Respexit deus populum suum", and argues that the crowd glorified the Creator and Jesus did not correct them. Interpretation: in the attested text the people of Israel name Jesus a prophet and see in the raising a visitation of their God. This is the attested place for the prophet Christology the library builds on; the phrase "a prophet mighty in deed and word" (24:19), used as a title in the library, is itself unattested for this text (working document §5).

Tertullian, Marc. 4.18.4–8 attests John hearing of Jesus' works, the question "Are you the one who is coming, or are we to wait for another?" (quoted twice) and the answer by works. Epiphanius, sch. 8 says the beatitude of 7:23 was "altered" because Marcion's text had it "as if addressed to John"; Holl explains this as Marcion's application of the saying, not a different wording. That is how the Marcionite community read the verse (reception). 7:21 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.18.7–8 and Epiphanius, sch. 9 attest the testimony to John: the question "What did you go out into the wilderness to see?", "a prophet, and more", the quotation of Malachi 3:1, and "the lesser one in the kingdom of God is greater than he". 7:25 is not cited and is printed in grey. Tertullian reports the Marcionite reading that the kingdom of 7:28 belongs to a different god from John's; he answers that both belong to the same God (reception).

7:29–30 (the people and the tax collectors "justified God" by John's baptism; the Pharisees rejected "the counsel of God") and 7:31–35 ("this generation" and the children in the market-place; "wisdom is justified by all her children") are not cited. Tertullian works through 7:18–28 and then 7:36–50 without a gap in his argument, and these verses would have been his best evidence that John's baptism was God's own plan. They are classed "unattested, probably absent" (METHOD §3).

Epiphanius, sch. 10–11 quotes 7:36, 7:38 and 7:44–46; Tertullian, Marc. 4.18.9 attests the woman, her tears, kisses and ointment, the forgiveness and "Your trust has saved you". The Pharisee's thought and the parable of the two debtors (7:39–43) and the guests' question (7:49) are not cited and are printed in grey. Tertullian uses the woman's touch as proof that Jesus had a real body (4.18.9), his own argument against Marcion's Christology.

Interpretation. In the attested scene the woman's faith (7:50) is visible in what she does: the tears, the kisses, the ointment. Her forgiveness is tied to her love ("because she loved much", 7:47). The pairing of faith with acts matches the Epistle of James ("faith was active along with his works", Jas 2:22), which the library takes as the closest written witness to the community behind this text (Carriers of Living Water §3.4).

notes.term: ἐπλήρωσεν… εἰς τὰς ἀκοάς, "completed… in the ears"
notes.explanation: Literally "filled up… into the hearing". ῥήματα are "sayings", things spoken.
A Roman officer commanding about a hundred soldiers.
A person owned by another. "Servant" softens what the word says. The centurion calls the same person παῖς, "boy" (7:7).

notes.term: ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν, "was about to come to his end"
notes.explanation: To reach the end, to die.
Held in honour, precious. It can mean dear to him or of high value.
Literally "older men", the leaders of a community.
Ἰουδαῖος is a person of Judea and its people, defined by land and ancestry as much as by religion. "Jews" is the later, wider category.
δια-σῴζω, to save through, bring through danger.
Two different words. ἄξιος is deserving, of weight; ἱκανός is sufficient, adequate. 7:7 ἠξίωσα, "count worthy", returns to the first.
Here the building where the assembly meets.
"Lord, sir": the capital is only the start of the address. Not the divine name.
Literally "be harassed, be put to bother".

notes.term: εἰπὲ λόγῳ, "say it with a word"
notes.explanation: λόγος, word, as at 4:32.
παῖς means a child, a boy, and is used of a young slave. Here it is the slave of 7:2.
Put in place, ranked: a military word.
The road verb, πορεύομαι.
As at 5:20.

notes.term: ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς, "on the next day"
notes.explanation: Literally "in the next", in sequence. It can also mean "soon afterwards".
The only child born to her.
The narrator calls Jesus "the lord", the ordinary word for a master. Lower case: it is not the divine name, and capitals would make it a doctrine.
From σπλάγχνα, the inner organs, felt as the seat of feeling: "his inward parts were moved".
An open coffin or bier.
The aorist passive of ἐγείρω, "be raised, rise". The people's "has been raised" (7:16) is the same verb.

notes.term: Προφήτης μέγας ἠγέρθη, "a great prophet has been raised"
notes.explanation: The passive leaves unnamed who raised him.
To look upon, look after, go to see. The word for an overseer comes from it.
One who dips, immerses (βαπτίζω). "The Baptist" makes it a title and hides the verb.
Literally "whips", afflictions felt as blows.
χαρίζομαι, to give as a favour (χάρις). The same verb is "freely granted" at 7:42–43.
Literally "look up". It means to regain one's sight.
As at 5:12.

notes.term: πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται, "the destitute are being given the good news"
notes.explanation: A passive: good news is announced to them.
As at 6:20.
σκάνδαλον is the trigger of a trap, a stumbling block. "Take offence" is the meaning in use; the image is of tripping.
ἄγγελος, messenger: here two men. The same word as in 7:27.
To look at as at a spectacle.
Palaces.
A quotation (Mal 3:1; Ex 23:20). ἄγγελος is the word for messenger, here a human one.
To prepare, equip.
A comparative, "the smaller, the lesser". It is often read as a superlative, "the least".
Formal meals were eaten lying on couches.
The text does not say what her sin was. The common idea that she was a prostitute is not in the Greek.

notes.term: ἀλάβαστρον μύρου, "an alabaster flask of perfumed oil"
notes.explanation: μύρον is scented oil, perfume. It is kept apart from ἔλαιον, plain olive oil (7:46).
The imperfect of a strengthened verb: she kept kissing.
The present tense, in the middle of past narration. The Greek has it, and so does the English.
The denarius was a day's wage for a labourer. δανιστής is a moneylender.
χαρίζομαι, to give as a favour. The debt is not "cancelled" in so many words; it is given as a gift.

notes.term: ὅτι ἠγάπησεν πολύ, "because she loved much"
notes.explanation: ὅτι can give the cause ("because she loved") or the evidence ("as is shown by her love"). The sentence that follows ("the one to whom little is let go loves little") points to the second. The Greek allows both.
As at 5:20.

notes.term: συνανακείμενοι, "those reclining at table with him"
notes.explanation: The other guests.
σῴζω, to save, rescue, make well.
εἰς, "into". Behind it lies the Hebrew greeting lekhi le-shalom, "go to peace".

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 5
chapters.preamble: A short section on hearing. Women who had been healed travel with Jesus and the twelve and support them from their own means. The parable of the sower ends in a call to hear, and the sayings on the lamp and the measure of hearing follow. When his mother and brothers are reported to be outside, the text has Jesus ask, "Who is my mother, and who are my brothers, except those who hear my words and do them?" (Tertullian, Marc. 4.19.6, 11). The section closes with the calming of the storm. Two passages of canonical Luke are not printed. The first is the explanation of the sower with its quotation of Isaiah 6, which no witness cites. The second is the narrative sentence in which his mother and brothers arrive: Epiphanius says the text had only the report to Jesus.

verses.english: And it happened afterwards that he was travelling through, city by city and village by village, proclaiming and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God, and the twelve with him,
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ καθεξῆς καὶ αὐτὸς διώδευεν κατὰ πόλιν καὶ κώμην κηρύσσων καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ οἱ δώδεκα σὺν αὐτῷ,

verses.english: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and weaknesses: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven daimons had gone out,
verses.greek: καὶ γυναῖκές τινες αἳ ἦσαν τεθεραπευμέναι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν καὶ ἀσθενειῶν, Μαρία ἡ καλουμένη Μαγδαληνή, ἀφ’ ἧς δαιμόνια ἑπτὰ ἐξεληλύθει,

verses.english: and Joanna, wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, who were serving them out of what belonged to them.
verses.greek: καὶ Ἰωάννα γυνὴ Χουζᾶ ἐπιτρόπου Ἡρῴδου καὶ Σουσάννα καὶ ἕτεραι πολλαί, αἵτινες διηκόνουν αὐτοῖς ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐταῖς.

verses.english: And as a large crowd was coming together, and people from city after city were making their way to him, he spoke through a parable:
verses.greek: Συνιόντος δὲ ὄχλου πολλοῦ καὶ τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ἐπιπορευομένων πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν διὰ παραβολῆς·

verses.english: "The sower went out to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell beside the road, and it was trampled down, and the birds of the sky ate it up.
verses.greek: Ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπεῖραι τὸν σπόρον αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ κατεπατήθη καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατέφαγεν αὐτό.

verses.english: And other seed fell down on the rock, and when it had grown it dried up, because it had no moisture.
verses.greek: καὶ ἕτερον κατέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν, καὶ φυὲν ἐξηράνθη διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ἰκμάδα.

verses.english: And other seed fell in the middle of the thorns, and the thorns, growing up with it, choked it.
verses.greek: καὶ ἕτερον ἔπεσεν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ἀκανθῶν, καὶ συμφυεῖσαι αἱ ἄκανθαι ἀπέπνιξαν αὐτό.

verses.english: And other seed fell into the good earth, and when it had grown it produced fruit a hundredfold." Saying these things, he was calling out, "The one who has ears to hear, let him hear."
verses.greek: καὶ ἕτερον ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν ἀγαθήν, καὶ φυὲν ἐποίησεν καρπὸν ἑκατονταπλασίονα. ταῦτα λέγων ἐφώνει· Ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.

verses.english: "No one, having lit a lamp, covers it with a vessel or puts it underneath a bed; but he puts it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
verses.greek: Οὐδεὶς δὲ λύχνον ἅψας καλύπτει αὐτὸν σκεύει ἢ ὑποκάτω κλίνης τίθησιν, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ λυχνίας τίθησιν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι βλέπωσιν τὸ φῶς.

verses.english: For nothing is hidden that will not become visible, nor secret that will not be known and come into the open.
verses.greek: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ φανερὸν γενήσεται, οὐδὲ ἀπόκρυφον ὃ οὐ μὴ γνωσθῇ καὶ εἰς φανερὸν ἔλθῃ.

verses.english: Look, then, how you hear; for whoever has, it will be given to him; and whoever does not have, even what he seems to have will be taken from him."
verses.greek: βλέπετε οὖν πῶς ἀκούετε· ὃς ἂν γὰρ ἔχῃ, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ, καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ ἔχῃ, καὶ ὃ δοκεῖ ἔχειν ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And it was reported to him, "Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you."
verses.greek: ἀπηγγέλη δὲ αὐτῷ· Ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἑστήκασιν ἔξω ἰδεῖν θέλοντές σε.

verses.english: But he answered and said to them, "Who is my mother, and who are my brothers, except those who hear my words and do them?"
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίς μοι μήτηρ καὶ τίνες μοι ἀδελφοί, εἰ μὴ οἱ τοὺς λόγους μου ἀκούοντες καὶ ποιοῦντες αὐτούς;

verses.english: And it happened on one of the days that he got into a boat, and his learners, and he said to them, "Let us go across to the other side of the lake"; and they put out.
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἐνέβη εἰς πλοῖον καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς λίμνης, καὶ ἀνήχθησαν.

verses.english: And as they sailed, he fell asleep. And a squall of wind came down onto the lake, and they were being filled, and were in danger.
verses.greek: πλεόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀφύπνωσεν. καὶ κατέβη λαῖλαψ ἀνέμου εἰς τὴν λίμνην, καὶ συνεπληροῦντο καὶ ἐκινδύνευον.

verses.english: And coming up, they roused him, saying, "Overseer, overseer, we are perishing!" And being roused, he rebuked the wind and the surge of the water; and they stopped, and there was a calm.
verses.greek: προσελθόντες δὲ διήγειραν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ἐπιστάτα ἐπιστάτα, ἀπολλύμεθα· ὁ δὲ διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ τῷ κλύδωνι τοῦ ὕδατος, καὶ ἐπαύσαντο, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη.

verses.english: And he said to them, "Where is your trust?" And being afraid, they marvelled, saying to one another, "Who then is this, that he gives orders even to the winds and the water, and they obey him?"
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ποῦ ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν; φοβηθέντες δὲ ἐθαύμασαν, λέγοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ τοῖς ἀνέμοις ἐπιτάσσει καὶ τῷ ὕδατι, καὶ ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ;

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.19.1: "that rich women adhered to Christ and ministered to him from their means, among them the wife of the king's procurator". 8:2–3 are attested in substance; the names (Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Chuza, Susanna) are not cited and are printed in the NA27 wording within the attested verses. 8:1 is not cited and is printed in grey. Tertullian reads "ministered to him" (αὐτῷ); NA27 has "to them" (αὐτοῖς).

notes.term: The sower and the call to hear (8:4–8, 8:16–18)
notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.19.2–5 attests the parable, the call "whoever has ears, let him hear", the lamp not hidden, the hidden made manifest and "take care how you hear; to whoever has more will be given". 8:5–7 are not cited and are printed in grey.

The disciples' question, Jesus' quotation of Isaiah 6:9 ("so that seeing they may not see") and the allegorical explanation of the sower are not cited by any witness. At 8:8 Tertullian brings in Isaiah 6:9 himself ("Aure audietis et non audietis", Marc. 4.19.2) to show that the Creator foretold this way of speaking. Had the text contained Jesus quoting the same prophet (8:10), it would have been his best evidence. 8:9–10 are classed "unattested, probably absent". 8:11–15 belong to the same NA27 paragraph, which has no attested verse, and are not printed.

Epiphanius, sch. 12: the text "did not have 'his mother and his brothers' [8:19], but only 'your mother and your brothers'" [8:20]; so the arrival of the family is not narrated, only reported to Jesus. Tertullian, Marc. 4.19.6–13, quotes the reply twice as a question, "Quae mihi mater et qui mihi fratres?", and completes it: "Nisi qui audiunt verba mea et faciunt ea". That differs from canonical Luke in form (a question, as in Mark 3:33 and Matthew 12:48) and in content ("my words", not "the word of God"). The Greek printed is Roth's reconstruction from Tertullian's Latin (a retroversion). Tertullian records the Marcionite argument that the saying denies Jesus' birth; he answers that it transfers the names of kin to those who hear and do (4.19.11). The Marcionite argument is reception.

Interpretation. The attested form of 8:21 makes kinship with Jesus a matter of hearing his words and doing them, the same standard as 6:46 ("why do you call me Lord, Lord, and do not do what I say?"). The demand is the one the library finds in the Epistle of James ("be doers of the word", Jas 1:22). In this text it is attested twice, in two independent sayings.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.20.1–3; Epiphanius, sch. 13: "as they sailed he fell asleep; and he rose and rebuked the wind and the sea". Both witnesses speak of "the sea" where NA27 has "the surge of the water" (8:24) and "the water" (8:25), as in Matthew and Mark. Tertullian's "mare" comes in words he is quoting from Nahum 1:4, and Epiphanius may be giving the familiar Matthean phrase; Roth rates the reading possible. NA27 is printed and the evidence noted. "Master" renders ἐπιστάτα.
In what follows, next in order.
To go through, travel about. The imperfect: he went on doing it.

notes.term: κηρύσσων καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενος, "proclaiming and announcing the good news"
notes.explanation: Two verbs: to proclaim aloud as a herald, and to announce good news.
θεραπεύω, heal, as at 4:40.
A woman of Magdala, a town on the lake.
A manager of property, a household administrator.
διακονέω, to serve, wait on, provide for. The imperfect: they went on doing it. The word for "deacon" comes from it.

notes.term: ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐταῖς, "out of what belonged to them"
notes.explanation: Their own possessions, their means.
πορεύομαι with ἐπι-, "journeying to".
διά, "through, by means of".
With the article: "the sower", one who sows.
ὁδός, road, way. The same word is "the way" elsewhere (7:27).

notes.term: τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, "the birds of the sky"
notes.explanation: οὐρανός is both "sky" and "heaven".
From ξηρός, "dry", the word of the dry hand (6:6).
Damp, sap.
The imperfect: he kept crying it out.
Any container or utensil.
The stand on which a lamp is set.
Manifest, out in the open. The same word ends the verse: "come into the open".

notes.term: Βλέπετε… πῶς ἀκούετε, "look, then, how you hear"
notes.explanation: βλέπω, "see, look". The Greek says "see how you hear".
δοκέω can mean both "seem" and "think": "what he seems to have" or "what he thinks he has".
ἀδελφός, brother. The Greek does not say cousins or relatives.
The reading of this text. Canonical Luke has "the word of God".
Set sail, put out to sea.
Dropped off to sleep.
A sudden violent storm.
The Greek says "they" were being filled: the boat, and they in it.
As at 5:5: not κύριε ("lord") or διδάσκαλε ("teacher").
ἐγείρω with δια-, "wake fully". It is the verb of being raised (7:14, 7:22).
ἀπόλλυμι, as at 4:34.
The rough water, the swell.
As at 4:36, of the unclean spirits.
Literally "listen under", hear and obey.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 6
chapters.preamble: Three works of power and the mission of the twelve. On the far shore Jesus frees a man held by a "legion" of daimons, who beg not to be sent into the abyss. Back among the crowds, a woman who has bled for twelve years touches his cloak and is healed, and the text has him ask, "Who touched me?" Tertullian quotes the question and uses it against Marcion's teaching that Jesus' body was not real (Marc. 4.20.7–14). The twelve are sent to proclaim the kingdom without provisions. Herod hears that Jesus is taken for John, Elijah or one of the ancient prophets. In a deserted place five thousand are fed from five loaves and two fish. The witnesses cite the woman's healing but not the raising of Jairus' daughter that frames it; the frame is printed in grey, because Epiphanius' "as they were going" presupposes the journey to Jairus' house.

verses.english: And they sailed down to the country of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.
verses.greek: Καὶ κατέπλευσαν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἀντιπέρα τῆς Γαλιλαίας.

verses.english: And as he went out onto the land, a certain man from the city met him, having daimons; and for a long time he had not put on a garment, and he did not stay in a house but among the tombs.
verses.greek: ἐξελθόντι δὲ αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ὑπήντησεν ἀνήρ τις ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ἔχων δαιμόνια· καὶ χρόνῳ ἱκανῷ οὐκ ἐνεδύσατο ἱμάτιον, καὶ ἐν οἰκίᾳ οὐκ ἔμενεν ἀλλ’ ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν.

verses.english: And seeing Jesus, crying out, he fell down before him and said with a loud voice, "What is there between me and you, Jesus, son of the Highest God? I beg you, do not torture me."
verses.greek: ἰδὼν δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀνακράξας προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ εἶπεν· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου; δέομαί σου, μή με βασανίσῃς·

verses.english: For he was ordering the unclean spirit to go out from the person. For many times it had seized him, and he was bound with chains and fetters and kept under guard, and tearing the bonds apart he was driven by the daimon into the deserts.
verses.greek: παρήγγελλεν γὰρ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. πολλοῖς γὰρ χρόνοις συνηρπάκει αὐτόν, καὶ ἐδεσμεύετο ἁλύσεσιν καὶ πέδαις φυλασσόμενος, καὶ διαρρήσσων τὰ δεσμὰ ἠλαύνετο ὑπὸ τοῦ δαιμονίου εἰς τὰς ἐρήμους.

verses.english: And Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" And he said, "Legion," because many daimons had gone into him.
verses.greek: ἐπηρώτησεν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί σοι ὄνομά ἐστιν; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Λεγιών, ὅτι εἰσῆλθεν δαιμόνια πολλὰ εἰς αὐτόν.

verses.english: And they were urging him not to order them to go away into the abyss.
verses.greek: καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μὴ ἐπιτάξῃ αὐτοῖς εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον ἀπελθεῖν.

verses.english: Now there was a sizeable herd of pigs there, feeding on the mountain; and they urged him to allow them to go into those; and he allowed them.
verses.greek: Ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἀγέλη χοίρων ἱκανῶν βοσκομένη ἐν τῷ ὄρει· καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιτρέψῃ αὐτοῖς εἰς ἐκείνους εἰσελθεῖν· καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: And the daimons, going out from the person, went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the cliff into the lake and was choked.
verses.greek: ἐξελθόντα δὲ τὰ δαιμόνια ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν λίμνην καὶ ἀπεπνίγη.

verses.english: And those feeding them, seeing what had happened, fled and reported it in the city and in the fields.
verses.greek: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ βόσκοντες τὸ γεγονὸς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς.

verses.english: And they went out to see what had happened, and came to Jesus, and found the person from whom the daimons had gone out sitting, clothed and of sound mind, at the feet of Jesus; and they were afraid.
verses.greek: ἐξῆλθον δὲ ἰδεῖν τὸ γεγονὸς καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ εὗρον καθήμενον τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀφ’ οὗ τὰ δαιμόνια ἐξῆλθεν ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.

verses.english: And those who had seen it reported to them how the one who had been daimonised was saved.
verses.greek: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐσώθη ὁ δαιμονισθείς.

verses.english: And the whole multitude of the surrounding region of the Gerasenes asked him to go away from them, because they were held by a great fear; and he got into a boat and returned.
verses.greek: καὶ ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῆς περιχώρου τῶν Γερασηνῶν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπ’ αὐτῶν, ὅτι φόβῳ μεγάλῳ συνείχοντο· αὐτὸς δὲ ἐμβὰς εἰς πλοῖον ὑπέστρεψεν.

verses.english: And the man from whom the daimons had gone out was begging him to be with him; but he released him, saying,
verses.greek: ἐδεῖτο δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀνὴρ ἀφ’ οὗ ἐξεληλύθει τὰ δαιμόνια εἶναι σὺν αὐτῷ· ἀπέλυσεν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγων·

verses.english: "Return to your house, and tell in full what God has done for you." And he went away through the whole city, proclaiming what Jesus had done for him.
verses.greek: Ὑπόστρεφε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου, καὶ διηγοῦ ὅσα σοι ἐποίησεν ὁ θεός. καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καθ’ ὅλην τὴν πόλιν κηρύσσων ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς.

verses.english: And as Jesus returned, the crowd received him, for they were all waiting for him.
verses.greek: Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑποστρέφειν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπεδέξατο αὐτὸν ὁ ὄχλος, ἦσαν γὰρ πάντες προσδοκῶντες αὐτόν.

verses.english: And look, a man came whose name was Jairus, and he was a ruler of the assembly; and falling at the feet of Jesus he was urging him to come into his house,
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἦλθεν ἀνὴρ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰάϊρος, καὶ οὗτος ἄρχων τῆς συναγωγῆς ὑπῆρχεν, καὶ πεσὼν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ,

verses.english: because he had an only-born daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. And as he went, the crowds were choking him.
verses.greek: ὅτι θυγάτηρ μονογενὴς ἦν αὐτῷ ὡς ἐτῶν δώδεκα καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέθνῃσκεν. Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι συνέπνιγον αὐτόν.

verses.english: And a woman who had been in a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent her whole living on physicians and could not be healed by anyone,
verses.greek: καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος ἀπὸ ἐτῶν δώδεκα, ἥτις ἰατροῖς προσαναλώσασα ὅλον τὸν βίον οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἀπ’ οὐδενὸς θεραπευθῆναι,

verses.english: coming up behind, touched the fringe of his garment, and at once the flow of her blood stood still.
verses.greek: προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ, καὶ παραχρῆμα ἔστη ἡ ῥύσις τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς.

verses.english: And Jesus said, "Who touched me?" And when all were denying it, Peter said, "Overseer, the crowds are hemming you in and pressing against you."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τίς μου ἥψατο; ἀρνουμένων δὲ πάντων εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος· Ἐπιστάτα, οἱ ὄχλοι συνέχουσίν σε καὶ ἀποθλίβουσιν.

verses.english: But Jesus said, "Someone touched me, for I knew power had gone out from me."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἥψατό μού τις, ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔγνων δύναμιν ἐξεληλυθυῖαν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ.

verses.english: And the woman, seeing that she had not escaped notice, came trembling, and falling down before him, she reported before all the people for what reason she had touched him and how she had been cured at once.
verses.greek: ἰδοῦσα δὲ ἡ γυνὴ ὅτι οὐκ ἔλαθεν τρέμουσα ἦλθεν καὶ προσπεσοῦσα αὐτῷ δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν ἥψατο αὐτοῦ ἀπήγγειλεν ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ὡς ἰάθη παραχρῆμα.

verses.english: And he said to her, "Daughter, your trust has saved you; journey into peace."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Θυγάτηρ, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην.

verses.english: While he was still speaking, someone comes from the ruler of the assembly, saying, "Your daughter has died; trouble the teacher no longer."
verses.greek: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχεταί τις παρὰ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγων ὅτι Τέθνηκεν ἡ θυγάτηρ σου, μηκέτι σκύλλε τὸν διδάσκαλον.

verses.english: But Jesus, hearing it, answered him, "Do not be afraid; only trust, and she will be saved."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀκούσας ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, μόνον πίστευσον, καὶ σωθήσεται.

verses.english: And coming into the house, he did not let anyone go in with him except Peter and John and Jacob, and the father of the child and the mother.
verses.greek: ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν οὐκ ἀφῆκεν εἰσελθεῖν τινα σὺν αὐτῷ εἰ μὴ Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν πατέρα τῆς παιδὸς καὶ τὴν μητέρα.

verses.english: And all were weeping and beating their breasts for her. But he said, "Do not weep, for she did not die, but is sleeping."
verses.greek: ἔκλαιον δὲ πάντες καὶ ἐκόπτοντο αὐτήν. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Μὴ κλαίετε, οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει.

verses.english: And they were laughing him down, knowing that she had died.
verses.greek: καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ, εἰδότες ὅτι ἀπέθανεν.

verses.english: But he, taking hold of her hand, called out, saying, "Child, get up!"
verses.greek: αὐτὸς δὲ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς ἐφώνησεν λέγων· Ἡ παῖς, ἔγειρε.

verses.english: And her spirit returned, and she stood up at once, and he directed that something be given to her to eat.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπέστρεψεν τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτῆς, καὶ ἀνέστη παραχρῆμα, καὶ διέταξεν αὐτῇ δοθῆναι φαγεῖν.

verses.english: And her parents were beside themselves; but he ordered them to tell no one what had happened.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτῆς· ὁ δὲ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν τὸ γεγονός.

verses.english: And calling the twelve together, he gave them power and authority over all the daimons, and to heal diseases,
verses.greek: Συγκαλεσάμενος δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δύναμιν καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ νόσους θεραπεύειν,

verses.english: and he sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to cure,
verses.greek: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἰᾶσθαι,

verses.english: and he said to them, "Take nothing for the road, neither staff nor bag nor bread nor silver, nor are you to have two tunics each.
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μηδὲν αἴρετε εἰς τὴν ὁδόν, μήτε ῥάβδον μήτε πήραν μήτε ἄρτον μήτε ἀργύριον, μήτε ἀνὰ δύο χιτῶνας ἔχειν.

verses.english: And whatever house you go into, stay there, and go out from there.
verses.greek: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν οἰκίαν εἰσέλθητε, ἐκεῖ μένετε καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἐξέρχεσθε.

verses.english: And as many as do not receive you, when you go out from that city, shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony against them."
verses.greek: καὶ ὅσοι ἂν μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐξερχόμενοι ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης τὸν κονιορτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν ἀποτινάσσετε εἰς μαρτύριον ἐπ’ αὐτούς.

verses.english: And going out, they were going through the villages, announcing the good news and healing everywhere.
verses.greek: ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ διήρχοντο κατὰ τὰς κώμας εὐαγγελιζόμενοι καὶ θεραπεύοντες πανταχοῦ.

verses.english: And Herod the tetrarch heard of all the things that were happening, and he was at a loss, because it was said by some that John had been raised from the dead,
verses.greek: Ἤκουσεν δὲ Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὰ γινόμενα πάντα, καὶ διηπόρει διὰ τὸ λέγεσθαι ὑπό τινων ὅτι Ἰωάννης ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν,

verses.english: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the prophets of old had stood up.
verses.greek: ὑπό τινων δὲ ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐφάνη, ἄλλων δὲ ὅτι προφήτης τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη.

verses.english: And Herod said, "John I beheaded; but who is this about whom I hear such things?" And he was seeking to see him.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης· Ἰωάννην ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα· τίς δέ ἐστιν οὗτος περὶ οὗ ἀκούω τοιαῦτα; καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν αὐτόν.

verses.english: And returning, the emissaries described to him all that they had done. And taking them along, he withdrew privately to a city called Bethsaida.
verses.greek: Καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες οἱ ἀπόστολοι διηγήσαντο αὐτῷ ὅσα ἐποίησαν. καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ὑπεχώρησεν κατ’ ἰδίαν εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Βηθσαϊδά.

verses.english: But the crowds, knowing it, followed him; and receiving them, he was speaking to them about the kingdom of God, and those who had need of healing he was curing.
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι γνόντες ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ. καὶ ἀποδεξάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τοὺς χρείαν ἔχοντας θεραπείας ἰᾶτο.

verses.english: And the day began to decline; and coming up, the twelve said to him, "Release the crowd, so that going into the villages and fields around they may lodge and find provisions, because here we are in a desert place."
verses.greek: Ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤρξατο κλίνειν· προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δώδεκα εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἀπόλυσον τὸν ὄχλον, ἵνα πορευθέντες εἰς τὰς κύκλῳ κώμας καὶ ἀγροὺς καταλύσωσιν καὶ εὕρωσιν ἐπισιτισμόν, ὅτι ὧδε ἐν ἐρήμῳ τόπῳ ἐσμέν.

verses.english: But he said to them, "You give them something to eat." But they said, "We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we are to go and buy food for all this people."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν. οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οὐκ εἰσὶν ἡμῖν πλεῖον ἢ ἄρτοι πέντε καὶ ἰχθύες δύο, εἰ μήτι πορευθέντες ἡμεῖς ἀγοράσωμεν εἰς πάντα τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον βρώματα.

verses.english: For there were about five thousand men. And he said to his learners, "Make them recline in table groups of about fifty each."
verses.greek: ἦσαν γὰρ ὡσεὶ ἄνδρες πεντακισχίλιοι. εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Κατακλίνατε αὐτοὺς κλισίας ὡσεὶ ἀνὰ πεντήκοντα.

verses.english: And they did so, and made them all recline.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐποίησαν οὕτως καὶ κατέκλιναν ἅπαντας.

verses.english: And taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up to the sky, he blessed over them and broke them in pieces, and he was giving them to the learners to set before the crowd.
verses.greek: λαβὼν δὲ τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς καὶ κατέκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς παραθεῖναι τῷ ὄχλῳ.

verses.english: And they ate and were fed, all of them; and what was left over to them was taken up: twelve baskets of broken pieces.
verses.greek: καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν πάντες, καὶ ἤρθη τὸ περισσεῦσαν αὐτοῖς κλασμάτων κόφινοι δώδεκα.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.20.4–7: "a multitude of daimons in one man", the name "legion", the cry that Jesus is "son of God", and the plea not to be sent into the abyss, which he says Jesus granted ("Denique impetraverunt"). The binding with chains (8:29), the drowning of the herd and the reaction of the townspeople (8:33–39) are not cited and are printed in grey.

Reception. Tertullian argues that the daimons knew whose son Jesus was because they feared the Creator's abyss, and that Jesus' granting their request proves he belonged to that God (Marc. 4.20.5–7). The text itself says only that they begged not to be sent into the abyss (ἄβυσσος, the deep in the Greek Bible).

notes.term: The woman who touched his cloak (8:42b–48)
notes.explanation: Epiphanius, sch. 14: »ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτούς, συνέπνιγον αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι. καὶ γυνὴ ἁψαμένη αὐτοῦ ἰάθη τοῦ αἵματος· καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος· τίς μου ἥψατο;« and »ἥψατό μού τις. καὶ γὰρ ἔγνων δύναμιν ἐξελθοῦσαν ἀπ' ἐμοῦ«. Tertullian, Marc. 4.20.7–13: "Quis me, inquit, tetigit?… Tetigit me aliquis… Sensi enim virtutem ex me profectam… Fides tua te salvam fecit." Both witnesses give the question as "Who touched me?" (τίς μου ἥψατο;) where NA27 has "Who is the one who touched me?"; the attested form is printed. 8:47 is not cited and is printed in grey.

notes.term: The woman and the law of purity
notes.explanation: Reception and interpretation. The Marcionites read the healing as Jesus setting aside the law that made a woman with a flow of blood unclean (Lev 15:25–27). Tertullian answers that the law concerns the regular flow, not a disease, and that the woman did not break it (Marc. 4.20.9–12). The text itself says nothing about the law: it reports the touch, the power going out, and the woman's faith. The legal questions belong to the readers.

No witness cites the request of Jairus or the raising of his daughter. Epiphanius' quotation begins "as they were going", which presupposes the journey to Jairus' house, and NA27 prints 8:40–56 as one paragraph. The frame is therefore printed in grey, as part of an attested passage. Tertullian had already used the raising of the widow's son (7:11–17) to argue that raising the dead was the Creator's sign (4.18.2), so a second raising would add nothing to his case. That is why his silence here is not counted as evidence of absence.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.21.1: the disciples are sent to preach the kingdom of God, are forbidden to take food or clothing for the road, and are told to shake the dust from their feet "as a testimony". 9:1–2 and 9:6 are also read in the Dialogue of Adamantius (82,2–7) by the orthodox speaker, as an argument the Marcionite is expected to accept; Roth counts this as attestation. 9:4 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.21.2: "some said John, some Elijah, some one of the ancient prophets". He argues that whichever of these Jesus was, he was not raised to preach another god. 9:9 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.21.2–5 compares the feeding with the manna and with Elisha's loaves (2 Kgs 4:42–44); Epiphanius, sch. 15 quotes 9:16 as »ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν ἐπ' αὐτούς« ("he blessed over them"), printed here (Roth: very likely). 9:10–11 and 9:15 are not cited and are printed in grey. The previous text treated the distribution clause of 9:16 as an excision; no witness supports that.

Both this text and canonical Luke pass from the feeding (Mark 6:30–44) to Peter's confession (Mark 8:27–30) and lack the intervening block of Mark (6:45–8:26). The previous note presented this "Great Omission" as evidence that Proto-Luke is independent of Mark; since canonical Luke lacks the same block, it tells nothing about the relation between the two texts (audit context §5).
ἀνήρ, a male. In 8:29, 8:33 and 8:35 the text calls him ἄνθρωπος, "the person".
μνῆμα, a memorial, a tomb.

notes.term: Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, "what is there between me and you"
notes.explanation: The idiom of 4:34, here in the singular.

notes.term: υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου, "son of the Highest God"
notes.explanation: Lower case for "son", as at 4:41. "The Highest" as at 6:35.
βασανίζω, to examine by torture, torment.
The imperfect: he had been ordering it, or he was in the course of ordering it.
To seize and carry off.
The Latin word for a Roman army unit of several thousand soldiers, taken into Greek.
"The bottomless", the deep below the earth.
Unclean animals under the law.
ὄρος, as at 4:29 and 6:12.
To give leave, permit.
The verb of the thorns that choked the seed (8:7). It means drowned here.
Answers 8:27, "had not put on a garment".
Sensible, in control of himself.

notes.term: ὁ δαιμονισθείς, "the one who had been daimonised"
notes.explanation: One acted on by daimons. "Possessed" is an interpretation of what that means.
σῴζω: here, made well.
Gripped, held fast.
ἀπολύω, to release, send away, dismiss.
To tell through, recount in detail.

notes.term: "what God has done… what Jesus had done"
notes.explanation: The Greek has God in the command and Jesus in what the man proclaims. The English keeps both.
To welcome, receive gladly.

notes.term: ἄρχων τῆς συναγωγῆς, "a ruler of the assembly"
notes.explanation: The leader of the local assembly. In 8:49 one word, ἀρχισυνάγωγος, says the same.
As at 7:12.
The verb of 8:7, choking: the crowd crushing him.

notes.term: ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος, "in a flow of blood"
notes.explanation: A continuous flow of blood, which made her unclean under the law.
βίος is livelihood, the means one lives on.
The edge or tassel of a garment, as the law required (Num 15:38).
The ordinary verb "stood", used of the flow stopping.
As at 5:5.
As at 6:19.
λανθάνω, to be hidden, unnoticed.
ἰάομαι, cure.
The address is "daughter", as the Greek has it.
The present tense in the middle of past narration, kept.
πιστεύω, here without an object: trust.
παῖς, here feminine: the girl.
κόπτομαι, to strike oneself in mourning, lament.
To laugh at, deride.
ἐγείρω, as at 7:14.

notes.term: ἐπέστρεψεν τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτῆς, "her spirit returned"
notes.explanation: πνεῦμα, spirit, also breath.
ἀνίστημι.
From the same root as ἔκστασις (5:26), standing out of oneself.
δύναμις, the ability to act; ἐξουσία, the right to act.
Both verbs, kept apart.
Silver, money.
The tunic worn next to the skin, as at 6:29.

notes.term: εἰς μαρτύριον ἐπ' αὐτούς, "as a testimony against them"
notes.explanation: ἐπί with the accusative, "upon, against".
To be perplexed, not to know which way to go.

notes.term: ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν, "had been raised from the dead"
notes.explanation: ἐγείρω, passive.
ἀνίστημι. A different verb from "raised" (9:7) in the same sentence. Both are kept.
As at 6:13.
To tell in full, as at 8:39.
As at 8:40.
ἀπολύω, to send away, dismiss, release.
To unharness and put up for the night.
ἀνήρ: males.

notes.term: Κατακλίνατε… κλισίας, "make them recline in table groups"
notes.explanation: κλισία, a company reclining together at a meal.

notes.term: ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, "looking up to the sky"
notes.explanation: οὐρανός, "sky" and "heaven".

notes.explanation: The reading of this text, "upon them". Canonical Luke has "blessed them".
The imperfect: he kept giving.

Large wicker baskets.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 7
chapters.preamble: Peter's confession and what follows from it. Asked who he is, Peter answers "the Anointed One of God", and Jesus at once speaks of suffering, rejection, death and being raised "after three days" (the form of Mark and of both witnesses). On the mountain he is seen with Moses and Elijah, and the voice from the cloud says "This is my son, the beloved; hear him." Tertullian dwells on this scene to argue that Jesus stands with the law and the prophets, not against them (Marc. 4.22). Then come the epileptic boy ("O untrusting generation", without "and perverse"), the dispute about greatness, the Samaritan village where Jesus rebukes the disciples' wish to call down fire, and three would-be followers. Unattested verses inside these passages are printed in grey. The strange exorcist (9:49–50), which no witness cites, is not printed.

verses.english: And it happened, while he was praying alone, that the learners were with him, and he asked them, saying, "Who do the crowds say that I am?"
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν προσευχόμενον κατὰ μόνας συνῆσαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί, καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς λέγων· Τίνα με λέγουσιν οἱ ὄχλοι εἶναι;

verses.english: And they answered and said, "John the baptiser; but others, Elijah; and others, that one of the prophets of old has stood up."
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν, ἄλλοι δὲ ὅτι προφήτης τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη.

verses.english: And he said to them, "But you, who do you say that I am?" And Peter answered and said, "The Anointed One of God."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι; Πέτρος δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Τὸν χριστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: But he, rebuking them, ordered them to tell this to no one,
verses.greek: Ὁ δὲ ἐπιτιμήσας αὐτοῖς παρήγγειλεν μηδενὶ λέγειν τοῦτο,

verses.english: saying, "The son of the human must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and high priests and scribes, and be killed, and after three days be raised."
verses.greek: εἰπὼν ὅτι Δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐγερθῆναι.

verses.english: And he was saying to all, "If anyone wants to come after me, let him disown himself, and take up his cross day by day, and follow me.
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς πάντας· Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἔρχεσθαι, ἀρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καθ’ ἡμέραν, καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.

verses.english: For whoever wants to save his soul will destroy it; but whoever destroys his soul for my sake, he will save it.
verses.greek: ὃς γὰρ ἂν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι, ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ, οὗτος σώσει αὐτήν.

verses.english: For what does a person gain, having won the whole world, but having destroyed himself or suffered the loss of himself?
verses.greek: τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖται ἄνθρωπος κερδήσας τὸν κόσμον ὅλον ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἀπολέσας ἢ ζημιωθείς;

verses.english: For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, of him the son of the human will be ashamed, when he comes in his glory and that of the Father and of the holy messengers.
verses.greek: ὃς γὰρ ἂν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους, τοῦτον ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται, ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων.

verses.english: But I tell you truly, there are some of those standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God."
verses.greek: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ἀληθῶς, εἰσίν τινες τῶν αὐτοῦ ἑστηκότων οἳ οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: And it happened about eight days after these words that, taking along Peter and John and Jacob, he went up into the mountain to pray.
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὡσεὶ ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ καὶ παραλαβὼν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι.

verses.english: And it happened, as he was praying, that the look of his face became other, and his clothing white, flashing like lightning.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ προσεύχεσθαι αὐτὸν τὸ εἶδος τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἕτερον καὶ ὁ ἱματισμὸς αὐτοῦ λευκὸς ἐξαστράπτων.

verses.english: And look, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο συνελάλουν αὐτῷ, οἵτινες ἦσαν Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας,

verses.english: who were seen in glory.
verses.greek: οἳ ὀφθέντες ἐν δόξῃ.

verses.english: But Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep; but becoming fully awake, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ ἦσαν βεβαρημένοι ὕπνῳ· διαγρηγορήσαντες δὲ εἶδον τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς δύο ἄνδρας τοὺς συνεστῶτας αὐτῷ.

verses.english: And it happened, as they were parting from him, that Peter said to Jesus, "Overseer, it is fine for us to be here; and let us make three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah," not knowing what he was saying.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ διαχωρίζεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Ἐπιστάτα, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι, καὶ ποιήσωμεν σκηνὰς τρεῖς, μίαν σοὶ καὶ μίαν Μωϋσεῖ καὶ μίαν Ἠλίᾳ, μὴ εἰδὼς ὃ λέγει.

verses.english: And as he was saying these things, a cloud came and was overshadowing them; and they were afraid as they went into the cloud.
verses.greek: ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ἐγένετο νεφέλη καὶ ἐπεσκίαζεν αὐτούς· ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ ἐν τῷ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν νεφέλην.

verses.english: And a voice came out of the cloud, saying, "This is my son, the beloved; hear him."
verses.greek: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε.

verses.english: And when the voice had come, Jesus was found alone. And they were silent and reported to no one in those days anything of what they had seen.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐν τῷ γενέσθαι τὴν φωνὴν εὑρέθη Ἰησοῦς μόνος. καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐσίγησαν καὶ οὐδενὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις οὐδὲν ὧν ἑώρακαν.

verses.english: And it happened on the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, that a large crowd met him.
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ τῇ ἑξῆς ἡμέρᾳ κατελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄρους συνήντησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς.

verses.english: And look, a man from the crowd shouted, saying, "Teacher, I beg you to look upon my son, because he is my only-born,
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ἐβόησεν λέγων· Διδάσκαλε, δέομαί σου ἐπιβλέψαι ἐπὶ τὸν υἱόν μου, ὅτι μονογενής μοί ἐστιν,

verses.english: and look, a spirit takes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it convulses him with foam, and it hardly goes away from him, crushing him.
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ πνεῦμα λαμβάνει αὐτόν, καὶ ἐξαίφνης κράζει, καὶ σπαράσσει αὐτὸν μετὰ ἀφροῦ καὶ μόγις ἀποχωρεῖ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ συντρῖβον αὐτόν·

verses.english: And I begged your learners to throw it out, and they were not able."
verses.greek: καὶ ἐδεήθην τῶν μαθητῶν σου ἵνα ἐκβάλωσιν αὐτό, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν.

verses.english: And Jesus answered and said, "O untrusting generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here."
verses.greek: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος, ἕως πότε ἔσομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν; προσάγαγε ὧδε τὸν υἱόν σου.

verses.english: And while he was still coming up, the daimon tore at him and convulsed him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and cured the boy, and gave him back to his father.
verses.greek: ἔτι δὲ προσερχομένου αὐτοῦ ἔρρηξεν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον καὶ συνεσπάραξεν· ἐπετίμησεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ, καὶ ἰάσατο τὸν παῖδα καὶ ἀπέδωκεν αὐτὸν τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And all were astounded at the majesty of God. And while all were marvelling at all the things he was doing, he said to his learners,
verses.greek: ἐξεπλήσσοντο δὲ πάντες ἐπὶ τῇ μεγαλειότητι τοῦ θεοῦ. Πάντων δὲ θαυμαζόντων ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐποίει εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ·

verses.english: "You, put these words into your ears: for the son of the human is about to be handed over into the hands of humans."
verses.greek: Θέσθε ὑμεῖς εἰς τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ὁ γὰρ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων.

verses.english: But they did not understand this saying, and it was veiled from them so that they should not perceive it; and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο, καὶ ἦν παρακεκαλυμμένον ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἵνα μὴ αἴσθωνται αὐτό, καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο ἐρωτῆσαι αὐτὸν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος τούτου.

verses.english: And a reasoning came in among them, which of them might be greater.
verses.greek: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ διαλογισμὸς ἐν αὐτοῖς, τὸ τίς ἂν εἴη μείζων αὐτῶν.

verses.english: But Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their heart, took hold of a little child and stood it beside himself,
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἰδὼς τὸν διαλογισμὸν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενος παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ παρ’ ἑαυτῷ,

verses.english: and said to them, "Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me. For the one who is lesser among you all, this one is great."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὃς ἐὰν δέξηται τοῦτο τὸ παιδίον ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐμὲ δέξηται δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με· ὁ γὰρ μικρότερος ἐν πᾶσιν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχων οὗτός ἐστιν μέγας.

verses.english: And it happened, as the days of his taking up were being filled, that he set his face firmly to journey to Jerusalem,
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ἀναλήμψεως αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς τὸ πρόσωπον ἐστήρισεν τοῦ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ,

verses.english: and he sent messengers before his face. And journeying, they went into a village of Samaritans, to make ready for him;
verses.greek: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν ἀγγέλους πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ. καὶ πορευθέντες εἰσῆλθον εἰς κώμην Σαμαριτῶν, ὡς ἑτοιμάσαι αὐτῷ·

verses.english: and they did not receive him, because his face was journeying to Jerusalem.
verses.greek: καὶ οὐκ ἐδέξαντο αὐτόν, ὅτι τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἦν πορευόμενον εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.

verses.english: And seeing it, the learners Jacob and John said, "Lord, do you want us to tell fire to come down from the sky and consume them?"
verses.greek: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης εἶπαν· Κύριε, θέλεις εἴπωμεν πῦρ καταβῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀναλῶσαι αὐτούς;

verses.english: But turning, he rebuked them.
verses.greek: στραφεὶς δὲ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: And they journeyed to another village.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς ἑτέραν κώμην.

verses.english: And as they were journeying on the road, someone said to him, "I will follow you wherever you go away to."
verses.greek: Καὶ πορευομένων αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπέν τις πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀκολουθήσω σοι ὅπου ἐὰν ἀπέρχῃ.

verses.english: And Jesus said to him, "The foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have places to settle, but the son of the human has nowhere to lay his head."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Αἱ ἀλώπεκες φωλεοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνώσεις, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνῃ.

verses.english: And he said to another, "Follow me." But he said, "Lord, allow me first to go away and bury my father."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς ἕτερον· Ἀκολούθει μοι. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ἀπελθόντι πρῶτον θάψαι τὸν πατέρα μου.

verses.english: But he said to him, "Let the dead bury their own dead; but you, go away and announce the kingdom of God far and wide."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς, σὺ δὲ ἀπελθὼν διάγγελλε τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: And another also said, "I will follow you, lord; but first allow me to take leave of those in my house."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ καὶ ἕτερος· Ἀκολουθήσω σοι, κύριε· πρῶτον δὲ ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ἀποτάξασθαι τοῖς εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου.

verses.english: But Jesus said to him, "No one who has put his hand to a plough and is looking at the things behind is well placed for the kingdom of God."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδεὶς ἐπιβαλὼν τὴν χεῖρα ἐπ’ ἄροτρον καὶ βλέπων εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω εὔθετός ἐστιν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.21.6–7: Peter answers "Tu es Christus", Jesus imposes silence, and gives as the reason that "the son of man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders and scribes and priests, be killed, and rise after the third day". Epiphanius, sch. 16 quotes the prediction in Greek with μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ("after three days") for canonical Luke's "on the third day"; that form is printed (D and the Old Latin have it, as does Mark 8:31). 9:18–19 are read in the Dialogue of Adamantius (84,1–4); Roth counts them as attested. NA27 reads λέγουσιν οἱ ὄχλοι at 9:18 (SBLGNT has a different order).

Tertullian, Marc. 4.21.8–12 quotes 9:24 ("whoever wants to save his soul will destroy it…") and 9:26 ("whoever is ashamed of me, I will be ashamed of him"), and argues at length that only a Christ with a real birth and flesh could be a cause of shame. His quotation of 9:26 lacks "and my words" (also lacking in D and some Old Latin and Old Syriac witnesses) and the coming "in his glory" (9:26b). One witness; NA27 printed and the evidence noted. 9:23, 9:25 and 9:27 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.22.1–16; Epiphanius, sch. 17–18. Both witnesses give the voice as "This is my son, the beloved" (ἀγαπητός; "filius meus dilectus"), and NA27 cites Marcion for it with A C* W, the Byzantine text and the Old Latin; it is printed for canonical Luke's "my chosen". Tertullian says that Marcion did not want Moses shown "speaking with the Lord, but standing" (4.22.16). Roth takes this to mean 9:31b ("they spoke of his departure, which he was to fulfil at Jerusalem") was not in the text, and it is not printed. Epiphanius' copy did have them "talking with him" (9:30), so the copies may have differed on the conversation. 9:36 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Reception and interpretation. For Tertullian the scene proves that Jesus belongs with the law and the prophets: "he would not show them in conversation, a sign of familiarity, nor in a share of his glory" if he had come to destroy them (4.22.2). The Marcionite reading took the voice ("hear him") as transferring authority away from Moses and Elijah (4.22.1). The attested text shows Jesus with Moses and Elijah in glory and the voice naming him son. It does not itself say whether their authority is confirmed or ended.

Epiphanius, sch. 19 quotes the father's words and the reply "to them": »ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος, ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν;«. Tertullian quotes the reply twice (4.23.1–2), "O genitura incredula, quousque ero apud vos? quousque sustinebo vos?". Neither has "and perverse" (καὶ διεστραμμένη), which canonical Luke shares with Matthew 17:17; the shorter address is Mark's (9:19). The words are absent from two witnesses' quotations and are not printed (METHOD §5.3). The witnesses differ on the rest: Tertullian has two "how long" clauses, as in Matthew and Mark, and Epiphanius one. Their copies were harmonized differently, a point made by Williams and BeDuhn (working document §2.2). 9:37–39 and 9:42–43a are not cited and are printed in grey.

Epiphanius, sch. 20 quotes the second passion prediction (9:44). Tertullian, Marc. 4.23.4 sets Jesus' love of children against the Antitheses' example of Elisha and the bears (2 Kgs 2:23–24). NA27 reads ὃς ἐὰν δέξηται at 9:48 (SBLGNT ὃς ἄν). 9:43b and 9:45 are not cited and are printed in grey. 9:49–50 (the strange exorcist) form a separate paragraph that no witness cites, and are not printed.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.23.8–9: against the Creator's fire called down by Elijah (2 Kgs 1:10–12) stands Christ's leniency, "rebuking the disciples who wanted the same punishment for that village of the Samaritans". This attests 9:52, which Roth lists as unattested, and 9:54–55. Two longer readings of canonical manuscripts, "as Elijah did" (9:54) and "you do not know of what spirit you are…" (9:55–56), are not attested for this text. Tertullian brings in Elijah himself, as the Antitheses did. 9:51, 9:53 and 9:56 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.23.9–11 attests all three exchanges, quoting "Let the dead bury their dead, but you go and proclaim the kingdom of God". He argues that the reply keeps the law forbidding priests and Nazirites contact with the dead (Lev 21:1; Num 6:6–7). NA27 prints [κύριε] at 9:59 and [πρὸς αὐτόν] at 9:62 in brackets; both are printed.

Interpretation. The attested text predicts suffering, death and being raised "after three days", and Tertullian takes the prediction as the Creator's prophecy fulfilled (4.21.7). In 9:60 he reads the call to leave the dead to bury their dead as the Nazirite and priestly rule applied to those devoted to the kingdom (4.23.10). Hegesippus' report that James lived as a Nazirite, which the library uses (Carriers of Living Water §3.2), concerns the same pattern of consecration; whether the saying was read that way in the community behind the text cannot be shown from the witnesses.
In private. The learners are with him all the same, as the sentence says.
ἀνίστημι, as at 9:8.

notes.term: Τὸν χριστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ, "the Anointed One of God"
notes.explanation: As at 4:41.
Necessity, as at 4:43.
To be tested and found wanting, thrown out after examination.
The plural: the high priest and the leading priestly families.

notes.term: μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐγερθῆναι, "after three days be raised"
notes.explanation: The reading of this text, "after three days". Canonical Luke has "on the third day". ἐγείρω, passive.
ἀρνέομαι, to say no to, disown, deny. It is the verb of 8:45, "all were denying it".
The Roman stake or cross on which the condemned were executed.
The living self, the life a person has. "Life" is the sense in many translations; "soul" keeps the word.
ἀπόλλυμι, to destroy or to lose. "Lose" is often used here. "Destroy" keeps the verb of 4:34, 5:37 and 6:9.
To be fined, to forfeit.
To be ashamed of, to disown out of shame.
ἄγγελος, messenger, as at 7:24 and 7:27. "Angels" is the Greek word left untranslated, and it brings the later doctrine of a class of beings.
A Greek word here, not ἀμήν.
A Semitic way of saying "die".

notes.term: τὸ εἶδος… ἕτερον, "the look… became other"
notes.explanation: εἶδος is form, appearance; ἕτερος is other, different. The Greek has no verb: "the look of his face, other".
From ἀστραπή, "lightning".
The aorist passive of ὁράω, "to see": "having been seen", "appearing".
Heavy with sleep.
To stay awake through, to wake fully.
καλός, as at 6:43.
Booths, as at the feast of Booths.
To cast a shadow over.

notes.term: ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, "my son, the beloved"
notes.explanation: The reading of this text. Canonical Luke has "my son, the chosen one". Lower case "son": the voice names a relation, not a title.
ἀκούω, to hear, listen, obey.
To cry aloud.
To tear, rend, throw into convulsions.
To break in pieces, shatter.
ἐκβάλλω, as at 6:42.
ἄπιστος, without trust (πίστις). This text lacks "and perverse".
To hold up under, endure.
ῥήγνυμι, to break, tear, throw down.
ἰάομαι.
Greatness, magnificence.

notes.term: Θέσθε… εἰς τὰ ὦτα, "put… into your ears"
notes.explanation: Literally "place these words into your ears".
παραδίδωμι, to hand over, deliver. "Betray" is one use of it, but the word itself says "hand over".
Covered over, hidden by a veil.
As at 5:22.
The Greek has comparatives and a positive, not superlatives. "The greatest" and "the least" are usual in English but say more than the Greek.
The diminutive of παῖς.
δέχομαι, to receive, welcome.

notes.term: ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὰς ἡμέρας, "as the days were being filled"
notes.explanation: The days are filled up, completed.

notes.term: τῆς ἀναλήμψεως αὐτοῦ, "of his taking up"
notes.explanation: ἀνάλημψις, a being taken up. It can mean his being taken up into heaven, or his being taken away from this life.

notes.term: τὸ πρόσωπον ἐστήρισεν, "set his face firmly"
notes.explanation: στηρίζω, to fix, make firm. A Hebrew idiom for resolve.
ἄγγελος, here human messengers.

notes.term: τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἦν πορευόμενον, "his face was journeying"
notes.explanation: Word for word. It means that he was on his way to Jerusalem.
To use up, destroy.
Literally "tentings", places to settle or roost.
κλίνω, to bend, lay down, incline. It is the same verb as "the day began to decline" (9:12).
ἀφίημι, as at 6:42.
To announce throughout, spread the news.
To say goodbye, set oneself apart from.
Fit, suitable, rightly set.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 8
chapters.preamble: The mission of the seventy and what follows from it. Jesus sends out seventy others, two by two, with the instructions Tertullian reads as the Creator's own: no sandals, no greetings on the road, peace to the house, "the worker deserves his wages", and the dust wiped off against a town that refuses them, "yet know this: the kingdom of God has come near". Whoever rejects them rejects him; he gives them authority over snakes and scorpions. He then thanks the "Lord of heaven" that what was hidden from the wise has been revealed to little children, and says that no one knows who the Father is except the son. To a lawyer who asks what he must do to inherit life ("life", not "eternal life", as Tertullian points out) he answers with the command to love God, and "do this and you will live". Canonical Luke's judgement on Sodom and the woes on the Galilean towns, "I saw Satan fall", the parable of the Samaritan and the visit to Martha and Mary are not cited by either witness and are not printed.

verses.english: After this the Lord appointed seventy others and sent them on ahead of him, two by two, into every town and place where he himself was about to come.
verses.greek: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἀνέδειξεν ὁ κύριος ἑτέρους ἑβδομήκοντα καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀνὰ δύο δύο πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν πόλιν καὶ τόπον οὗ ἤμελλεν αὐτὸς ἔρχεσθαι.

verses.english: He said to them, "The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few; so ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.
verses.greek: ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς, οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι· δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐργάτας ἐκβάλῃ εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: Go; behold, I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
verses.greek: ὑπάγετε· ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς ἄρνας ἐν μέσῳ λύκων.

verses.english: Carry no purse, no bag, no sandals; and greet no one on the road.
verses.greek: μὴ βαστάζετε βαλλάντιον, μὴ πήραν, μὴ ὑποδήματα, καὶ μηδένα κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἀσπάσησθε.

verses.english: Whatever house you enter, first say, "Peace to this house."
verses.greek: εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν εἰσέλθητε οἰκίαν πρῶτον λέγετε· Εἰρήνη τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ.

verses.english: And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐὰν ἐκεῖ ᾖ υἱὸς εἰρήνης, ἐπαναπαήσεται ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν· εἰ δὲ μή γε, ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἀνακάμψει.

verses.english: Stay in that same house, eating and drinking what they provide, for the worker deserves his wages. Do not move from house to house.
verses.greek: ἐν αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ οἰκίᾳ μένετε, ἐσθίοντες καὶ πίνοντες τὰ παρ’ αὐτῶν, ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ. μὴ μεταβαίνετε ἐξ οἰκίας εἰς οἰκίαν.

verses.english: Whenever you enter a town and they welcome you, eat what is set before you;
verses.greek: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν πόλιν εἰσέρχησθε καὶ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐσθίετε τὰ παρατιθέμενα ὑμῖν,

verses.english: heal the sick in it and say to them, "The kingdom of God has come near to you."
verses.greek: καὶ θεραπεύετε τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ ἀσθενεῖς, καὶ λέγετε αὐτοῖς· Ἤγγικεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: But whenever you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go out into its streets and say,
verses.greek: εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν πόλιν εἰσέλθητε καὶ μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐξελθόντες εἰς τὰς πλατείας αὐτῆς εἴπατε·

verses.english: "Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet we wipe off against you. Yet know this: the kingdom of God has come near."
verses.greek: Καὶ τὸν κονιορτὸν τὸν κολληθέντα ἡμῖν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ὑμῶν εἰς τοὺς πόδας ἀπομασσόμεθα ὑμῖν· πλὴν τοῦτο γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me; and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me."
verses.greek: Ὁ ἀκούων ὑμῶν ἐμοῦ ἀκούει, καὶ ὁ ἀθετῶν ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ ἀθετεῖ· ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ ἀθετῶν ἀθετεῖ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.

verses.english: The seventy returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the daimons submit to us in your name!"
verses.greek: Ὑπέστρεψαν δὲ οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα μετὰ χαρᾶς λέγοντες· Κύριε, καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ὑποτάσσεται ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου.

verses.english: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy; and nothing will harm you.
verses.greek: ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πατεῖν ἐπάνω ὄφεων καὶ σκορπίων, καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ, καὶ οὐδὲν ὑμᾶς οὐ μὴ ἀδικήσῃ.

verses.english: Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits submit to you; rejoice rather that your names are written in the heavens."
verses.greek: πλὴν ἐν τούτῳ μὴ χαίρετε ὅτι τὰ πνεύματα ὑμῖν ὑποτάσσεται, χαίρετε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ὀνόματα ὑμῶν ἐγγέγραπται ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.

verses.english: In that same hour he rejoiced in the holy spirit and said, "I thank you, Lord of heaven, that what was hidden from the wise and understanding you have revealed to little children. Yes, Father, for so it was pleasing in your sight.
verses.greek: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἠγαλλιάσατο ἐν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ καὶ εἶπεν· Εὐχαριστῶ σοι, κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ὅτι ἅτινα ἦν κρυπτὰ σοφοῖς καὶ συνετοῖς ἀπεκάλυψας νηπίοις· ναὶ ὁ πατήρ, ὅτι οὕτως εὐδοκία ἐγένετο ἔμπροσθέν σου.

verses.english: All things have been handed over to me by my Father; and no one knows who the Father is except the son, and who the son is except the Father, and anyone to whom the son chooses to reveal him."
verses.greek: πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ οὐδεὶς γινώσκει τίς ἐστιν ὁ πατὴρ εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱός, καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι.

verses.english: Then turning to the disciples he said privately, "Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
verses.greek: Καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς κατ’ ἰδίαν εἶπεν· Μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ οἱ βλέποντες ἃ βλέπετε.

verses.english: For I tell you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it."
verses.greek: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ βασιλεῖς ἠθέλησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ ὑμεῖς βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.

verses.english: And behold, a lawyer stood up to test him, saying, "Teacher, what must I do to inherit life?"
verses.greek: Καὶ ἰδοὺ νομικός τις ἀνέστη ἐκπειράζων αὐτὸν λέγων· Διδάσκαλε, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν κληρονομήσω;

verses.english: He said to him, "What is written in the law? How do you read it?"
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τί γέγραπται; πῶς ἀναγινώσκεις;

verses.english: He answered, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbour as yourself."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου, καὶ τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.

verses.english: He said to him, "You have answered rightly; do this, and you will live."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἀπεκρίθης· τοῦτο ποίει καὶ ζήσῃ.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.24.1–7 follows the instructions in order: seventy others appointed, sent into towns, no sandals, no greetings on the road (as Elisha told Gehazi, 2 Kgs 4:29), peace to the house (as Elisha to the Shunammite, 2 Kgs 4:26), "the worker deserves his wages" (as the law on the ox, Deut 25:4), the kingdom announced as "near", and the words to a town that refuses them. The number is seventy: Tertullian sets the seventy beside the seventy palms of Elim as he sets the twelve beside its twelve springs (Exod 15:27). NA27 prints "seventy [two]" with the second word bracketed; it is not printed here (METHOD §5.7). 10:2–3 and 10:6 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Sodom "on that day" and the woes on Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum. Tertullian goes from 10:11 to 10:16 and argues, at length, that the dust saying implies a judgement: "if he does not command it as a threat, he commands it in vain" (4.24.7). The verses that state the judgement in so many words, and name the Creator's judgement on Sodom, would have ended the argument. He does not cite them. They are classed "unattested, probably absent".

Tertullian quotes "Whoever rejects you rejects me" (4.24.8) and asks who will give power "to tread on snakes and scorpions" if not the Lord of all creatures (4.24.9). He reads the snakes and scorpions as the spiritual powers of wickedness and their prince as the serpent and dragon of Ps 91:13 and Isa 27:1 (4.24.10). "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven" (10:18), which would have suited that reading, is not cited and is not printed. 10:17 and 10:20 are printed in grey. "Seventy" at 10:17 follows 10:1.

Both witnesses quote the thanksgiving. Epiphanius, sch. 22: "I thank you, Lord of heaven"; the text "did not have 'and of the earth', nor did it have 'Father'", but it did have "Yes, Father" further on. Tertullian, Marc. 4.25.1: "Gratias ago, et confiteor, domine caeli, quod ea quae erant abscondita sapientibus et prudentibus, revelaveris parvulis." The address without "and of the earth" is also the reading of 𝔓45. In Tertullian the hiding has no stated subject: what was hidden, God has revealed. His later reply that the Marcionite God, revealing what the Creator had hidden, would have been doing the Creator's work (4.25.6) presupposes that wording. The Greek printed is Roth's retroversion; the sense is attested, the exact words are not. Tertullian's "et confiteor" (= canonical ἐξομολογοῦμαι) is in his text only and is not printed.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.25.10 quotes the saying with the Father first: "No one knows who the Father is except the son, and who the son is except the Father" (canonical Luke has the son first). The order is attested also by the Dialogue of Adamantius and by Eznik, and is found in some manuscripts and fathers (Roth). Tertullian comments: "and so Christ preached an unknown God" — the Marcionite reading of the saying, which he answers from Isaiah ("Israel did not know me", Isa 1:3). The words in brackets after the quotation in the manuscripts of Tertullian give Matthew's wording and are a copyist's addition.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.25.14: "In the gospel of truth the lawyer asks, 'What must I do to obtain eternal life?' In the heretical one only 'life' is set down, with no mention of 'eternal'." This is one of the few places where Tertullian states a difference between the two texts, and in 4.25.18 he allows that "ours" may have added the word. The text printed reads "inherit life". Epiphanius, sch. 23 quotes Jesus' question "What is written in the law?" and his reply "You have said rightly; do this and you will live" (10:26, 28). Tertullian's quotation of the command (10:27) has three clauses (heart, soul, strength) and no neighbour clause; NA27 cites his Marcion for the lack of "with all your mind". These are noted, not adopted (one witness).

The parable of the Samaritan (10:29–37) and the visit to Martha and Mary (10:38–42). In both witnesses the exchange with the lawyer ends at 10:28; Tertullian goes on to 11:1 and Epiphanius to 11:5. For the parable, silence counts: it expounds the law's own command of love, the point Tertullian was arguing ("he set before him the head of the law", 4.25.15), and it would have served him. It is classed "unattested, probably absent". The Martha and Mary passage touches nothing either father argues, so their silence shows nothing; it is "unattested, undetermined" and, as a paragraph with no attested verse, is not printed (METHOD §4.3).

Interpretation. In the attested text the way to "life" is the command of Deuteronomy 6:5, and Jesus' answer is "do this, and you will live" (cf. Lev 18:5). Tertullian takes the shorter question to concern the long life the law promises (4.25.14); the text itself does not say which life is meant. What it does show is a teacher who answers a question about life with the law's first command and a call to do it — the pattern of 6:46 and 8:21 in this reconstruction, and of the Epistle of James ("be doers of the word", Jas 1:22).

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 9
chapters.preamble: Prayer, the finger of God, and the woes. Asked by a disciple to teach them to pray, Jesus gives a prayer that in this text asks first for the holy spirit, then for the kingdom, for "your bread", forgiveness, and not to be brought into temptation (Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.3–5; Origen). Its parables end with the Father who gives the holy spirit to those who ask.
