Accused of casting out daimons by Beelzebul, Jesus answers that he does it "by the finger of God", the words the Egyptian magicians used before Moses (Exod 8:19). To a generation seeking a sign he says that no sign will be given to it; this text has no sign of Jonah and no Nineveh or queen of the south (Epiphanius, sch. 25). At a Pharisee's table come the sayings on the inside and the outside of the cup and the woes on Pharisees and lawyers; the Pharisees pass over "the calling and the love of God". The saying of "the wisdom of God" about the blood of the prophets is not in this text (sch. 28).

verses.english: Once he was praying in a certain place, and when he had finished, one of his disciples said to him, "Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples."
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ προσευχόμενον, ὡς ἐπαύσατο, εἶπέν τις τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· Κύριε, δίδαξον ἡμᾶς προσεύχεσθαι, καθὼς καὶ Ἰωάννης ἐδίδαξεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: He said to them, "When you pray, say: Father, may your holy spirit come; may your kingdom come;
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὅταν προσεύχησθε, λέγετε· Πάτερ, ἐλθέτω τὸ πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἅγιον· ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου·

verses.english: give us each day your bread for the coming day;
verses.greek: τὸν ἄρτον σου τὸν ἐπιούσιον δίδου ἡμῖν τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν·

verses.english: and forgive us our sins, for we ourselves forgive everyone indebted to us; and do not bring us into temptation."
verses.greek: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἀφίομεν παντὶ ὀφείλοντι ἡμῖν· καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "Which of you has a friend, and goes to him at midnight and says to him, 'Friend, lend me three loaves,
verses.greek: Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἕξει φίλον καὶ πορεύσεται πρὸς αὐτὸν μεσονυκτίου καὶ εἴπῃ αὐτῷ· Φίλε, χρῆσόν μοι τρεῖς ἄρτους,

verses.english: for a friend of mine has arrived from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him';
verses.greek: ἐπειδὴ φίλος μου παρεγένετο ἐξ ὁδοῦ πρός με καὶ οὐκ ἔχω ὃ παραθήσω αὐτῷ·

verses.english: and he answers from inside, 'Do not bother me; the door is already shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot get up and give you anything'?
verses.greek: κἀκεῖνος ἔσωθεν ἀποκριθεὶς εἴπῃ· Μή μοι κόπους πάρεχε· ἤδη ἡ θύρα κέκλεισται, καὶ τὰ παιδία μου μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὴν κοίτην εἰσίν· οὐ δύναμαι ἀναστὰς δοῦναί σοι.

verses.english: I tell you, even if he will not get up and give him anything because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence he will rise and give him whatever he needs.
verses.greek: λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ καὶ οὐ δώσει αὐτῷ ἀναστὰς διὰ τὸ εἶναι φίλον αὐτοῦ, διά γε τὴν ἀναίδειαν αὐτοῦ ἐγερθεὶς δώσει αὐτῷ ὅσων χρῄζει.

verses.english: So I say to you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
verses.greek: Κἀγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν·

verses.english: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
verses.greek: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει, καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει, καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.

verses.english: What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead of a fish?
verses.greek: τίνα δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν τὸν πατέρα αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς ἰχθύν, καὶ ἀντὶ ἰχθύος ὄφιν αὐτῷ ἐπιδώσει;

verses.english: Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
verses.greek: ἢ καὶ αἰτήσει ᾠόν, ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ σκορπίον;

verses.english: If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the holy spirit to those who ask him!"
verses.greek: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὑπάρχοντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ δώσει πνεῦμα ἅγιον τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.

verses.english: Now he was casting out a daimon, and it was mute. When the daimon had gone out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds were amazed.
verses.greek: Καὶ ἦν ἐκβάλλων δαιμόνιον καὶ αὐτὸ ἦν κωφόν· ἐγένετο δὲ τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐξελθόντος ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι·

verses.english: But some of them said, "He casts out the daimons by Beelzebul, the ruler of the daimons."
verses.greek: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπον· Ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια·

verses.english: Others, to test him, demanded from him a sign from heaven.
verses.greek: ἕτεροι δὲ πειράζοντες σημεῖον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐζήτουν παρ’ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: But he knew their thoughts and said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls on house.
verses.greek: αὐτὸς δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὰ διανοήματα εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν διαμερισθεῖσα ἐρημοῦται, καὶ οἶκος ἐπὶ οἶκον πίπτει.

verses.english: If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out the daimons by Beelzebul.
verses.greek: εἰ δὲ καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν διεμερίσθη, πῶς σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ; ὅτι λέγετε ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλειν με τὰ δαιμόνια.

verses.english: And if I cast out the daimons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
verses.greek: εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν; διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ ὑμῶν κριταὶ ἔσονται.

verses.english: But if I cast out the daimons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
verses.greek: εἰ δὲ ἐν δακτύλῳ θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own court, his possessions are safe;
verses.greek: ὅταν ὁ ἰσχυρὸς καθωπλισμένος φυλάσσῃ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ αὐλήν, ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἐστὶν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ·

verses.english: but when one stronger than he attacks him and overcomes him, he takes away the armour in which he trusted and divides his plunder.
verses.greek: ἐπὰν δὲ ἰσχυρότερος αὐτοῦ ἐπελθὼν νικήσῃ αὐτόν, τὴν πανοπλίαν αὐτοῦ αἴρει ἐφ’ ᾗ ἐπεποίθει, καὶ τὰ σκῦλα αὐτοῦ διαδίδωσιν.

verses.english: Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
verses.greek: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.

verses.english: While he was saying this, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him, "Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts that you sucked!"
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας·

verses.english: But he said, "Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it!"
verses.greek: αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν· Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες.

verses.english: As the crowds were increasing, he began to say, "This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it."
verses.greek: Τῶν δὲ ὄχλων ἐπαθροιζομένων ἤρξατο λέγειν· Ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη γενεὰ πονηρά ἐστιν· σημεῖον ζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ.

verses.english: No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
verses.greek: Οὐδεὶς λύχνον ἅψας εἰς κρύπτην τίθησιν οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι τὸ φῶς βλέπωσιν.

verses.english: While he was speaking, a Pharisee asked him to dine with him; so he went in and reclined at table.
verses.greek: Ἐν δὲ τῷ λαλῆσαι ἐρωτᾷ αὐτὸν Φαρισαῖος ὅπως ἀριστήσῃ παρ’ αὐτῷ· εἰσελθὼν δὲ ἀνέπεσεν.

verses.english: The Pharisee began to debate within himself, saying, "Why did he not first wash before the meal?"
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Φαρισαῖος ἤρξατο διακρινόμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγειν διὰ τί οὐ πρῶτον ἐβαπτίσθη πρὸ τοῦ ἀρίστου.

verses.english: But the Lord said to him, "Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and of the dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· Νῦν ὑμεῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τοῦ πίνακος καθαρίζετε, τὸ δὲ ἔσωθεν ὑμῶν γέμει ἁρπαγῆς καὶ πονηρίας.

verses.english: Fools! Did not the one who made the outside make the inside also?
verses.greek: ἄφρονες, οὐχ ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔξωθεν καὶ τὸ ἔσωθεν ἐποίησεν;

verses.english: But give as alms what is within, and behold, everything is clean for you.
verses.greek: πλὴν τὰ ἐνόντα δότε ἐλεημοσύνην, καὶ ἰδοὺ πάντα καθαρὰ ὑμῖν ἐστιν.

verses.english: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, and pass over the calling and the love of God. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.
verses.greek: Ἀλλὰ οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ πήγανον καὶ πᾶν λάχανον, καὶ παρέρχεσθε τὴν κλῆσιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ· ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ παρεῖναι.

verses.english: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seat in the synagogues and greetings in the market-places.
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀγαπᾶτε τὴν πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς.

verses.english: Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, and people walk over them without knowing it."
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἐστὲ ὡς τὰ μνημεῖα τὰ ἄδηλα, καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ περιπατοῦντες ἐπάνω οὐκ οἴδασιν.

verses.english: One of the lawyers answered him, "Teacher, in saying this you insult us too."
verses.greek: Ἀποκριθεὶς δέ τις τῶν νομικῶν λέγει αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα λέγων καὶ ἡμᾶς ὑβρίζεις.

verses.english: And he said, "Woe to you lawyers also! For you load people with burdens hard to bear, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς οὐαί, ὅτι φορτίζετε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους φορτία δυσβάστακτα, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἑνὶ τῶν δακτύλων ὑμῶν οὐ προσψαύετε τοῖς φορτίοις.

verses.english: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν προφητῶν οἱ δὲ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτούς.

verses.english: So you are witnesses and approve of the deeds of your fathers; for they killed them, and you build.
verses.greek: ἄρα μάρτυρές ἐστε καὶ συνευδοκεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν, ὅτι αὐτοὶ μὲν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτοὺς ὑμεῖς δὲ οἰκοδομεῖτε.

verses.english: Woe to you lawyers! For you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not enter yourselves, and you hindered those who were entering."
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς, ὅτι ἤρατε τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς γνώσεως· αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσήλθατε καὶ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἐκωλύσατε.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.1–5 does not quote the prayer. He turns each petition into a question about which God it is addressed to, in the order of the prayer, and then says "in this order" (hoc ordine): "To whom shall I say, Father?… From whom shall I ask the holy spirit?… Whose kingdom shall I wish to come?… Who will give me daily bread?… Who will forgive me my sins?… Who will not let us be led into temptation?" There is no question about the hallowing of the name. The text therefore asked for the holy spirit where canonical Luke has "hallowed be your name", and kept "your kingdom come". Tertullian does not give the wording of the request for the spirit. The Greek printed takes the form of the only Greek witnesses with such a petition in Luke (minuscules 700 and 162, Gregory of Nyssa), shortened to what Tertullian attests. In those witnesses it replaces "your kingdom come"; here it stands beside it. Origen quotes the bread petition of "those from Marcion" in Greek: "your bread" (τὸν ἄρτον σου), not "our bread". He asks them "what is the bread of God?" ἐπιούσιος is translated "for the coming day"; Tertullian has "daily" (cotidianum).

notes.term: The holy spirit asked and given (11:2, 11:13)
notes.explanation: Interpretation. In this text the prayer opens with a request for the holy spirit, and the teaching that follows ends with the Father who will "give the holy spirit to those who ask him" (11:13; Tertullian 4.26.10). The unit begins and ends with the spirit. The bread asked for is the Father's ("your bread"), and Origen's question to the Marcionites, "what is the bread of God?", shows that they read it as more than food. This is the reception, and the text does not settle that reading. What the text itself shows is a prayer centred on receiving from the Father. The library reads such receiving as influx into a vessel (The River and the Vessel).

Epiphanius, sch. 24 quotes 11:5, 11:9a and 11:11–13 in one scholion; Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.5–10 alludes to the friend at midnight, the door already shut with the children in bed, the request granted because of persistence, the asking, seeking and knocking, and the snake and scorpion. Neither witness has the pair "bread and stone" that most manuscripts add at 11:11 (it is also absent in 𝔓45, 𝔓75 and B). 11:6 and 11:10 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.10–12 quotes "If I cast out daimons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out?" and "If I by the finger of God cast out daimons, has the kingdom of God not come near to you?" He points out that the Egyptian magicians called the Creator's power "the finger of God" (Exod 8:19), and that the stronger man of the parable overcomes the prince of daimons. NA27 prints [καὶ αὐτὸ ἦν] at 11:14 and [ἐγώ] at 11:20 in brackets; both are printed (SBLGNT omits them). 11:16–17 and 11:23 are not cited and are printed in grey. The return of the unclean spirit (11:24–26), a paragraph that no witness cites, is not printed.

Epiphanius, sch. 25: "he cut out what is about Jonah the prophet; for he had 'this generation — no sign will be given to it'; he did not have what is about Nineveh and the queen of the south and Solomon." Tertullian: Christ "does not give a sign to those who ask" (4.27.1). The saying in this text ends "no sign will be given to it". Canonical Luke adds "except the sign of Jonah" and the sayings on the Ninevites and the queen of the south (11:30–32, Matthew 12:39–42). The verbs "he cut" are Epiphanius' charge. What they report as content is that the words were not there.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.27.2–5. The Pharisee "was debating within himself why he had not first been washed before reclining, according to the law". That is the reading of codex D and the Old Latin, and it is printed in D's Greek. Canonical Luke has the Pharisee "amazed". Jesus' reply on the outside and inside of the cup, "Did not the one who made the outside make the inside also?", is glossed by Tertullian as flesh and soul made by one God. At 11:42 both witnesses read that the Pharisees pass over "the calling (κλῆσις) and the love of God", not "justice (κρίσις) and the love of God"; Tertullian repeats "calling" in 4.27.6. The reading is printed. 11:44 is not cited and is printed in grey.

notes.term: Woes on the lawyers (11:45–52; 11:49–51 not printed)
notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.27.6–9; Epiphanius, sch. 27–28. The lawyers load others with burdens hard to bear; they build the tombs of the prophets their fathers killed; they have taken the key of knowledge (Tertullian: "the interpretation of the law"). Epiphanius states that the text did not have the saying "Therefore the wisdom of God said, 'I will send them prophets…'" or the blood of the prophets from Abel to Zechariah "required of this generation" (11:49–51). At 11:48 Tertullian's comment ("they testified that they did not consent to the deeds of their fathers") agrees with the reading of D, "you testify that you do not approve"; it is not a quotation and is recorded, not adopted. 11:45 is not cited and is printed in grey. 11:53–54 form a paragraph that no witness cites and are not printed.

Interpretation. In the attested text the charge against the Pharisees is that they tithe herbs and pass over "the calling and the love of God". Tertullian reads "calling" as God calling Israel out of Egypt and "love" as the first commandment (Deut 6:5), quoted in that form (4.27.4). The pairing fits the reconstruction's earlier sayings: the lawyer is answered with the command to love God (10:27). It also fits a criticism of religious leaders made from within the law, for neglecting what the law puts first.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 10
chapters.preamble: Fear and trust. Jesus warns his disciples against the leaven of the Pharisees and tells them not to fear those who can only kill the body, but the one who has authority to cast into Gehenna. Whoever acknowledges him will be acknowledged "before God" (this text has no angels in 12:8–9), and the holy spirit will teach them what to say. He refuses to divide an inheritance and tells of the rich fool. He tells them not to worry about food and clothing, but to seek the kingdom of God, which "the Father" is pleased to give them. Then come the parables of watchfulness: servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding "in the evening watch", the thief, and the steward. He has come to cast fire on the earth and to bring division, and he calls the crowds hypocrites who read the face of heaven and earth but not the present time. The five sparrows (12:6), which Epiphanius says the text lacked, and the saying on God clothing the grass (12:28a) are not printed.

verses.english: Meanwhile, when the crowd had gathered in thousands, so that they trampled on one another, he began to say to his disciples first, "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
verses.greek: Ἐν οἷς ἐπισυναχθεισῶν τῶν μυριάδων τοῦ ὄχλου, ὥστε καταπατεῖν ἀλλήλους, ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ πρῶτον· Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης, ἥτις ἐστὶν ὑπόκρισις, τῶν Φαρισαίων.

verses.english: Nothing is covered up that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not be known.
verses.greek: οὐδὲν δὲ συγκεκαλυμμένον ἐστὶν ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.

verses.english: Therefore whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered in private rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
verses.greek: ἀνθ’ ὧν ὅσα ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτὶ ἀκουσθήσεται, καὶ ὃ πρὸς τὸ οὖς ἐλαλήσατε ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις κηρυχθήσεται ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.

verses.english: I tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do nothing more.
verses.greek: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν τοῖς φίλοις μου, μὴ φοβηθῆτε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεινόντων τὸ σῶμα καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα μὴ ἐχόντων περισσότερόν τι ποιῆσαι.

verses.english: But I will show you whom to fear: fear the one who, after he has killed, has authority to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
verses.greek: ὑποδείξω δὲ ὑμῖν τίνα φοβηθῆτε· φοβήθητε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποκτεῖναι ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν βαλεῖν εἰς γέενναν· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, τοῦτον φοβήθητε.

verses.english: I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, the son of man also will acknowledge before God;
verses.greek: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, πᾶς ὃς ἂν ὁμολογήσῃ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὁμολογήσει ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θεοῦ·

verses.english: but whoever denies me before people will be denied before God.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ ἀρνησάμενός με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρνηθήσεται ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: And everyone who speaks a word against the son of man will be forgiven; but whoever blasphemes against the holy spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.greek: καὶ πᾶς ὃς ἐρεῖ λόγον εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ τῷ δὲ εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα βλασφημήσαντι οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.

verses.english: When they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not worry about how or what you are to answer, or what you are to say;
verses.greek: ὅταν δὲ εἰσφέρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐπὶ τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί ἀπολογήσησθε ἢ τί εἴπητε·

verses.english: for the holy spirit will teach you in that very hour what you ought to say."
verses.greek: τὸ γὰρ ἅγιον πνεῦμα διδάξει ὑμᾶς ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἃ δεῖ εἰπεῖν.

verses.english: Someone in the crowd said to him, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me."
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δέ τις ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπὲ τῷ ἀδελφῷ μου μερίσασθαι μετ’ ἐμοῦ τὴν κληρονομίαν.

verses.english: But he said to him, "Man, who appointed me a judge or arbitrator over you?"
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπε, τίς με κατέστησεν κριτὴν ἢ μεριστὴν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς;

verses.english: And he said to them, "Take care, and be on your guard against all greed; for one's life does not consist in the abundance of one's possessions."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ φυλάσσεσθε ἀπὸ πάσης πλεονεξίας, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν τινὶ ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ.

verses.english: And he told them a parable: "The land of a rich man produced plentifully.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων· Ἀνθρώπου τινὸς πλουσίου εὐφόρησεν ἡ χώρα.

verses.english: And he thought to himself, 'What shall I do, for I have nowhere to store my crops?'
verses.greek: καὶ διελογίζετο ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Τί ποιήσω, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχω ποῦ συνάξω τοὺς καρπούς μου;

verses.english: Then he said, 'I will do this: I will pull down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτο ποιήσω· καθελῶ μου τὰς ἀποθήκας καὶ μείζονας οἰκοδομήσω, καὶ συνάξω ἐκεῖ πάντα τὸν σῖτον καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά μου,

verses.english: And I will say to my soul: Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years; relax, eat, drink, be merry.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἐρῶ τῇ ψυχῇ μου· Ψυχή, ἔχεις πολλὰ ἀγαθὰ κείμενα εἰς ἔτη πολλά· ἀναπαύου, φάγε, πίε, εὐφραίνου.

verses.english: But God said to him, 'Fool! This night your soul is demanded of you; and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?'
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός· Ἄφρων, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τὴν ψυχήν σου ἀπαιτοῦσιν ἀπὸ σοῦ· ἃ δὲ ἡτοίμασας, τίνι ἔσται;

verses.english: So it is with whoever stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God."
verses.greek: οὕτως ὁ θησαυρίζων ἑαυτῷ καὶ μὴ εἰς θεὸν πλουτῶν.

verses.english: And he said to his disciples, "Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will wear.
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι τί ἐνδύσησθε.

verses.english: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
verses.greek: ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος.

verses.english: Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have neither storehouse nor barn, and God feeds them. Of how much more value are you than the birds!
verses.greek: κατανοήσατε τοὺς κόρακας ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν, οἷς οὐκ ἔστιν ταμεῖον οὐδὲ ἀποθήκη, καὶ ὁ θεὸς τρέφει αὐτούς· πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμεῖς διαφέρετε τῶν πετεινῶν.

verses.english: And which of you by worrying can add a single cubit to his span of life?
verses.greek: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ προσθεῖναι πῆχυν;

verses.english: If then you are not able to do so small a thing as that, why do you worry about the rest?
verses.greek: εἰ οὖν οὐδὲ ἐλάχιστον δύνασθε, τί περὶ τῶν λοιπῶν μεριμνᾶτε;

verses.english: Consider the lilies, how they neither spin nor weave; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not clothed like one of these.
verses.greek: κατανοήσατε τὰ κρίνα πῶς οὔτε νήθει οὔτε ὑφαίνει· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.

verses.english: How much more you, you of little faith!
verses.greek: πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι.

verses.english: And do not seek what you are to eat and what you are to drink, and do not be anxious.
verses.greek: καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ ζητεῖτε τί φάγητε καὶ τί πίητε, καὶ μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε,

verses.english: For all the nations of the world seek these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
verses.greek: ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου ἐπιζητοῦσιν, ὑμῶν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ οἶδεν ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων.

verses.english: Instead, seek the kingdom of God, and these things will be added to you.
verses.greek: πλὴν ζητεῖτε τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.

verses.english: Do not be afraid, little flock, for it has pleased the Father to give you the kingdom.
verses.greek: Μὴ φοβοῦ, τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον, ὅτι εὐδόκησεν ὁ πατὴρ δοῦναι ὑμῖν τὴν βασιλείαν.

verses.english: Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning,
verses.greek: Ἔστωσαν ὑμῶν αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι καὶ οἱ λύχνοι καιόμενοι,

verses.english: and be like people waiting for their master to come home from the wedding feast, so that they may open to him at once when he comes and knocks.
verses.greek: καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅμοιοι ἀνθρώποις προσδεχομένοις τὸν κύριον ἑαυτῶν πότε ἀναλύσῃ ἐκ τῶν γάμων, ἵνα ἐλθόντος καὶ κρούσαντος εὐθέως ἀνοίξωσιν αὐτῷ.

verses.english: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds awake when he comes; truly I tell you, he will gird himself and have them recline at table, and he will come and serve them.
verses.greek: μακάριοι οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι, οὓς ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος εὑρήσει γρηγοροῦντας· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι περιζώσεται καὶ ἀνακλινεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ παρελθὼν διακονήσει αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: If he comes in the evening watch and finds them so, blessed are they.
verses.greek: κἂν ἐν τῇ ἑσπερινῇ φυλακῇ ἔλθῃ καὶ εὕρῃ οὕτως, μακάριοί εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι.

verses.english: But know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
verses.greek: Τοῦτο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ ὥρᾳ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, οὐκ ἂν ἀφῆκεν διορυχθῆναι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: You also must be ready, for the son of man is coming at an hour you do not expect."
verses.greek: καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.

verses.english: Peter said, "Lord, are you telling this parable for us or for all?"
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Κύριε, πρὸς ἡμᾶς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγεις ἢ καὶ πρὸς πάντας;

verses.english: And the Lord said, "Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his master will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the proper time?
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος· Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς οἰκονόμος, ὁ φρόνιμος, ὃν καταστήσει ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς θεραπείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ διδόναι ἐν καιρῷ τὸ σιτομέτριον;

verses.english: Blessed is that servant whom his master will find so doing when he comes.
verses.greek: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος, ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει ποιοῦντα οὕτως·

verses.english: Truly I tell you, he will set him over all his possessions.
verses.greek: ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.

verses.english: But if that servant says in his heart, 'My master is delayed in coming', and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
verses.greek: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἔρχεσθαι, καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰς παιδίσκας, ἐσθίειν τε καὶ πίνειν καὶ μεθύσκεσθαι,

verses.english: the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in pieces and put him with the unfaithful.
verses.greek: ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει, καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀπίστων θήσει.

verses.english: That servant who knew his master's will but did not get ready or act according to his will shall receive a severe beating.
verses.greek: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ὁ γνοὺς τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ ἑτοιμάσας ἢ ποιήσας πρὸς τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ δαρήσεται πολλάς·

verses.english: But the one who did not know, and did what deserved a beating, shall receive a light beating. Everyone to whom much was given, of him much will be required; and from the one to whom much was entrusted, they will demand the more.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ μὴ γνοὺς ποιήσας δὲ ἄξια πληγῶν δαρήσεται ὀλίγας. παντὶ δὲ ᾧ ἐδόθη πολύ, πολὺ ζητηθήσεται παρ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ᾧ παρέθεντο πολύ, περισσότερον αἰτήσουσιν αὐτόν.

verses.english: I came to cast fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
verses.greek: Πῦρ ἦλθον βαλεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τί θέλω εἰ ἤδη ἀνήφθη;

verses.english: I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how I am constrained until it is accomplished!
verses.greek: βάπτισμα δὲ ἔχω βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ πῶς συνέχομαι ἕως ὅτου τελεσθῇ.

verses.english: Do you think that I have come to give peace on earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.
verses.greek: δοκεῖτε ὅτι εἰρήνην παρεγενόμην δοῦναι ἐν τῇ γῇ; οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλ’ ἢ διαμερισμόν.

verses.english: For from now on in one house there will be five divided, three against two and two against three.
verses.greek: ἔσονται γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν πέντε ἐν ἑνὶ οἴκῳ διαμεμερισμένοι, τρεῖς ἐπὶ δυσὶν καὶ δύο ἐπὶ τρισίν,

verses.english: Father will be divided against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law."
verses.greek: διαμερισθήσεται πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ καὶ υἱὸς ἐπὶ πατρί, μήτηρ ἐπὶ θυγατέρα καὶ θυγάτηρ ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα, πενθερὰ ἐπὶ τὴν νύμφην αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφη ἐπὶ τὴν πενθεράν.

verses.english: He also said to the crowds, "When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say at once, 'A shower is coming', and so it happens.
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὅταν ἴδητε τὴν νεφέλην ἀνατέλλουσαν ἐπὶ δυσμῶν, εὐθέως λέγετε ὅτι Ὄμβρος ἔρχεται, καὶ γίνεται οὕτως·

verses.english: And when you see the south wind blowing, you say, 'There will be scorching heat', and it happens.
verses.greek: καὶ ὅταν νότον πνέοντα, λέγετε ὅτι Καύσων ἔσται, καὶ γίνεται.

verses.english: Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of heaven and earth, but why do you not know how to interpret the present time?
verses.greek: ὑποκριταί, τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν, τὸν καιρὸν δὲ τοῦτον πῶς οὐκ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν;

verses.english: And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?
verses.greek: Τί δὲ καὶ ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν οὐ κρίνετε τὸ δίκαιον;

verses.english: As you go with your accuser before a magistrate, make an effort on the way to settle with him, so that he does not drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
verses.greek: ὡς γὰρ ὑπάγεις μετὰ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου σου ἐπ’ ἄρχοντα, ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ δὸς ἐργασίαν ἀπηλλάχθαι ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, μήποτε κατασύρῃ σε πρὸς τὸν κριτήν, καὶ ὁ κριτὴς παραδώσει σε τῷ πράκτορι, καὶ ὁ πράκτωρ σε βαλεῖ εἰς φυλακήν.

verses.english: I tell you, you will not get out of there until you have paid the very last copper."
verses.greek: λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως καὶ τὸ ἔσχατον λεπτὸν ἀποδῷς.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.28.1–8 follows the passage closely: the leaven of the Pharisees, nothing hidden that will not be known, "do not fear those who can only kill", "fear him who after killing has power to cast into Gehenna", which he says means the Creator, acknowledging and denying "before God", the sin against the holy spirit, and the spirit teaching in that hour. Epiphanius, sch. 29–30 quotes 12:4–5 in Greek ("to cast into Gehenna", βαλεῖν εἰς γέενναν) and states that the text had "before God" where canonical Luke has "before the angels of God". Both are printed. NA27 cites Marcion for the omission of "the angels of" in both 12:8 and 12:9.

Epiphanius, sch. 29: the text "did not have 'Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? And not one of them is forgotten before God'". In his refutation he presses Marcion with it: "nothing happens without God, even if you take away what is about the sparrows". 12:7 ("the hairs of your head are all numbered… you are of more value than many sparrows") depends on 12:6, and Tertullian, who goes straight from 12:5 to 12:8, does not cite it, though it would have suited his argument for the Creator's care. It is classed "unattested, probably absent".

Tertullian, Marc. 4.28.9–11. He sets Jesus' refusal to divide the inheritance ("Who made me a judge over you?") against Moses, who was rejected with the same words when he tried to make peace between two Hebrews (Exod 2:14), and quotes God's words to the rich man: "Fool, this night they will demand your soul; and what you have prepared, whose will it be?" 12:15, 12:17–18 and 12:21 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.29.1–5 recasts the passage rhetorically, but the lilies "neither weave nor spin" (D: "neither spin nor weave"), not "toil nor spin" as in canonical Luke, and he quotes "Seek the kingdom of God". Epiphanius, sch. 31–34 states that the text lacked "God clothes the grass" (12:28a), quotes 12:30b and 12:31 ("the kingdom of God"), and states that 12:32 read "the Father", not "your Father". The text printed therefore goes from Solomon not clothed like the lilies to "How much more you, you of little faith!" 12:25–26 and 12:29 are not cited and are printed in grey. 12:33–34 ("sell your possessions") form a paragraph that no witness cites and are not printed.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.29.6–11 reads the girded loins and burning lamps as the life of faith, asks from whose wedding the master returns, and says that the thief is the devil, while the son of man comes as judge. He takes Peter's question to mean that the parable of the stewards is addressed to those "who would preside over the churches". Epiphanius, sch. 35 states that the master comes "in the evening watch", as in D and the Old Latin, not "in the second or third watch"; that reading is printed. Sch. 36 quotes 12:46. Tertullian reports that the Marcionites read "cut him in pieces" as mere separation (4.29.10); that is their reception, and the text has διχοτομήσει.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.29.12–16 quotes "I came to cast fire on the earth", "Do you think I came to bring peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but division", and the division of father and son, mother and daughter (Micah 7:6). He charges that "sword" is what is written and that Marcion changed it, but "sword" is Matthew's word (Matt 10:34); every Greek manuscript of Luke reads "division". He paraphrases 12:56 with "heaven and earth", the order of 𝔓45, 𝔓75 and D, which is printed. Epiphanius, sch. 37 quotes 12:58b. 12:50, 12:52 and 12:54–55 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Interpretation. In this text the Father knows what the disciples need, gives them the kingdom, and the holy spirit teaches them what to say. Tertullian's argument through 4.28–4.29 is that the God who provides food and clothing and judges is one and the same. The text as attested does not separate a providing God from a judging one. It speaks of the Father who gives and of the one to be feared who can cast into Gehenna (12:5), and Tertullian identifies them. Whether the community behind the text read the two as one cannot be decided from the witnesses.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 11
chapters.preamble: Healing on the sabbath, and the kingdom compared. Jesus heals a woman bent over for eighteen years, "a daughter of Abraham whom Satan bound", and answers the leader of the synagogue with the ox or donkey watered on the sabbath. He compares the kingdom of God to a mustard seed sown in a garden and to leaven. Those who come to the door once the master has shut it will be told "I do not know where you come from", and will weep "when you see all the righteous in the kingdom of God, and yourselves held outside". In this text it is "the righteous", not Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and the prophets, whom they see in the kingdom. Two blocks of canonical Luke are not in this text, by Epiphanius' statement. The first is the Galileans killed by Pilate, the tower of Siloam and the barren fig tree (13:1–9). The second is the many coming from east and west, the warning about Herod and the lament over Jerusalem (13:29–35).

verses.english: Now he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
verses.greek: Ἦν δὲ διδάσκων ἐν μιᾷ τῶν συναγωγῶν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν.

verses.english: And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of weakness for eighteen years; she was bent over and could not straighten herself at all.
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ πνεῦμα ἔχουσα ἀσθενείας ἔτη δεκαοκτώ, καὶ ἦν συγκύπτουσα καὶ μὴ δυναμένη ἀνακύψαι εἰς τὸ παντελές.

verses.english: When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said to her, "Woman, you are freed from your weakness."
verses.greek: ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὴν ὁ Ἰησοῦς προσεφώνησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Γύναι, ἀπολέλυσαι τῆς ἀσθενείας σου,

verses.english: And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and glorified God.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτῇ τὰς χεῖρας· καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνωρθώθη, καὶ ἐδόξαζεν τὸν θεόν.

verses.english: But the leader of the synagogue, indignant that Jesus had healed on the sabbath, said to the crowd, "There are six days on which work ought to be done; come on those days and be healed, and not on the sabbath day."
verses.greek: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος, ἀγανακτῶν ὅτι τῷ σαββάτῳ ἐθεράπευσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἔλεγεν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὅτι Ἓξ ἡμέραι εἰσὶν ἐν αἷς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι· ἐν αὐταῖς οὖν ἐρχόμενοι θεραπεύεσθε καὶ μὴ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου.

verses.english: The Lord answered him, "Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the sabbath untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to water it?
verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος καὶ εἶπεν· Ὑποκριταί, ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τῷ σαββάτῳ οὐ λύει τὸν βοῦν αὐτοῦ ἢ τὸν ὄνον ἀπὸ τῆς φάτνης καὶ ἀπαγαγὼν ποτίζει;

verses.english: And this woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan bound for eighteen long years, ought she not to be set free from this bond on the sabbath day?"
verses.greek: ταύτην δὲ θυγατέρα Ἀβραὰμ οὖσαν, ἣν ἔδησεν ὁ Σατανᾶς ἰδοὺ δέκα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἔτη, οὐκ ἔδει λυθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσμοῦ τούτου τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;

verses.english: As he said this, all his opponents were put to shame, and the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things he was doing.
verses.greek: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντος αὐτοῦ κατῃσχύνοντο πάντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι αὐτῷ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἔχαιρεν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐνδόξοις τοῖς γινομένοις ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: He said therefore, "What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν οὖν· Τίνι ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τίνι ὁμοιώσω αὐτήν;

verses.english: It is like a grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky made nests in its branches."
verses.greek: ὁμοία ἐστὶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔβαλεν εἰς κῆπον ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ ηὔξησεν καὶ ἐγένετο εἰς δένδρον, καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατεσκήνωσεν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And again he said, "To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
verses.greek: Καὶ πάλιν εἶπεν· Τίνι ὁμοιώσω τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ;

verses.english: It is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened."
verses.greek: ὁμοία ἐστὶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.

verses.english: Someone said to him, "Lord, will those who are saved be few?" He said to them,
verses.greek: εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ ὀλίγοι οἱ σῳζόμενοι; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς·

verses.english: "Strive to enter through the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able.
verses.greek: Ἀγωνίζεσθε εἰσελθεῖν διὰ τῆς στενῆς θύρας, ὅτι πολλοί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ζητήσουσιν εἰσελθεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἰσχύσουσιν,

verses.english: Once the master of the house has risen and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, 'Lord, open to us', he will answer you, 'I do not know where you come from.'
verses.greek: ἀφ’ οὗ ἂν ἐγερθῇ ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης καὶ ἀποκλείσῃ τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἄρξησθε ἔξω ἑστάναι καὶ κρούειν τὴν θύραν λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν· καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ἐρεῖ ὑμῖν· Οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς πόθεν ἐστέ.

verses.english: Then you will begin to say, 'We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.'
verses.greek: τότε ἄρξεσθε λέγειν· Ἐφάγομεν ἐνώπιόν σου καὶ ἐπίομεν, καὶ ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις ἡμῶν ἐδίδαξας·

verses.english: But he will say to you, 'I do not know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of injustice!'
verses.greek: καὶ ἐρεῖ λέγων ὑμῖν· Οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς πόθεν ἐστέ· ἀπόστητε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, πάντες ἐργάται ἀδικίας.

verses.english: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see all the righteous in the kingdom of God, and yourselves held outside.
verses.greek: ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων, ὅταν ὄψησθε πάντας τοὺς δικαίους ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὑμᾶς δὲ κρατουμένους ἔξω.

notes.explanation: Epiphanius, sch. 38: the text "was cut off" from "some came and told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices", through the eighteen killed by the tower in Siloam and "unless you repent", to the parable of the fig tree and the vinedresser's "I will dig and put on manure; and if it does not bear fruit, cut it down". Tertullian goes from 12:59 to the sabbath healing (13:14). The charge of cutting is Epiphanius'. What it reports as content is that the passage was not in the text.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.30.1: asked again about a healing on the sabbath, Christ answers "Does not each of you on the sabbaths untie his donkey or ox from the manger and lead it to drink?" Tertullian concludes that he "confirmed the law, not dissolved it", since the law permits work done to save a life. Epiphanius, sch. 39 quotes 13:16: "this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound". 13:10–13 and 13:17 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.30.1–3 quotes the mustard seed "which a man took and sowed in his garden" and asks whose garden the world is. Of the leaven he says mockingly that the kingdom of the other God might be compared to leaven because the Creator prefers unleavened bread. 13:18 is not cited and is printed in grey. 13:22, a travel notice, forms a paragraph that no witness cites and is not printed.

notes.term: The shut door and "all the righteous" (13:23–28)
notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.30.4–6: the master of the house rises and shuts the door; to those knocking he answers "I do not know where you are from"; to those who say they ate and drank before him and that he taught in their streets, "Depart from me, all workers of iniquity. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth", "when they see the righteous entering the kingdom of God and themselves held outside". Epiphanius, sch. 40 confirms the wording: the text had "all the righteous" where canonical Luke has "Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets", and "held" (κρατουμένους) outside. 13:23–24 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Epiphanius, sch. 41 names every saying of 13:29–35 as absent: people coming from east and west to recline in the kingdom, "the last will be first", the Pharisees' warning about Herod, the answer to "that fox", "no prophet can perish outside Jerusalem", and the lament "Jerusalem, Jerusalem" with "you will not see me until you say, Blessed…". Tertullian goes from 13:28 to 14:12.

Interpretation. In the attested text those seen in the kingdom are "all the righteous", not the patriarchs and prophets by name, while the woman healed on the sabbath is still "a daughter of Abraham" (13:16). The text therefore does not cut the tie to Abraham. It describes the kingdom by righteousness, not by descent. The leader of the Jerusalem community was remembered as James "the Just" (Gospel of Thomas 12; Carriers of Living Water §3.1). Whether "the righteous" in this saying reflects that usage cannot be shown from the witnesses. The readings themselves are attested by two witnesses; why canonical Luke has the patriarchs instead (as Matt 8:11 does) they do not say.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 12
chapters.preamble: Whom to invite. Jesus tells his host not to invite those who can repay, but the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind, for he will be repaid at the resurrection. He tells the parable of a man who gave a great banquet: the invited guests excuse themselves with a field, five yoke of oxen and a marriage, and the master, angry, has his servant bring in the poor from the streets and then from the roads and hedges. Tertullian reads the parable as the Creator's long history of inviting Israel through the prophets and then calling the nations (Marc. 4.31). The healing on the sabbath and the places at table (14:1–11), and the sayings on the cost of discipleship (14:25–35), are not cited by any witness and are not printed.

verses.english: He said also to the man who had invited him, "When you give a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbours, in case they invite you in return and you are repaid.
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τῷ κεκληκότι αὐτόν· Ὅταν ποιῇς ἄριστον ἢ δεῖπνον, μὴ φώνει τοὺς φίλους σου μηδὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου μηδὲ τοὺς συγγενεῖς σου μηδὲ γείτονας πλουσίους, μήποτε καὶ αὐτοὶ ἀντικαλέσωσίν σε καὶ γένηται ἀνταπόδομά σοι.

verses.english: But when you give a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind;
verses.greek: ἀλλ’ ὅταν δοχὴν ποιῇς, κάλει πτωχούς, ἀναπείρους, χωλούς, τυφλούς·

verses.english: and you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."
verses.greek: καὶ μακάριος ἔσῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνταποδοῦναί σοι, ἀνταποδοθήσεται γάρ σοι ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῶν δικαίων.

verses.english: When one of those at table with him heard this, he said to him, "Blessed is anyone who will eat bread in the kingdom of God!"
verses.greek: Ἀκούσας δέ τις τῶν συνανακειμένων ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακάριος ὅστις φάγεται ἄρτον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: But he said to him, "A man once gave a great banquet and invited many.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπός τις ἐποίει δεῖπνον μέγα, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν πολλούς,

verses.english: At the hour of the banquet he sent his servant to say to those who had been invited, 'Come, for everything is now ready.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ δείπνου εἰπεῖν τοῖς κεκλημένοις· Ἔρχεσθε, ὅτι ἤδη ἕτοιμά ἐστιν.

verses.english: But they all alike began to make excuses. The first said to him, 'I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it; please have me excused.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀπὸ μιᾶς πάντες παραιτεῖσθαι. ὁ πρῶτος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀγρὸν ἠγόρασα καὶ ἔχω ἀνάγκην ἐξελθὼν ἰδεῖν αὐτόν· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.

verses.english: Another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out; please have me excused.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν· Ζεύγη βοῶν ἠγόρασα πέντε καὶ πορεύομαι δοκιμάσαι αὐτά· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.

verses.english: Another said, 'I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν· Γυναῖκα ἔγημα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὐ δύναμαι ἐλθεῖν.

verses.english: So the servant came and reported this to his master. Then the master of the house, in anger, said to his servant, 'Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the town, and bring in here the poor and the crippled and the blind and the lame.'
verses.greek: καὶ παραγενόμενος ὁ δοῦλος ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ κυρίῳ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα. τότε ὀργισθεὶς ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἶπεν τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ· Ἔξελθε ταχέως εἰς τὰς πλατείας καὶ ῥύμας τῆς πόλεως, καὶ τοὺς πτωχοὺς καὶ ἀναπείρους καὶ τυφλοὺς καὶ χωλοὺς εἰσάγαγε ὧδε.

verses.english: And the servant said, 'Master, what you commanded has been done, and there is still room.'
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ δοῦλος· Κύριε, γέγονεν ὃ ἐπέταξας, καὶ ἔτι τόπος ἐστίν.

verses.english: Then the master said to the servant, 'Go out into the roads and hedgerows, and compel people to come in, so that my house may be filled.
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος πρὸς τὸν δοῦλον· Ἔξελθε εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς καὶ φραγμοὺς καὶ ἀνάγκασον εἰσελθεῖν, ἵνα γεμισθῇ μου ὁ οἶκος·

verses.english: For I tell you, none of those men who were invited will taste my banquet.'"
verses.greek: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων τῶν κεκλημένων γεύσεταί μου τοῦ δείπνου.

notes.explanation: The healing of a man with dropsy on the sabbath and the advice to take the lowest place at table are not cited by Tertullian or Epiphanius. They form two NA27 paragraphs with no attested verse, and their absence is undetermined. Tertullian had just argued the sabbath question at 13:15 (4.30.1), and a second sabbath healing would have added nothing new to his case.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.31.1 sets the command to invite those who cannot repay beside Isaiah 58:7 ("break your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house"). He notes that Christ promises the repayment "in the resurrection". 14:13 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.31.1–8 follows the parable step by step: a man made a dinner and invited many, sent to those invited, they excused themselves ("I have bought a field, I have bought oxen, I have married a wife"), the householder was moved and sent into the streets and lanes, then, with room to spare, into the roads and hedges. He remarks that Marcion denies that his God is ever moved to anger. He reads the excuses as Israel refusing the prophets (Jer 7:23–26) and the second gathering as the call of the nations (Deut 32:20–21). 14:15 is not cited; it is printed in grey because the parable answers it.

Hating father and mother, carrying one's cross, counting the cost of a tower or a war, and the salt that loses its taste. No witness cites any of these verses as part of the text, and they are not printed. The previous version printed 14:26 and 14:33.

Interpretation. In the attested text the host's duty is to invite those who cannot repay, and the parable ends with the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame brought in, and then strangers from the roads. Tertullian reads this as the Creator's own pattern (Isaiah 58). The same preference for the poor over the rich appears in the Epistle of James (Jas 2:1–7, the rich man and the poor man in the assembly).

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 13
chapters.preamble: The lost found. Tax collectors and sinners come to listen to Jesus, and the Pharisees complain that he eats with them. He answers with two parables: a man who leaves the ninety-nine sheep to look for the one that is lost, and a woman who sweeps the house for a lost coin. Each rejoices with friends at finding it, and so there is joy over one sinner who repents. Tertullian's point is that only the one who owned what was lost could look for it (Marc. 4.32). The parable of the two sons (15:11–32) is not in this text: Epiphanius states that "the whole parable of the two sons" was absent.

verses.english: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming near to listen to him.
verses.greek: Ἦσαν δὲ αὐτῷ ἐγγίζοντες πάντες οἱ τελῶναι καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And the Pharisees and the scribes were grumbling, saying, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them."
verses.greek: καὶ διεγόγγυζον οἵ τε Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ἁμαρτωλοὺς προσδέχεται καὶ συνεσθίει αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: So he told them this parable:
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγων·

verses.english: "Which of you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost until he finds it?
verses.greek: Τίς ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ὑμῶν ἔχων ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ ἀπολέσας ἐξ αὐτῶν ἓν οὐ καταλείπει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ καὶ πορεύεται ἐπὶ τὸ ἀπολωλὸς ἕως εὕρῃ αὐτό;

verses.english: And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
verses.greek: καὶ εὑρὼν ἐπιτίθησιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους αὐτοῦ χαίρων,

verses.english: And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbours, saying to them, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον συγκαλεῖ τοὺς φίλους καὶ τοὺς γείτονας, λέγων αὐτοῖς· Συγχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὸ πρόβατόν μου τὸ ἀπολωλός.

verses.english: I tell you, just so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
verses.greek: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως χαρὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἔσται ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι ἢ ἐπὶ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα δικαίοις οἵτινες οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν μετανοίας.

verses.english: Or what woman, having ten silver coins, if she loses one coin, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?
verses.greek: Ἢ τίς γυνὴ δραχμὰς ἔχουσα δέκα, ἐὰν ἀπολέσῃ δραχμὴν μίαν, οὐχὶ ἅπτει λύχνον καὶ σαροῖ τὴν οἰκίαν καὶ ζητεῖ ἐπιμελῶς ἕως οὗ εὕρῃ;

verses.english: And when she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbours, saying, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found the coin that I had lost.'
verses.greek: καὶ εὑροῦσα συγκαλεῖ τὰς φίλας καὶ γείτονας λέγουσα· Συγχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα.

verses.english: Just so, I tell you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
verses.greek: οὕτως, λέγω ὑμῖν, γίνεται χαρὰ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.32.1–2: "Who looks for the lost sheep and the lost coin? Surely the one who lost them. And who lost them? The one who had them. And who had them? The one whose they were." Since man belongs to the Creator, he concludes, the joy over the sinner's repentance is the Creator's, "who said long ago that he prefers the repentance of a sinner to his death" (Ezek 18:23). 15:1–2 are not cited. They are printed in grey because the parables answer them.

Epiphanius, sch. 42: "again he cut out the whole parable of the two sons, the one who took his share of the property and spent it wastefully, and the other". Tertullian, after the coin, goes to the two masters (16:13). The parable would have served him: its father receives back a son who left his house, the Creator's own image of repentance. Two witnesses agree that it was not there. "Cut out" is Epiphanius' charge; the content of his statement is that the parable was absent.

Interpretation. Tertullian's argument, "no one looks for what he never had", is aimed at the Marcionite claim that a stranger God redeems humans who were not his. The attested parables themselves say only that the one who lost the sheep or coin is the one who looks for it and rejoices. The Prodigal Son, which carries the theme of return most fully in canonical Luke, is absent here; in this text the theme rests on the two short parables alone.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 14
chapters.preamble: Mammon, the law and the rich man. A steward about to be dismissed reduces his master's debtors' bills, and Jesus tells his disciples to make friends by the mammon of injustice: no one can serve God and mammon. The Pharisees, lovers of money, ridicule him; he answers that God knows their hearts. "The law and the prophets were until John; since then the kingdom of God is proclaimed." In this text the next saying is about his own words: "it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of my words to fall" (Tertullian, Marc. 4.33.9). There follow the saying on divorce, which Tertullian links to John's rebuke of Herod, and the rich man and Lazarus. The rich man asks for a messenger to his brothers and is told: "They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them."

verses.english: He also said to the disciples, "There was a rich man who had a steward, and charges were brought to him that this man was squandering his property.
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς· Ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν πλούσιος ὃς εἶχεν οἰκονόμον, καὶ οὗτος διεβλήθη αὐτῷ ὡς διασκορπίζων τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: So he called him and said to him, 'What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward.'
verses.greek: καὶ φωνήσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί τοῦτο ἀκούω περὶ σοῦ; ἀπόδος τὸν λόγον τῆς οἰκονομίας σου, οὐ γὰρ δύνῃ ἔτι οἰκονομεῖν.

verses.english: And the steward said to himself, 'What shall I do, since my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to dig, and I am ashamed to beg.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὁ οἰκονόμος· Τί ποιήσω ὅτι ὁ κύριός μου ἀφαιρεῖται τὴν οἰκονομίαν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ; σκάπτειν οὐκ ἰσχύω, ἐπαιτεῖν αἰσχύνομαι·

verses.english: I have decided what to do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship, people will receive me into their houses.'
verses.greek: ἔγνων τί ποιήσω, ἵνα ὅταν μετασταθῶ ἐκ τῆς οἰκονομίας δέξωνταί με εἰς τοὺς οἴκους ἑαυτῶν.

verses.english: So, summoning his master's debtors one by one, he said to the first, 'How much do you owe my master?'
verses.greek: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα ἕκαστον τῶν χρεοφειλετῶν τοῦ κυρίου ἑαυτοῦ ἔλεγεν τῷ πρώτῳ· Πόσον ὀφείλεις τῷ κυρίῳ μου;

verses.english: He said, 'A hundred measures of oil.' He said to him, 'Take your bill, sit down quickly and write fifty.'
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἑκατὸν βάτους ἐλαίου· ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ καθίσας ταχέως γράψον πεντήκοντα.

verses.english: Then he said to another, 'And how much do you owe?' He said, 'A hundred measures of wheat.' He said to him, 'Take your bill and write eighty.'
verses.greek: ἔπειτα ἑτέρῳ εἶπεν· Σὺ δὲ πόσον ὀφείλεις; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἑκατὸν κόρους σίτου· λέγει αὐτῷ· Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ γράψον ὀγδοήκοντα.

verses.english: And the master praised the dishonest steward for acting shrewdly; for the sons of this age are shrewder in dealing with their own generation than the sons of light.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπῄνεσεν ὁ κύριος τὸν οἰκονόμον τῆς ἀδικίας ὅτι φρονίμως ἐποίησεν· ὅτι οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου φρονιμώτεροι ὑπὲρ τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ φωτὸς εἰς τὴν γενεὰν τὴν ἑαυτῶν εἰσιν.

verses.english: And I tell you, make friends for yourselves by means of the mammon of injustice, so that when it fails they may receive you into the eternal dwellings.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, ἑαυτοῖς ποιήσατε φίλους ἐκ τοῦ μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας, ἵνα ὅταν ἐκλίπῃ δέξωνται ὑμᾶς εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους σκηνάς.

verses.english: Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much, and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.
verses.greek: Ὁ πιστὸς ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ καὶ ἐν πολλῷ πιστός ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ ἄδικος καὶ ἐν πολλῷ ἄδικός ἐστιν.

verses.english: If then you have not been faithful in the unjust mammon, who will entrust to you the true riches?
verses.greek: εἰ οὖν ἐν τῷ ἀδίκῳ μαμωνᾷ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ἀληθινὸν τίς ὑμῖν πιστεύσει;

verses.english: And if you have not been faithful in what belongs to another, who will give you what is mine?
verses.greek: καὶ εἰ ἐν τῷ ἀλλοτρίῳ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ἐμὸν τίς ὑμῖν δώσει;

verses.english: No servant can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon."
verses.greek: οὐδεὶς οἰκέτης δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.

verses.english: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all this, and they ridiculed him.
verses.greek: Ἤκουον δὲ ταῦτα πάντα οἱ Φαρισαῖοι φιλάργυροι ὑπάρχοντες, καὶ ἐξεμυκτήριζον αὐτόν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "You are those who justify yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts; for what is exalted among people is an abomination before God.
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ δικαιοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁ δὲ θεὸς γινώσκει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν· ὅτι τὸ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὑψηλὸν βδέλυγμα ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: The law and the prophets were until John; since then the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone forces his way into it.
verses.greek: Ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται μέχρι Ἰωάννου· ἀπὸ τότε ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγελίζεται καὶ πᾶς εἰς αὐτὴν βιάζεται.

verses.english: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of my words to fall.
verses.greek: Εὐκοπώτερον δέ ἐστιν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν παρελθεῖν ἢ τῶν λόγων μου μίαν κεραίαν πεσεῖν.

verses.english: Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and he who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.
verses.greek: Πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμῶν ἑτέραν μοιχεύει, καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς γαμῶν μοιχεύει.

verses.english: There was a rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen and feasted splendidly every day.
verses.greek: Ἄνθρωπος δέ τις ἦν πλούσιος, καὶ ἐνεδιδύσκετο πορφύραν καὶ βύσσον εὐφραινόμενος καθ’ ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς.

verses.english: And at his gate lay a poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores,
verses.greek: πτωχὸς δέ τις ὀνόματι Λάζαρος ἐβέβλητο πρὸς τὸν πυλῶνα αὐτοῦ εἱλκωμένος

verses.english: longing to be fed with what fell from the rich man's table; and even the dogs came and licked his sores.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπιθυμῶν χορτασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τοῦ πλουσίου· ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ κύνες ἐρχόμενοι ἐπέλειχον τὰ ἕλκη αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: The poor man died and was carried by the angels to Abraham's bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
verses.greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πτωχὸν καὶ ἀπενεχθῆναι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἰς τὸν κόλπον Ἀβραάμ· ἀπέθανεν δὲ καὶ ὁ πλούσιος καὶ ἐτάφη.

verses.english: And in Hades, being in torment, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham far off and Lazarus in his bosom.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, ὑπάρχων ἐν βασάνοις, ὁρᾷ Ἀβραὰμ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν καὶ Λάζαρον ἐν τῷ κόλπῳ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And he called out, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am in anguish in this flame.'
verses.greek: καὶ αὐτὸς φωνήσας εἶπεν· Πάτερ Ἀβραάμ, ἐλέησόν με καὶ πέμψον Λάζαρον ἵνα βάψῃ τὸ ἄκρον τοῦ δακτύλου αὐτοῦ ὕδατος καὶ καταψύξῃ τὴν γλῶσσάν μου, ὅτι ὀδυνῶμαι ἐν τῇ φλογὶ ταύτῃ.

verses.english: But Abraham said, 'Child, remember that you received your good things in your lifetime, and Lazarus likewise bad things; but now he is comforted here, and you are in anguish.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ἀβραάμ· Τέκνον, μνήσθητι ὅτι ἀπέλαβες τὰ ἀγαθά σου ἐν τῇ ζωῇ σου, καὶ Λάζαρος ὁμοίως τὰ κακά· νῦν δὲ ὧδε παρακαλεῖται σὺ δὲ ὀδυνᾶσαι.

verses.english: And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, so that those who would pass from here to you cannot, and none may cross from there to us.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τούτοις μεταξὺ ἡμῶν καὶ ὑμῶν χάσμα μέγα ἐστήρικται, ὅπως οἱ θέλοντες διαβῆναι ἔνθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς μὴ δύνωνται, μηδὲ ἐκεῖθεν πρὸς ἡμᾶς διαπερῶσιν.

verses.english: And he said, 'Then I beg you, father, to send him to my father's house,
verses.greek: εἶπεν δέ· Ἐρωτῶ σε οὖν, πάτερ, ἵνα πέμψῃς αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου,

verses.english: for I have five brothers, so that he may warn them, lest they also come into this place of torment.'
verses.greek: ἔχω γὰρ πέντε ἀδελφούς, ὅπως διαμαρτύρηται αὐτοῖς, ἵνα μὴ καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔλθωσιν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦτον τῆς βασάνου.

verses.english: But Abraham said, 'They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them.'
verses.greek: λέγει δὲ Ἀβραάμ· Ἔχουσι Μωϋσέα καὶ τοὺς προφήτας· ἀκουσάτωσαν αὐτῶν.

verses.english: And he said, 'No, father Abraham; but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.'
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Οὐχί, πάτερ Ἀβραάμ, ἀλλ’ ἐάν τις ἀπὸ νεκρῶν πορευθῇ πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετανοήσουσιν.

verses.english: He said to him, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be convinced if someone rises from the dead.'"
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Εἰ Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἀκούουσιν, οὐδ’ ἐάν τις ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ πεισθήσονται.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.33.1 summarizes the parable: the servant removed from his post relieves his master's debtors by reducing their bonds, to provide for himself. He then quotes "And I tell you, make friends for yourselves of the mammon of injustice" and explains mammon as money. The previous version marked 16:1–8 as "conflicting evidence"; the parable is attested. 16:1, 16:3 and 16:8 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.33.1–6. "You cannot serve God and mammon": he argues that the two masters are God and money, not the Creator and another God, so that one God is named. He quotes 16:11–12 in the form "who will give you what is mine?", which he reads as Christ's own. That reading, "mine" for "your own", is printed; it is also in three Old Latin manuscripts. 16:10 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Epiphanius, sch. 43 and Tertullian 4.33.7 quote "The law and the prophets were until John". On 16:17 Tertullian writes: "Let heaven and earth pass away sooner, as the law and the prophets also did, than one stroke of the words of the Lord", and "he added that the elements would pass more easily than his words". NA27 cites this as Marcion's reading (τῶν λόγων μου, "of my words"). Roth rates it probable only, allowing for the influence of 21:33 ("my words will not pass away") and Isa 40:8. The audit prints it, for a reason in Tertullian's argument. He sets out to show that Christ fulfilled the law and did not destroy it. Canonical Luke's "one stroke of the law" would have proved that directly, and he does not use it. He had to deal with a text in which what does not pass away is Christ's word, and the law and the prophets are what has come to an end with John.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.34.1–9 quotes the saying twice. He argues that it forbids divorce for the purpose of remarriage and so agrees with Moses, and he connects it with John's rebuke of Herod, who married his brother's wife. He reports that the Marcionites refused baptism to the married unless they renounced marriage (4.34.5); that is their practice, not the text.

Three witnesses attest the parable. Epiphanius, sch. 44–46: Lazarus carried by the angels to Abraham's bosom, "now he is comforted here", "they have Moses and the prophets, let them listen to them". Tertullian, Marc. 4.34.10–17: the rich man in torment in Hades, the great chasm, Lazarus in the bosom of Abraham. The Dialogue of Adamantius (76–78) quotes the whole parable, but Roth rates its wording probable only. The singular "in his bosom" (16:23), with Tertullian, the Dialogue, D and the Old Latin, is printed. 16:21, 16:24, 16:27–28 and 16:30 rest on the Dialogue alone. They are printed as part of the attested parable, in the NA27 wording.

Reception and interpretation. The Marcionite reading, which Tertullian reports, was that both torment and rest "in the underworld" are the Creator's reward for those who obey the law and the prophets, while Christ's heaven is elsewhere (4.34.11). Tertullian replies that the text itself distinguishes Abraham's bosom from Hades by a great chasm, and he calls Abraham's bosom a temporary place of rest for the souls of the righteous until the resurrection (4.34.13). The attested text describes a state after death that follows at once on the life lived: the poor man is carried to Abraham, the rich man is in torment, and the two are separated. It does not speak of a later resurrection. To the request for a messenger from the dead, the parable answers with "Moses and the prophets".

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 15
chapters.preamble: Stumbling, forgiveness, the ten lepers, and the days of the son of man. Jesus warns against causing "one of these little ones" to stumble and tells his disciples to forgive a brother seven times a day. Passing between Samaria and Galilee, he meets ten lepers. In this text he recalls that in Elisha's time only Naaman the Syrian was cleansed (Luke 4:27, placed here by both witnesses) and sends them to show themselves to the priests. They are cleansed on the way, and the one who turns back to give glory to God is a Samaritan: "your faith has saved you". Asked when the kingdom comes, he says that it does not come with observation, "for behold, the kingdom of God is within you". He speaks of the days of Noah and of Lot, and says: "Remember Lot's wife." Faith like a mustard seed and the unworthy servants (17:5–10) are not printed.

verses.english: He said to his disciples, "It is impossible that causes of stumbling should not come, but woe to the one through whom they come!
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Ἀνένδεκτόν ἐστιν τοῦ τὰ σκάνδαλα μὴ ἐλθεῖν, πλὴν οὐαὶ δι’ οὗ ἔρχεται·

verses.english: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
verses.greek: λυσιτελεῖ αὐτῷ εἰ λίθος μυλικὸς περίκειται περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔρριπται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἢ ἵνα σκανδαλίσῃ τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ἕνα.

verses.english: Take heed to yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.
verses.greek: προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς. ἐὰν ἁμάρτῃ ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἐπιτίμησον αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐὰν μετανοήσῃ ἄφες αὐτῷ·

verses.english: And if he sins against you seven times in the day, and turns to you seven times, saying, 'I repent', you shall forgive him."
verses.greek: καὶ ἐὰν ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ καὶ ἑπτάκις ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς σὲ λέγων· Μετανοῶ, ἀφήσεις αὐτῷ.

verses.english: On the way to Jerusalem he was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ αὐτὸς διήρχετο διὰ μέσον Σαμαρείας καὶ Γαλιλαίας.

verses.english: As he entered a village, ten lepers met him.
verses.greek: καὶ εἰσερχομένου αὐτοῦ εἴς τινα κώμην ἀπήντησαν αὐτῷ δέκα λεπροὶ ἄνδρες.

verses.english: "There were many lepers in Israel in the days of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed except Neeman the Syrian."
verses.greek: πολλοὶ λεπροὶ ἦσαν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ ἐν ἡμέραις Ἐλισαίου τοῦ προφήτου, καὶ οὐδεὶς αὐτῶν ἐκαθαρίσθη εἰ μὴ Νεεμὰν ὁ Σύρος.

verses.english: When he saw them he said to them, "Go and show yourselves to the priests." And as they went, they were cleansed.
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἐπιδείξατε ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν. καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτοὺς ἐκαθαρίσθησαν.

verses.english: Then one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, praising God with a loud voice;
verses.greek: εἷς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν, ἰδὼν ὅτι ἰάθη, ὑπέστρεψεν μετὰ φωνῆς μεγάλης δοξάζων τὸν θεόν,

verses.english: and he fell on his face at his feet, giving him thanks. And he was a Samaritan.
verses.greek: καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ εὐχαριστῶν αὐτῷ· καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Σαμαρίτης.

verses.english: Then Jesus said, "Were not ten cleansed? Where are the nine?
verses.greek: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Οὐχὶ οἱ δέκα ἐκαθαρίσθησαν; οἱ δὲ ἐννέα ποῦ;

verses.english: Was no one found to return and give glory to God except this foreigner?"
verses.greek: οὐχ εὑρέθησαν ὑποστρέψαντες δοῦναι δόξαν τῷ θεῷ εἰ μὴ ὁ ἀλλογενὴς οὗτος;

verses.english: And he said to him, "Rise and go; your faith has saved you."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀναστὰς πορεύου· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.

verses.english: Being asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, he answered them, "The kingdom of God is not coming with observation;
verses.greek: Ἐπερωτηθεὶς δὲ ὑπὸ τῶν Φαρισαίων πότε ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς καὶ εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ παρατηρήσεως,

verses.english: nor will they say, 'Look, here it is!' or 'Look, there it is!' For behold, the kingdom of God is within you."
verses.greek: οὐδὲ ἐροῦσιν· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε ἤ· Ἰδοὺ ἐκεῖ· ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἐντὸς ὑμῶν ἐστιν.

verses.english: And he said to the disciples, "Days are coming when you will long to see one of the days of the son of man, and you will not see it.
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς· Ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ὅτε ἐπιθυμήσετε μίαν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἰδεῖν καὶ οὐκ ὄψεσθε.

verses.english: And they will say to you, 'Look, there!' or 'Look, here!' Do not go out or follow them.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐροῦσιν ὑμῖν· Ἰδοὺ ἐκεῖ, ἤ· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε· μὴ ἀπέλθητε μηδὲ διώξητε.

verses.english: For as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one side to the other, so will the son of man be in his day.
verses.greek: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἀστράπτουσα ἐκ τῆς ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν εἰς τὴν ὑπ’ οὐρανὸν λάμπει, οὕτως ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
verses.greek: πρῶτον δὲ δεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης.

verses.english: Just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the son of man:
verses.greek: καὶ καθὼς ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Νῶε, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·

verses.english: they were eating, drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
verses.greek: ἤσθιον, ἔπινον, ἐγάμουν, ἐγαμίζοντο, ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, καὶ ἦλθεν ὁ κατακλυσμὸς καὶ ἀπώλεσεν πάντας.

verses.english: Likewise, as it was in the days of Lot: they were eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting and building;
verses.greek: ὁμοίως καθὼς ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Λώτ· ἤσθιον, ἔπινον, ἠγόραζον, ἐπώλουν, ἐφύτευον, ᾠκοδόμουν·

verses.english: but on the day Lot went out from Sodom, fire and sulphur rained from heaven and destroyed them all.
verses.greek: ᾗ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ἐξῆλθεν Λὼτ ἀπὸ Σοδόμων, ἔβρεξεν πῦρ καὶ θεῖον ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀπώλεσεν πάντας.

verses.english: So will it be on the day when the son of man is revealed.
verses.greek: κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ ἔσται ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκαλύπτεται.

verses.english: On that day, let the one who is on the housetop, with his goods in the house, not come down to take them away; and likewise let the one in the field not turn back.
verses.greek: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὃς ἔσται ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, μὴ καταβάτω ἆραι αὐτά, καὶ ὁ ἐν ἀγρῷ ὁμοίως μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω.

verses.english: Remember Lot's wife.
verses.greek: μνημονεύετε τῆς γυναικὸς Λώτ.

verses.english: Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses it will keep it alive.
verses.greek: ὃς ἐὰν ζητήσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ περιποιήσασθαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν, ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ ζῳογονήσει αὐτήν.

verses.english: I tell you, in that night there will be two in one bed; one will be taken and the other left.
verses.greek: λέγω ὑμῖν, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ ἔσονται δύο ἐπὶ κλίνης μιᾶς, ὁ εἷς παραλημφθήσεται καὶ ὁ ἕτερος ἀφεθήσεται·

verses.english: There will be two women grinding together; one will be taken and the other left."
verses.greek: ἔσονται δύο ἀλήθουσαι ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, ἡ μία παραλημφθήσεται ἡ δὲ ἑτέρα ἀφεθήσεται.

verses.english: And they answered him, "Where, Lord?" He said to them, "Where the body is, there the eagles will gather."
verses.greek: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ποῦ, κύριε; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅπου τὸ σῶμα, ἐκεῖ καὶ οἱ ἀετοὶ ἐπισυναχθήσονται.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.35.1–3. He takes the woe on the one who causes stumbling as a judge's threat, and compares the command to rebuke a sinning brother with Lev 19:17. He says the forgiveness "seven times" is "too little" compared with the Creator, who sets no limit. NA27 begins a new paragraph at 17:3b.

Epiphanius, sch. 47: the text lacked "say, we are unworthy servants; we have done what we ought to have done" (17:10b). NA27 cites Marcion for the omission. The rest of 17:5–10, faith like a mustard seed and the servant who serves at table before he eats, is not cited by either witness. Its two paragraphs have no attested verse, and they are not printed.

Epiphanius, sch. 48: "when the ten lepers met him"; Marcion "cut out much", had "he sent them away saying, Show yourselves to the priests", and put in "other things in place of others", saying "there were many lepers in the days of Elisha the prophet and none was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian". Tertullian, Marc. 4.35.4–11 says Christ had said this "beforehand" (praefatus est) and goes through the healing: sent to the priests, cleansed on the way "without touch and without a word", one of them a Samaritan who gave glory to God. Luke 4:27 is therefore printed here, after the meeting and before the command, and the lepers' cry for mercy (17:12b–13) is not printed. In canonical Luke 4:27 belongs to the Nazareth sermon (4:25–27), whose sayings on Elijah and Elisha this text does not have at that point (batch 1).

Reception and interpretation. Marcion, Tertullian says, presented the healing on the way as Christ outrunning the ceremonies of the law (4.35.4). Tertullian replies that the ten were healed because they obeyed the law and went to the priests (4.35.8), and that the Samaritan was sent to Jerusalem because "salvation is from the Jews" (4.35.10). The attested text has Jesus send all ten to the priests, as the law of Leviticus 14 requires, and praise the Samaritan's return to give glory to God. Naaman, cleansed by Elisha, is the precedent the text itself cites. It sets the healing within Israel's prophetic history and not against it.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.35.12–13 quotes "The kingdom of God does not come with observation, nor do they say, Look here, look there; for behold, the kingdom of God is within you". He explains "within you" as "in your hand, in your power, if you hear and do the commandment of God", and compares Deut 30:11–14 ("the word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it"). The second "Look" (ἰδού) is printed with Tertullian and the Byzantine text.

notes.term: The days of the son of man (17:22–37)
notes.explanation: Epiphanius, sch. 49 quotes 17:22. Tertullian, Marc. 4.35.14–16 cites the son of man who "must first suffer many things and be rejected" (17:25), drawing the word "rejected" from Ps 118:22 ("the stone the builders rejected"). He asks why a gentle God would compare his coming to the dark days of Noah and Lot and warn his hearers to remember Lot's wife. The other verses of the paragraph are not cited and are printed in grey. NA27 has no verse 17:36.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 16
chapters.preamble: Prayer, the commandments and the son of David. Jesus tells of a widow who wore down an unjust judge, and says that God will give justice to his chosen ones who cry to him day and night. He tells of a Pharisee and a tax collector praying in temple, and of the one who went home justified. A ruler asks what he must do to inherit eternal life. Jesus answers, "No one is good except God alone," and lists the commandments in the order "do not kill, do not commit adultery". He then tells the man: "One thing you lack: sell all that you have and give to the poor… and come, follow me." Near Jericho a blind man calls him "Jesus, son of David" and is healed. The third prediction of the passion, with its appeal to "everything written by the prophets" (18:31–33), is not in the text (Epiphanius, sch. 52).

verses.english: He told them a parable to show that they ought always to pray and not lose heart.
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν δὲ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς πρὸς τὸ δεῖν πάντοτε προσεύχεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ μὴ ἐγκακεῖν,

verses.english: He said, "In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected people.
verses.greek: λέγων· Κριτής τις ἦν ἔν τινι πόλει τὸν θεὸν μὴ φοβούμενος καὶ ἄνθρωπον μὴ ἐντρεπόμενος.

verses.english: And there was a widow in that town who kept coming to him and saying, 'Give me justice against my adversary.'
verses.greek: χήρα δὲ ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσα· Ἐκδίκησόν με ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου μου.

verses.english: For a while he refused, but afterwards he said to himself, 'Though I neither fear God nor respect people,
verses.greek: καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἐπὶ χρόνον, μετὰ ταῦτα δὲ εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ· Εἰ καὶ τὸν θεὸν οὐ φοβοῦμαι οὐδὲ ἄνθρωπον ἐντρέπομαι,

verses.english: yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will give her justice, so that she does not wear me out by her continual coming.'"
verses.greek: διά γε τὸ παρέχειν μοι κόπον τὴν χήραν ταύτην ἐκδικήσω αὐτήν ἵνα μὴ εἰς τέλος ἐρχομένη ὑπωπιάζῃ με.
