verses.english: And the Lord said, "Hear what the unjust judge says.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος· Ἀκούσατε τί ὁ κριτὴς τῆς ἀδικίας λέγει·

verses.english: And will not God give justice to his chosen ones, who cry to him day and night? Will he delay long over them?
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ θεὸς οὐ μὴ ποιήσῃ τὴν ἐκδίκησιν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ τῶν βοώντων αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, καὶ μακροθυμεῖ ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς;

verses.english: I tell you, he will give them justice quickly. Nevertheless, when the son of man comes, will he find faith on earth?"
verses.greek: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ποιήσει τὴν ἐκδίκησιν αὐτῶν ἐν τάχει. πλὴν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐλθὼν ἆρα εὑρήσει τὴν πίστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;

verses.english: He also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and treated others with contempt:
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ πρός τινας τοὺς πεποιθότας ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι εἰσὶν δίκαιοι καὶ ἐξουθενοῦντας τοὺς λοιποὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην·

verses.english: "Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
verses.greek: Ἄνθρωποι δύο ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσεύξασθαι, ὁ εἷς Φαρισαῖος καὶ ὁ ἕτερος τελώνης.

verses.english: The Pharisee, standing by himself, prayed thus: 'God, I thank you that I am not like other people, robbers, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
verses.greek: ὁ Φαρισαῖος σταθεὶς πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ταῦτα προσηύχετο· Ὁ θεός, εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὥσπερ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἅρπαγες, ἄδικοι, μοιχοί, ἢ καὶ ὡς οὗτος ὁ τελώνης·

verses.english: I fast twice a week; I give tithes of all that I get.'
verses.greek: νηστεύω δὶς τοῦ σαββάτου, ἀποδεκατῶ πάντα ὅσα κτῶμαι.

verses.english: But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, 'God, be merciful to me, a sinner!'
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ τελώνης μακρόθεν ἑστὼς οὐκ ἤθελεν οὐδὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἐπᾶραι εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, ἀλλ’ ἔτυπτεν τὸ στῆθος αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ὁ θεός, ἱλάσθητί μοι τῷ ἁμαρτωλῷ.

verses.english: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted."
verses.greek: λέγω ὑμῖν, κατέβη οὗτος δεδικαιωμένος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ παρ’ ἐκεῖνον· ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.

verses.english: Now they were bringing even infants to him that he might touch them; and when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
verses.greek: Προσέφερον δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ τὰ βρέφη ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅπτηται· ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: But Jesus called them to him, saying, "Let the children come to me, and do not hinder them; for to such belongs the kingdom of God.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσεκαλέσατο αὐτὰ λέγων· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it."
verses.greek: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.

verses.english: And a ruler asked him, "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησέν τις αὐτὸν ἄρχων λέγων· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;

verses.english: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός.

verses.english: You know the commandments: Do not kill, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honour your father and mother."
verses.greek: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· Μὴ φονεύσῃς, Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μηδὲ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.

verses.english: And he said, "All these I have kept from my youth."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ταῦτα πάντα ἐφύλαξα ἐκ νεότητος.

verses.english: When Jesus heard this, he said to him, "One thing you lack: sell all that you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me."
verses.greek: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἕν σοι λείπει· πάντα ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ δὸς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.

verses.english: But when he heard these things, he became very sad, for he was very rich.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας ταῦτα περίλυπος ἐγενήθη, ἦν γὰρ πλούσιος σφόδρα.

verses.english: As he drew near to Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the roadside begging.
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἐγγίζειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰεριχὼ τυφλός τις ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἐπαιτῶν.

verses.english: Hearing a crowd going by, he asked what this meant.
verses.greek: ἀκούσας δὲ ὄχλου διαπορευομένου ἐπυνθάνετο τί εἴη τοῦτο·

verses.english: They told him, "Jesus of Nazareth is passing by."
verses.greek: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος παρέρχεται.

verses.english: And he cried out, "Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me!"
verses.greek: καὶ ἐβόησεν λέγων· Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.

verses.english: And those who were in front rebuked him, telling him to be silent; but he cried out all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
verses.greek: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ ἵνα σιγήσῃ· αὐτὸς δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν· Υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.

verses.english: Jesus stopped and commanded him to be brought to him. When he came near, he asked him,
verses.greek: σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ἀχθῆναι πρὸς αὐτόν. ἐγγίσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν·

verses.english: "What do you want me to do for you?" He said, "Lord, let me see again."
verses.greek: Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.

verses.english: And Jesus said to him, "See again; your faith has saved you."
verses.greek: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀνάβλεψον· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.

verses.english: And immediately he saw again and followed him, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.
verses.greek: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν. καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἰδὼν ἔδωκεν αἶνον τῷ θεῷ.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.36.1: Christ "set the parable of the judge forced to hear the widow by her persistence" and "added that God would avenge his chosen ones who cry to him day and night". So the God to be prayed to is a judge and avenger, the Creator. 18:4, 18:6 and 18:8 are not cited and are printed in grey.

notes.term: The Pharisee and the tax collector (18:9–14)
notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.36.1–2: two men praying in the temple "with different minds", the Pharisee in pride and the tax collector in humility, "one rejected and the other went down justified". He notes that the temple is the Creator's temple. 18:9 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Epiphanius, sch. 50 quotes the exchange: "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?" "Do not call me good; one is good, God", to which, he says, Marcion "added 'the Father'". The Marcionite speaker in the Dialogue of Adamantius has the same "except one, the Father", and Origen reports the heretics' use of it. Tertullian (4.36.3–7), the earliest witness, has "one God" without "the Father", and lists the commandments in the order "not to kill, not to commit adultery, not to steal, not to bear false witness, to love father and mother". He quotes the command to sell all and give to the poor, "and you will have treasure in heaven, and come, follow me", and says Christ "kept the earlier commandments and added what was lacking", as in Micah 6:8. "The Father" belongs to the later copies of Marcion's text and is not printed: the text before Marcion is decided by the earliest witness together with the correspondential reading, in which "Father" is relational throughout and only this reading makes it a title (METHOD §11). The order of the commandments and "give… treasure in heaven" are printed.

18:24–30 (the camel and the needle; the reward for leaving home and family) are not cited by any witness and form a paragraph without an attested verse. 18:31–33, the third prediction of the passion with "everything written by the prophets about the son of man will be fulfilled", is stated by Epiphanius to have been absent (sch. 52). 18:34, the disciples not understanding "these things", depends on it.

Three witnesses attest the healing. Epiphanius, sch. 51: "as he drew near to Jericho a blind man cried, Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me… your faith has saved you". Tertullian (4.36.8–14) dwells on the title: the blind man called him "son of David", and Jesus, far from correcting him, healed him and praised his faith. Tertullian takes this as proof that Jesus was known to be of David's family. The Dialogue (200) quotes the whole story; 18:36 and 18:40–41 rest on it alone.

Interpretation. The attested text has a blind man twice call Jesus "son of David", and Jesus answer with healing and "your faith has saved you". Tertullian's argument from this is that a Christ with no birth could not have been publicly known as David's descendant (4.36.8). The text does not say how the title was known. The library connects the Davidic descent of Jesus' family with the desposyni, the relatives who led the Jerusalem community (Carriers of Living Water). The verse shows only that the title was used of him and accepted.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 17
chapters.preamble: Zacchaeus and the money entrusted to the servants. In Jericho, Zacchaeus, a rich chief tax collector, receives Jesus into his house, gives half his goods to the poor and restores fourfold what he has taken by fraud. "Today salvation has come to this house… for the son of man came to seek and to save the lost." Jesus then tells of a nobleman who gives his servants money to trade with and, on his return, judges them by what they have done with it. In this text the parable ends with "from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away". The slaughter of the master's enemies (19:27) is not cited. The entry into Jerusalem, the lament over the city and the cleansing of the temple (19:29–46) are absent: Epiphanius states that the text lacked them.

verses.english: He entered Jericho and was passing through.
verses.greek: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν διήρχετο τὴν Ἰεριχώ.

verses.english: And there was a man named Zacchaeus; he was a chief tax collector and was rich.
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι καλούμενος Ζακχαῖος, καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἀρχιτελώνης καὶ αὐτὸς πλούσιος·

verses.english: He was trying to see who Jesus was, but on account of the crowd he could not, because he was small in stature.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν τίς ἐστιν, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ὅτι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ μικρὸς ἦν.

verses.english: So he ran ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was about to pass that way.
verses.greek: καὶ προδραμὼν εἰς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν ἀνέβη ἐπὶ συκομορέαν ἵνα ἴδῃ αὐτόν, ὅτι ἐκείνης ἤμελλεν διέρχεσθαι.

verses.english: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today."
verses.greek: καὶ ὡς ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον, ἀναβλέψας ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ζακχαῖε, σπεύσας κατάβηθι, σήμερον γὰρ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ σου δεῖ με μεῖναι.

verses.english: So he hurried and came down and received him joyfully.
verses.greek: καὶ σπεύσας κατέβη, καὶ ὑπεδέξατο αὐτὸν χαίρων.

verses.english: And when they saw it, they all grumbled, "He has gone in to be the guest of a man who is a sinner."
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδόντες πάντες διεγόγγυζον λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ ἁμαρτωλῷ ἀνδρὶ εἰσῆλθεν καταλῦσαι.

verses.english: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, "Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold."
verses.greek: σταθεὶς δὲ Ζακχαῖος εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν κύριον· Ἰδοὺ τὰ ἡμίσιά μου τῶν ὑπαρχόντων, κύριε, τοῖς πτωχοῖς δίδωμι, καὶ εἴ τινός τι ἐσυκοφάντησα ἀποδίδωμι τετραπλοῦν.

verses.english: And Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come to this house, since he also is a son of Abraham.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Σήμερον σωτηρία τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ ἐγένετο, καθότι καὶ αὐτὸς υἱὸς Ἀβραάμ ἐστιν·

verses.english: For the son of man came to seek and to save the lost."
verses.greek: ἦλθεν γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ζητῆσαι καὶ σῶσαι τὸ ἀπολωλός.

verses.english: As they heard these things, he went on to tell a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and because they supposed that the kingdom of God was to appear immediately.
verses.greek: Ἀκουόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ταῦτα προσθεὶς εἶπεν παραβολὴν διὰ τὸ ἐγγὺς εἶναι Ἰερουσαλὴμ αὐτὸν καὶ δοκεῖν αὐτοὺς ὅτι παραχρῆμα μέλλει ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναφαίνεσθαι·

verses.english: He said therefore, "A nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom and then return.
verses.greek: εἶπεν οὖν· Ἄνθρωπός τις εὐγενὴς ἐπορεύθη εἰς χώραν μακρὰν λαβεῖν ἑαυτῷ βασιλείαν καὶ ὑποστρέψαι.

verses.english: Calling ten of his servants, he gave them ten minas, and said to them, 'Engage in business until I come.'
verses.greek: καλέσας δὲ δέκα δούλους ἑαυτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δέκα μνᾶς καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Πραγματεύσασθε ἐν ᾧ ἔρχομαι.

verses.english: But his citizens hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, 'We do not want this man to reign over us.'
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ πολῖται αὐτοῦ ἐμίσουν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν πρεσβείαν ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Οὐ θέλομεν τοῦτον βασιλεῦσαι ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς.

verses.english: When he returned, having received the kingdom, he ordered these servants to whom he had given the money to be called to him, that he might know what they had gained by doing business.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐπανελθεῖν αὐτὸν λαβόντα τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ εἶπεν φωνηθῆναι αὐτῷ τοὺς δούλους τούτους οἷς δεδώκει τὸ ἀργύριον, ἵνα γνοῖ τί διεπραγματεύσαντο.

verses.english: The first came before him, saying, 'Lord, your mina has made ten minas more.'
verses.greek: παρεγένετο δὲ ὁ πρῶτος λέγων· Κύριε, ἡ μνᾶ σου δέκα προσηργάσατο μνᾶς.

verses.english: And he said to him, 'Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.'
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εὖγε, ἀγαθὲ δοῦλε, ὅτι ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ πιστὸς ἐγένου, ἴσθι ἐξουσίαν ἔχων ἐπάνω δέκα πόλεων.

verses.english: And the second came, saying, 'Lord, your mina has made five minas.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἦλθεν ὁ δεύτερος λέγων· Ἡ μνᾶ σου, κύριε, ἐποίησεν πέντε μνᾶς.

verses.english: And he said to him, 'And you are to be over five cities.'
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ καὶ τούτῳ· Καὶ σὺ ἐπάνω γίνου πέντε πόλεων.

verses.english: Then another came, saying, 'Lord, here is your mina, which I kept laid away in a handkerchief;
verses.greek: καὶ ὁ ἕτερος ἦλθεν λέγων· Κύριε, ἰδοὺ ἡ μνᾶ σου ἣν εἶχον ἀποκειμένην ἐν σουδαρίῳ·

verses.english: for I was afraid of you, because you are a severe man. You take what you did not deposit, and reap what you did not sow.'
verses.greek: ἐφοβούμην γάρ σε ὅτι ἄνθρωπος αὐστηρὸς εἶ, αἴρεις ὃ οὐκ ἔθηκας καὶ θερίζεις ὃ οὐκ ἔσπειρας.

verses.english: He said to him, 'I will condemn you with your own words, you wicked servant! You knew that I was a severe man, taking what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow?
verses.greek: λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἐκ τοῦ στόματός σου κρίνω σε, πονηρὲ δοῦλε· ᾔδεις ὅτι ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος αὐστηρός εἰμι, αἴρων ὃ οὐκ ἔθηκα καὶ θερίζων ὃ οὐκ ἔσπειρα;

verses.english: Why then did you not put my money in the bank, and at my coming I might have collected it with interest?'
verses.greek: καὶ διὰ τί οὐκ ἔδωκάς μου τὸ ἀργύριον ἐπὶ τράπεζαν; κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν σὺν τόκῳ ἂν αὐτὸ ἔπραξα.

verses.english: And he said to those who stood by, 'Take the mina from him, and give it to the one who has the ten minas.'
verses.greek: καὶ τοῖς παρεστῶσιν εἶπεν· Ἄρατε ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὴν μνᾶν καὶ δότε τῷ τὰς δέκα μνᾶς ἔχοντι—

verses.english: And they said to him, 'Lord, he has ten minas!'
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἔχει δέκα μνᾶς—

verses.english: 'I tell you that to everyone who has, more will be given; but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away.
verses.greek: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι παντὶ τῷ ἔχοντι δοθήσεται, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ μὴ ἔχοντος καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.37.1–3: "the house of Zacchaeus also attains salvation". Zacchaeus received the Lord and fed him, offered half his goods for works of mercy and said "if I have taken anything from anyone by false accusation, I restore it fourfold"; "Today, he said, salvation to this house." Tertullian reads this as Isaiah 58:7 fulfilled, and "the son of man came to save what was lost" as the salvation of the whole person, body and soul. 19:1, 19:3–5 and 19:7 are not cited and are printed in grey.

notes.term: The money entrusted to the servants (19:11–26)
notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.37.4: "the parable of the servants who are judged according to the account of their master's money lent at interest shows God as judge, even on the side of severity". He has the "austere" master "taking what he did not deposit and reaping what he did not sow", and taking away "what one seemed to have". He mentions the parable again at 4.39.11 ("leaving money with his servants to trade with"). The unattested verses of the parable are printed in grey.

19:27, the slaughter of the enemies who did not want the nobleman to reign, is not cited by Tertullian, though his point was the master's severity; it is classed probably absent. 19:29–46 are absent by Epiphanius' statement (sch. 53): the colt and Bethphage, the city, and the temple with "my house shall be called a house of prayer". 19:28 and 19:47–48, the verses that frame them, form paragraphs with no attested verse. In this text Jesus goes from the parable to the question about his authority (20:1–8) without a royal entry into Jerusalem or the cleansing of the temple.

Interpretation. Without 19:29–46, the text has no royal entry on a colt and no action against the traders in the temple, the scenes in which canonical Luke presents Jesus as king and judge of the temple. In the attested text Jesus is in the temple teaching (20:1; 21:37), and the authorities question his authority there. Epiphanius' charge is that Marcion cut these scenes out. On the Marcionite-priority view, canonical Luke added them. The witnesses establish only that they were absent from the text.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 18
chapters.preamble: Questions in the temple. Asked by what authority he acts, Jesus asks in return whether John's baptism was from heaven or from men, and when the leaders will not answer, he will not tell them either. The leaders seek to seize him but fear the people. To the question about tribute he answers, "Give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's." To the Sadducees' question about the woman with seven husbands he answers that the sons of this age marry, "but those whom God has deemed worthy to attain to that age and to the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage… they are equal to angels and are sons of God". He asks how the Christ can be David's son when David calls him Lord. The parable of the tenants with the rejected stone (20:9–18) and the proof of the resurrection from Moses at the bush (20:37–38) are absent: Epiphanius states that the text lacked them.

verses.english: One day, as he was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the good news, the chief priests and the scribes with the elders came up
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν διδάσκοντος αὐτοῦ τὸν λαὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εὐαγγελιζομένου ἐπέστησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς σὺν τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις,

verses.english: and said to him, "Tell us by what authority you do these things, or who it is that gave you this authority."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπαν λέγοντες πρὸς αὐτόν· Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς, ἢ τίς ἐστιν ὁ δούς σοι τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην;

verses.english: He answered them, "I also will ask you a question. Now tell me:
verses.greek: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον, καὶ εἴπατέ μοι·

verses.english: was the baptism of John from heaven or from men?"
verses.greek: Τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;

verses.english: And they discussed it with one another, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven', he will say, 'Why did you not believe him?'
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ συνελογίσαντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ· Διὰ τί οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;

verses.english: But if we say, 'From men', all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."
verses.greek: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων, ὁ λαὸς ἅπας καταλιθάσει ἡμᾶς, πεπεισμένος γάρ ἐστιν Ἰωάννην προφήτην εἶναι·

verses.english: So they answered that they did not know where it came from.
verses.greek: καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν μὴ εἰδέναι πόθεν.

verses.english: And Jesus said to them, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."
verses.greek: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.

verses.english: The scribes and the chief priests sought to lay hands on him at that very hour, but they feared the people.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐζήτησαν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐπιβαλεῖν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν λαόν.

verses.english: So they watched him, and sent spies, who pretended to be sincere, that they might catch him in something he said, so as to deliver him up to the authority and jurisdiction of the governor.
verses.greek: Καὶ παρατηρήσαντες ἀπέστειλαν ἐγκαθέτους ὑποκρινομένους ἑαυτοὺς δικαίους εἶναι, ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται αὐτοῦ λόγου, ὥστε παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν τῇ ἀρχῇ καὶ τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος.

verses.english: So they asked him, "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, and show no partiality, but truly teach the way of God.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὀρθῶς λέγεις καὶ διδάσκεις καὶ οὐ λαμβάνεις πρόσωπον, ἀλλ’ ἐπ’ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ διδάσκεις·

verses.english: Is it lawful for us to give tribute to Caesar, or not?"
verses.greek: ἔξεστιν ἡμᾶς Καίσαρι φόρον δοῦναι ἢ οὔ;

verses.english: But he perceived their craftiness, and said to them,
verses.greek: κατανοήσας δὲ αὐτῶν τὴν πανουργίαν εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς·

verses.english: "Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have?" They said, "Caesar's."
verses.greek: Δείξατέ μοι δηνάριον· τίνος ἔχει εἰκόνα καὶ ἐπιγραφήν; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Καίσαρος.

verses.english: He said to them, "Then give back to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τοίνυν ἀπόδοτε τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ.

verses.english: And they were not able in the presence of the people to catch him in what he said, but marvelling at his answer they became silent.
verses.greek: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ἐπιλαβέσθαι αὐτοῦ ῥήματος ἐναντίον τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ θαυμάσαντες ἐπὶ τῇ ἀποκρίσει αὐτοῦ ἐσίγησαν.

verses.english: There came to him some Sadducees, those who deny that there is a resurrection, and they asked him,
verses.greek: Προσελθόντες δέ τινες τῶν Σαδδουκαίων, οἱ ἀντιλέγοντες ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι, ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν

verses.english: saying, "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies, having a wife but no children, the man must take the widow and raise up offspring for his brother.
verses.greek: λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν, ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ ἔχων γυναῖκα, καὶ οὗτος ἄτεκνος ᾖ, ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and died without children.
verses.greek: ἑπτὰ οὖν ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος λαβὼν γυναῖκα ἀπέθανεν ἄτεκνος·

verses.english: And the second
verses.greek: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος

verses.english: and the third took her, and likewise all seven left no children and died.
verses.greek: καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν, ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐ κατέλιπον τέκνα καὶ ἀπέθανον·

verses.english: Afterwards the woman also died.
verses.greek: ὕστερον καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν.

verses.english: In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife will the woman be? For the seven had her as wife."
verses.greek: ἡ γυνὴ οὖν ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τίνος αὐτῶν γίνεται γυνή; οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα.

verses.english: And Jesus said to them, "The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage,
verses.greek: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου γαμοῦσιν καὶ γαμίσκονται,

verses.english: but those whom God has deemed worthy to attain to that age and to the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage;
verses.greek: οὓς δὲ κατηξίωσεν ὁ θεὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος ἐκείνου τυχεῖν καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῆς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται·

verses.english: for they cannot die any more, because they are equal to angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
verses.greek: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἀποθανεῖν ἔτι δύνανται, ἰσάγγελοι γάρ εἰσιν καὶ υἱοί εἰσιν θεοῦ τῆς ἀναστάσεως υἱοὶ ὄντες.

verses.english: Then some of the scribes answered, "Teacher, you have spoken well."
verses.greek: ἀποκριθέντες δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν· Διδάσκαλε, καλῶς εἶπας·

verses.english: For they no longer dared to ask him any question.
verses.greek: οὐκέτι γὰρ ἐτόλμων ἐπερωτᾶν αὐτὸν οὐδέν.

verses.english: But he said to them, "How can they say that the Anointed One is David's son?
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Πῶς λέγουσιν τὸν χριστὸν εἶναι Δαυὶδ υἱόν;

verses.english: For David himself says in the Book of Psalms, 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand,
verses.greek: αὐτὸς γὰρ Δαυὶδ λέγει ἐν βίβλῳ ψαλμῶν· Εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου

verses.english: until I make your enemies your footstool.'
verses.greek: ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.

verses.english: David thus calls him Lord, so how is he his son?"
verses.greek: Δαυὶδ οὖν κύριον αὐτὸν καλεῖ, καὶ πῶς αὐτοῦ υἱός ἐστιν;

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.38.1–2: Christ knew where John's baptism came from, and asked so that the Pharisees would judge themselves. "Why did you not believe him?" shows that he wanted John to be believed, and so that John's baptism was the Creator's. The leaders' fear of being stoned and Jesus' "Neither do I tell you by what power I do these things" are both cited. 20:2–3 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Epiphanius, sch. 55: Marcion "again cut out what concerns the vineyard let out to tenants, and 'What then is this: the stone which the builders rejected?'". 20:18, on falling on that stone, goes with it. Epiphanius does quote 20:19 (sch. 54), the leaders seeking to seize Jesus and fearing the people. It is printed without its last clause, "for they knew that he had told this parable against them", which refers to the absent parable. In this text the leaders' hostility follows the exchange about John.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.38.3 quotes "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's". He explains that what is God's is what bears his image and likeness, the human being, so the saying gives man back to his maker. 20:20–23 and 20:26 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.38.4–9 follows the Sadducees' question and the reply closely. He quotes the reply three times as "those whom God has deemed worthy of that age and of the resurrection from the dead". He reports that the Marcionites read "the God of that age" together, a second God who grants the resurrection, and he argues for a different punctuation, not a different text. The active "whom God has deemed worthy" is printed; canonical Luke has the passive "those who are deemed worthy". Epiphanius states twice (sch. 56–57) that the text lacked the proof from Moses at the bush, "he is God not of the dead but of the living" (20:37–38). It is not printed. The scribes' "Teacher, you have spoken well" (20:39) follows directly on the sayings about the resurrection.

Interpretation. In this text the answer about the resurrection is that the worthy "neither marry nor are given in marriage, for they cannot die any more, because they are equal to angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection". There is no argument from the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, as there are no patriarchs in the kingdom at 13:28. The resurrection is described as a state God grants to the worthy, "equal to angels" and "sons of God". It is not described as the return of the body that was buried. The witnesses do not say how the community behind the text pictured it.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.38.10: the scribes thought the Christ was David's son; David calls him Lord. Tertullian connects this with the blind man's "son of David" (18:38): Jesus accepted that title then and now shows he is also David's Lord. 20:42–43, the quotation of Psalm 110:1, are not cited and are printed in grey. 20:45–47, the warning against the scribes, form a paragraph with no attested verse and are not printed.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 19
chapters.preamble: The signs of the end. The disciples ask when these things will be. Jesus warns them against those who will come in his name, and speaks of wars, earthquakes, famines, terrors and signs from heaven, and of persecution before kings and governors, "for my name's sake". He tells them not to prepare their defence, for he will give them wisdom, and that by endurance they will gain their lives. He speaks of Jerusalem surrounded by armies, of signs in sun, moon and stars, and of the son of man "coming from the heavens with great power" (Tertullian, Marc. 4.39.10). When these things begin, they are to lift up their heads, for their redemption is near; the fig tree shows that the kingdom of God is near. He warns them against dissipation and the cares of life. By day he teaches in the temple and by night he lodges on the Mount of Olives. Two sayings are absent, by Epiphanius' statement: "not a hair of your head will perish" (21:18) and the flight from Judea "that all that is written may be fulfilled" (21:21–22).

verses.english: And they asked him, "Teacher, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when these things are about to take place?"
verses.greek: Ἐπηρώτησαν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, πότε οὖν ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα γίνεσθαι;

verses.english: And he said, "See that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name, saying, 'I am he!' and, 'The time is at hand!' Do not go after them.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Βλέπετε μὴ πλανηθῆτε· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες· Ἐγώ εἰμι καί· Ὁ καιρὸς ἤγγικεν· μὴ πορευθῆτε ὀπίσω αὐτῶν.

verses.english: And when you hear of wars and tumults, do not be terrified, for these things must first take place, but the end will not be at once."
verses.greek: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκαταστασίας, μὴ πτοηθῆτε· δεῖ γὰρ ταῦτα γενέσθαι πρῶτον, ἀλλ’ οὐκ εὐθέως τὸ τέλος.

verses.english: Then he said to them, "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
verses.greek: τότε ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγερθήσεται ἔθνος ἐπ’ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν,

verses.english: There will be great earthquakes, and in various places famines and pestilences; and there will be terrors and great signs from heaven.
verses.greek: σεισμοί τε μεγάλοι καὶ κατὰ τόπους λιμοὶ καὶ λοιμοὶ ἔσονται, φόβητρά τε καὶ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἔσται.

verses.english: But before all this they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues and prisons, and you will be brought before kings and governors for my name's sake.
verses.greek: Πρὸ δὲ τούτων πάντων ἐπιβαλοῦσιν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν καὶ διώξουσιν, παραδιδόντες εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ φυλακάς, ἀπαγομένους ἐπὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἡγεμόνας ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου·

verses.english: This will be your opportunity to bear witness.
verses.greek: ἀποβήσεται ὑμῖν εἰς μαρτύριον.

verses.english: Settle it therefore in your minds not to prepare your defence beforehand,
verses.greek: θέτε οὖν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν μὴ προμελετᾶν ἀπολογηθῆναι,

verses.english: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which none of your adversaries will be able to withstand or contradict.
verses.greek: ἐγὼ γὰρ δώσω ὑμῖν στόμα καὶ σοφίαν ᾗ οὐ δυνήσονται ἀντιστῆναι ἢ ἀντειπεῖν ἅπαντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι ὑμῖν.

verses.english: You will be delivered up even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and some of you they will put to death.
verses.greek: παραδοθήσεσθε δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ γονέων καὶ ἀδελφῶν καὶ συγγενῶν καὶ φίλων, καὶ θανατώσουσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν,

verses.english: You will be hated by all for my name's sake.
verses.greek: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.

verses.english: By your endurance you will gain your lives.
verses.greek: ἐν τῇ ὑπομονῇ ὑμῶν κτήσασθε τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.

verses.english: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near.
verses.greek: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε κυκλουμένην ὑπὸ στρατοπέδων Ἰερουσαλήμ, τότε γνῶτε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ ἐρήμωσις αὐτῆς.

verses.english: Alas for women who are pregnant and for those who are nursing infants in those days! For there will be great distress upon the earth and wrath against this people.
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις· ἔσται γὰρ ἀνάγκη μεγάλη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὀργὴ τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ,

verses.english: They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive among all nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled underfoot by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
verses.greek: καὶ πεσοῦνται στόματι μαχαίρης καὶ αἰχμαλωτισθήσονται εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πάντα, καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἔσται πατουμένη ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν, ἄχρι οὗ πληρωθῶσιν καιροὶ ἐθνῶν.

verses.english: And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth distress of nations in perplexity because of the roaring of the sea and the waves,
verses.greek: Καὶ ἔσονται σημεῖα ἐν ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ καὶ ἄστροις, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς συνοχὴ ἐθνῶν ἐν ἀπορίᾳ ἤχους θαλάσσης καὶ σάλου,

verses.english: people fainting with fear and with foreboding of what is coming on the world. For the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
verses.greek: ἀποψυχόντων ἀνθρώπων ἀπὸ φόβου καὶ προσδοκίας τῶν ἐπερχομένων τῇ οἰκουμένῃ, αἱ γὰρ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.

verses.english: And then they will see the son of man coming from the heavens with great power.
verses.greek: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἀπὸ τῶν οὐρανῶν μετὰ δυνάμεως πολλῆς.

verses.english: Now when these things begin to take place, straighten up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near."
verses.greek: ἀρχομένων δὲ τούτων γίνεσθαι ἀνακύψατε καὶ ἐπάρατε τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑμῶν, διότι ἐγγίζει ἡ ἀπολύτρωσις ὑμῶν.

verses.english: And he told them a parable: "Look at the fig tree, and all the trees.
verses.greek: Καὶ εἶπεν παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Ἴδετε τὴν συκῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ δένδρα·

verses.english: As soon as they come into leaf, you see for yourselves and know that the summer is already near.
verses.greek: ὅταν προβάλωσιν ἤδη, βλέποντες ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤδη ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·

verses.english: So also, when you see these things taking place, you know that the kingdom of God is near.
verses.greek: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all has taken place.
verses.greek: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.

verses.english: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
verses.greek: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.

verses.english: But watch yourselves lest your hearts be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness and cares of this life, and that day come upon you suddenly
verses.greek: Προσέχετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς μήποτε βαρηθῶσιν ὑμῶν αἱ καρδίαι ἐν κραιπάλῃ καὶ μέθῃ καὶ μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς, καὶ ἐπιστῇ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς αἰφνίδιος ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη

verses.english: like a trap. For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth.
verses.greek: ὡς παγίς· ἐπεισελεύσεται γὰρ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.

verses.english: But stay awake at all times, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are going to take place, and to stand before the son of man."
verses.greek: ἀγρυπνεῖτε δὲ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ δεόμενοι ἵνα κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, καὶ σταθῆναι ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

verses.english: Every day he was teaching in the temple, but at night he went out and lodged on the mount called Olivet.
verses.greek: Ἦν δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων, τὰς δὲ νύκτας ἐξερχόμενος ηὐλίζετο εἰς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν·

verses.english: And all the people came early in the morning to hear him in the temple.
verses.greek: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ὤρθριζεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.

notes.explanation: The widow's two coins (21:1–4) and the prediction that not one stone of the temple will be left on another (21:5–6) are not cited by any witness. Each is a separate NA27 paragraph, and they are not printed. Tertullian describes the discourse as running "from the disciples' question to the parable of the fig tree" (4.39.13), so his account begins at 21:7.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.39.1–8 goes through the discourse in order. Those who "come in my name" use a name that belongs to the Creator's Christ. The wars, famines, earthquakes and portents "must take place". The persecutions come "before these things". The disciples are not to think beforehand what to answer before tribunals: for Tertullian, the one who forbids it is the one who gave Balaam words he had not thought of and promised Moses a mouth. "By endurance you will save yourselves." Epiphanius states that the text lacked 21:18, "not a hair of your head will perish" (sch. 58).

Tertullian (4.39.9–12): when Jerusalem begins to be surrounded by armies ("vallari exercitibus Hierusalem"), the signs of the end follow, in sun, moon and stars, nations in anguish "as at the roar of the sea", the powers of heaven shaken. "And then they will see the son of man coming from the heavens with great power". Then come "lift up your heads, for your redemption has drawn near". The reading "from the heavens with great power" is printed for canonical Luke's "in a cloud with power and great glory". Epiphanius states that the text lacked the flight of those in Judea to the mountains and "until all that is written is fulfilled" (21:21–22; sch. 59). No witness to this text has the "abomination of desolation" of Mark 13:14 and Matthew 24:15. 21:23–24 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.39.16–19: the fig tree that bears fruit is a sign of summer, as the troubles of the world are a sign of the kingdom. "Heaven and earth will pass away" and the Lord's word remains (he cites Isa 40:8). The disciples are warned against heaviness of heart "with dissipation, drunkenness and worldly cares", lest the day come on them "like a trap". Jesus taught by day in the temple and withdrew at night to the Mount of Olives. 21:36 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Interpretation. In this text the son of man comes "from the heavens with great power", without the cloud and the "glory" of canonical Luke. The redemption drawing near is set beside "the kingdom of God is near" (21:31), and the warning is against the heaviness of a heart taken up with drink and worldly cares. Tertullian's argument is that the terrors and the promises belong to one son of man and cannot be separated (4.39.13–15). The text keeps the coming and the call to watchfulness in one discourse.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 20
chapters.preamble: The Passover, the betrayal and the council. The feast of Unleavened Bread draws near. Judas, one of the twelve, agrees with the chief priests and officers to hand Jesus over for money; in this text he is not said to be entered by Satan (Tertullian, Marc. 5.6.7). Jesus has the Passover prepared and eats it with the apostles: "I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer." He gives the bread as his body and the cup as the covenant in his blood (Tertullian, Marc. 4.40.3–6). He foretells Peter's denial, prays kneeling a stone's throw from the disciples, and is betrayed with a kiss. He is mocked and beaten, and before the council says that from now on the son of man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God. Epiphanius states that the text lacked the saying about not eating the Passover again until the kingdom (22:16), the purse and the swords with "he was counted among the lawless" (22:35–38), and the servant's ear (22:50–51).

verses.english: Now the feast of Unleavened Bread drew near, which is called the Passover.
verses.greek: Ἤγγιζεν δὲ ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἀζύμων ἡ λεγομένη Πάσχα.

verses.english: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how to put him to death, for they feared the people.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὸ πῶς ἀνέλωσιν αὐτόν, ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν.

verses.english: Now Judas called Iscariot, who was of the number of the twelve,
verses.greek: Ἰούδας δὲ ὁ καλούμενος Ἰσκαριώτης, ὢν ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τῶν δώδεκα,

verses.english: went away and conferred with the chief priests and officers how he might hand him over to them.
verses.greek: καὶ ἀπελθὼν συνελάλησεν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ στρατηγοῖς τὸ πῶς αὐτὸν παραδῷ αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: And they were glad, and agreed to give him money.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐχάρησαν καὶ συνέθεντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι.

verses.english: So he consented and sought an opportunity to hand him over to them in the absence of a crowd.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐξωμολόγησεν, καὶ ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν τοῦ παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν ἄτερ ὄχλου αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: Then came the day of Unleavened Bread, on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
verses.greek: Ἦλθεν δὲ ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν ἀζύμων, ἐν ᾗ ἔδει θύεσθαι τὸ πάσχα·

verses.english: So he sent Peter and John, saying, "Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat it."
verses.greek: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην εἰπών· Πορευθέντες ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν τὸ πάσχα ἵνα φάγωμεν.

verses.english: They said to him, "Where will you have us prepare it?"
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ποῦ θέλεις ἑτοιμάσωμεν;

verses.english: He said to them, "Look, when you have entered the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house that he enters,
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἰδοὺ εἰσελθόντων ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν πόλιν συναντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων· ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν εἰς ἣν εἰσπορεύεται.

verses.english: and tell the master of the house, "The Teacher says to you, Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?"
verses.greek: καὶ ἐρεῖτε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ τῆς οἰκίας· Λέγει σοι ὁ διδάσκαλος· Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμα ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;

verses.english: And he will show you a large upper room furnished; prepare it there."
verses.greek: κἀκεῖνος ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον· ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε.

verses.english: And they went and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.greek: ἀπελθόντες δὲ εὗρον καθὼς εἰρήκει αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.

verses.english: And when the hour came, he reclined at table, and the apostles with him.
verses.greek: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡ ὥρα, ἀνέπεσεν καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι σὺν αὐτῷ.

verses.english: And he said to them, "I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπεθύμησα τοῦτο τὸ πάσχα φαγεῖν μεθ’ ὑμῶν πρὸ τοῦ με παθεῖν·

verses.english: And he took a cup, and when he had given thanks he said, "Take this, and divide it among yourselves.
verses.greek: καὶ δεξάμενος ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας εἶπεν· Λάβετε τοῦτο καὶ διαμερίσατε εἰς ἑαυτούς·

verses.english: For I tell you that from now on I shall not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
verses.greek: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως οὗ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἔλθῃ.

verses.english: And he took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me."
verses.greek: καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν διδόμενον· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.

verses.english: And likewise the cup after they had eaten, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
verses.greek: καὶ τὸ ποτήριον ὡσαύτως μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐν τῷ αἵματί μου, τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐκχυννόμενον.

verses.english: But see, the hand of him who betrays me is with me on the table.
verses.greek: πλὴν ἰδοὺ ἡ χεὶρ τοῦ παραδιδόντος με μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης·

verses.english: For the son of man goes as it has been determined, but woe to that man by whom he is betrayed!"
verses.greek: ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς μὲν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου κατὰ τὸ ὡρισμένον πορεύεται, πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ δι’ οὗ παραδίδοται.

verses.english: And they began to question one another, which of them it could be who was going to do this.
verses.greek: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς τὸ τίς ἄρα εἴη ἐξ αὐτῶν ὁ τοῦτο μέλλων πράσσειν.

verses.english: "Simon, Simon, look, Satan has demanded to have you, that he might sift you like wheat,
verses.greek: Σίμων Σίμων, ἰδοὺ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐξῃτήσατο ὑμᾶς τοῦ σινιάσαι ὡς τὸν σῖτον·

verses.english: but I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail. And when you have turned again, strengthen your brothers."
verses.greek: ἐγὼ δὲ ἐδεήθην περὶ σοῦ ἵνα μὴ ἐκλίπῃ ἡ πίστις σου· καὶ σύ ποτε ἐπιστρέψας στήρισον τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου.

verses.english: Peter said to him, "Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μετὰ σοῦ ἕτοιμός εἰμι καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν καὶ εἰς θάνατον πορεύεσθαι.

verses.english: Jesus said, "I tell you, Peter, the cock will not crow this day until you deny three times that you know me."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Λέγω σοι, Πέτρε, οὐ φωνήσει σήμερον ἀλέκτωρ ἕως τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ εἰδέναι.

verses.english: And he came out and went, as was his custom, to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed him.
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη κατὰ τὸ ἔθος εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν· ἠκολούθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταί.

verses.english: And when he came to the place, he said to them, "Pray that you may not enter into temptation."
verses.greek: γενόμενος δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ τόπου εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Προσεύχεσθε μὴ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς πειρασμόν.

verses.english: And he withdrew from them about a stone's throw, and knelt down and prayed,
verses.greek: καὶ αὐτὸς ἀπεσπάσθη ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λίθου βολήν, καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύχετο

verses.english: saying, "Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done."
verses.greek: λέγων· Πάτερ, εἰ βούλει παρένεγκε τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ· πλὴν μὴ τὸ θέλημά μου ἀλλὰ τὸ σὸν γινέσθω.

verses.english: And when he rose from prayer, he came to the disciples and found them sleeping for sorrow,
verses.greek: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἀπὸ τῆς προσευχῆς ἐλθὼν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εὗρεν κοιμωμένους αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς λύπης,

verses.english: and he said to them, "Why are you sleeping? Rise and pray that you may not enter into temptation."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί καθεύδετε; ἀναστάντες προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν.

verses.english: While he was still speaking, there came a crowd, and the man called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. He drew near to Jesus to kiss him,
verses.greek: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ ὄχλος, καὶ ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα προήρχετο αὐτούς, καὶ ἤγγισεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ φιλῆσαι αὐτόν.

verses.english: but Jesus said to him, "Judas, would you betray the son of man with a kiss?"
verses.greek: Ἰησοῦς δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἰούδα, φιλήματι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδως;

verses.english: Now the men who were holding Jesus in custody were mocking him as they beat him.
verses.greek: Καὶ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ συνέχοντες αὐτὸν ἐνέπαιζον αὐτῷ δέροντες,

verses.english: They also blindfolded him and kept asking him, "Prophesy! Who is it that struck you?"
verses.greek: καὶ περικαλύψαντες αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτων λέγοντες· Προφήτευσον, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε;

verses.english: And they said many other things against him, blaspheming him.
verses.greek: καὶ ἕτερα πολλὰ βλασφημοῦντες ἔλεγον εἰς αὐτόν.

verses.english: When day came, the assembly of the elders of the people gathered together, both chief priests and scribes. And they led him away to their council,
verses.greek: Καὶ ὡς ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, συνήχθη τὸ πρεσβυτέριον τοῦ λαοῦ, ἀρχιερεῖς τε καὶ γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ συνέδριον αὐτῶν,

verses.english: and they said, "If you are the Anointed One, tell us." But he said to them, "If I tell you, you will not believe,
verses.greek: λέγοντες· Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός, εἰπὸν ἡμῖν. εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἐὰν ὑμῖν εἴπω οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε·

verses.english: and if I ask you, you will not answer.
verses.greek: ἐὰν δὲ ἐρωτήσω, οὐ μὴ ἀποκριθῆτε.

verses.english: But from now on the son of man shall be seated at the right hand of the power of God."
verses.greek: ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν δὲ ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενος ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: So they all said, "Are you the Son of God, then?" And he said to them, "You say that I am."
verses.greek: εἶπαν δὲ πάντες· Σὺ οὖν εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ; ὁ δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔφη· Ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι.

verses.english: Then they said, "What further testimony do we need? We have heard it ourselves from his own lips."
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Τί ἔτι ἔχομεν μαρτυρίας χρείαν; αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἠκούσαμεν ἀπὸ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.40.1–2: of all the Jewish feasts Jesus chose the day of the Passover; he could have been betrayed by a stranger and without a price, but was betrayed by one who ate bread with him, and for money, as the prophets said. In book 5 (5.6.7) Tertullian writes that "in my text" Satan entered Judas, against what holds "according to Marcion". The words "Satan entered into" (22:3) are therefore not printed, and the rest of the verse is put in the nominative. Epiphanius quotes 22:4 (sch. 60) with the order "how he might hand him over to them", which is printed.

Epiphanius quotes the sending of the disciples to prepare the Passover (sch. 61) and Jesus reclining with "the twelve apostles" (sch. 62). Both witnesses quote "I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer" (Tertullian 4.40.1; sch. 62). Epiphanius states that "I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God" (22:16) was not in the text (sch. 63). Tertullian (4.40.3–6) argues from the bread, "this is my body", and from the cup, "establishing the covenant sealed in his blood", that the body was real flesh. 22:17–18 are not cited and are printed in grey.

notes.term: The long text of the Supper (22:19–20)
notes.explanation: 22:19b–20 ("which is given for you… the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you") are absent from D and part of the Old Latin, and Westcott and Hort counted them among the Western non-interpolations. Tertullian's allusion to the cup and the covenant in Jesus' blood (4.40.4) shows that the text he read had at least 22:20 in some form, and his "then he should have handed over bread for us" points to "given for you". The second-century text attested here therefore stands with the long text, not with D (Roth, 259 n. 390). Both verses are printed as NA27 has them; the words the witness does not cite are noted.

22:16 is absent by Epiphanius' statement (sch. 63). 22:24–30, the dispute about greatness and the twelve thrones, form a paragraph with no attested verse; Epiphanius' "or he cut these out again" (elenchus 63) suggests that 22:30 was not in the text. 22:35–38, the purse, the bag and the two swords with "he was counted among the lawless" (Isa 53:12), are absent by Epiphanius' statement (sch. 64).

Epiphanius quotes "he withdrew from them about a stone's throw and knelt down and prayed" (sch. 65) and argues from the kneeling that Jesus had a body. 22:43–44, the angel from heaven and the sweat like drops of blood, are printed by NA27 in double brackets as not part of its text, and no witness cites them for this text; they are not printed. Judas draws near to kiss Jesus (sch. 66), and Tertullian notes that he was to be betrayed "with a kiss" (4.41.2). Epiphanius states that the cutting off of the servant's ear and its healing were not in the text (sch. 67); 22:49, which asks whether to strike with the sword, depends on the absent swords (22:38) and the absent blow and is not printed. 22:52–53 and Peter's denial (22:54–62) form paragraphs with no attested verse.

Epiphanius quotes the mockery, the beating and "Prophesy, who is it that struck you?" (sch. 68), as proof of a body that could be struck. Tertullian (4.41.3–5) follows the council: asked whether he is the Christ, Jesus answers "if I tell you, you will not believe"; "from now on the son of man shall be seated at the right hand of the power of God" (Dan 7:13; Ps 110:1); asked "are you the Son of God?", he answers "you say", which Tertullian takes as an affirmation.

Interpretation. Without "Satan entered into Judas", the betrayal in this text is the act of one of the twelve, done for money, and the "woe" of 22:22 falls on him; Tertullian (4.41.1) argues from that "woe" that the God of this Jesus judges. The meal is a Passover that Jesus has "earnestly desired" to eat. In the attested text he gives the bread as his body and the cup as the covenant in his blood. Which canonical words go beyond what the witness cites ("do this in remembrance of me", "poured out for you") is recorded verse by verse; the verse-level evidence does not support reading this text as a fellowship meal without the cup of the covenant.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 21
chapters.preamble: Pilate, Herod and the cross. The council brings Jesus to Pilate. In this text the accusers say: "We found this man misleading our nation and destroying the law and the prophets, forbidding us to give tribute to Caesar and turning away the women and the children" (Epiphanius, sch. 69–70). Pilate sends him to Herod, who is glad to see him and hears no word from him. The crowd asks for Barabbas and demands that Jesus be crucified. He is crucified at the Skull between two criminals. There is darkness at the sixth hour and the curtain of the temple is torn. Jesus cries out with a loud voice to the Father and breathes his last. Joseph, who had not consented to the council's act, takes down the body, wraps it in linen and lays it in a rock-cut tomb. The women see the tomb and rest on the Sabbath. By the witnesses' statements the text lacked the dividing of the garments (Tertullian) and "Today you will be with me in paradise" (Epiphanius).

verses.english: Then the whole company of them arose and brought him before Pilate.
verses.greek: Καὶ ἀναστὰν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Πιλᾶτον.

verses.english: And they began to accuse him, saying, "We found this man misleading our nation and destroying the law and the prophets, forbidding us to give tribute to Caesar and turning away the women and the children, and saying that he himself is the Anointed One, a king."
verses.greek: ἤρξαντο δὲ κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Τοῦτον εὕραμεν διαστρέφοντα τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ καταλύοντα τὸν νόμον καὶ τοὺς προφήτας καὶ κωλύοντα φόρους Καίσαρι διδόναι καὶ ἀποστρέφοντα τὰς γυναῖκας καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ λέγοντα ἑαυτὸν χριστὸν βασιλέα εἶναι.

verses.english: And Pilate asked him, "Are you the King of the Jews?" And he answered him, "You say so."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη· Σὺ λέγεις.

verses.english: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, "I find no guilt in this man."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ὄχλους· Οὐδὲν εὑρίσκω αἴτιον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ.

verses.english: But they were urgent, saying, "He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, from Galilee where he began even to this place."
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἐπίσχυον λέγοντες ὅτι Ἀνασείει τὸν λαὸν διδάσκων καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἕως ὧδε.

verses.english: When Pilate heard this, he asked whether the man was a Galilean.
verses.greek: Πιλᾶτος δὲ ἀκούσας ἐπηρώτησεν εἰ ὁ ἄνθρωπος Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν,

verses.english: And when he learned that he belonged to Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him over to Herod, who was himself in Jerusalem at that time.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου ἐστὶν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν πρὸς Ἡρῴδην, ὄντα καὶ αὐτὸν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν ταύταις ταῖς ἡμέραις.

verses.english: When Herod saw Jesus, he was very glad, for he had long desired to see him, because he had heard about him, and he was hoping to see some sign done by him.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐχάρη λίαν, ἦν γὰρ ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων θέλων ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ ἀκούειν περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤλπιζέν τι σημεῖον ἰδεῖν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γινόμενον.

verses.english: So he questioned him at some length, but he made no answer.
verses.greek: ἐπηρώτα δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν λόγοις ἱκανοῖς· αὐτὸς δὲ οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτῷ.

verses.english: The chief priests and the scribes stood by, vehemently accusing him.
verses.greek: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς εὐτόνως κατηγοροῦντες αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And Herod with his soldiers treated him with contempt and mocked him. Then, arraying him in splendid clothing, he sent him back to Pilate.
verses.greek: ἐξουθενήσας δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ Ἡρῴδης σὺν τοῖς στρατεύμασιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμπαίξας περιβαλὼν ἐσθῆτα λαμπρὰν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν τῷ Πιλάτῳ.

verses.english: And Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day, for before this they had been at enmity with each other.
verses.greek: ἐγένοντο δὲ φίλοι ὅ τε Ἡρῴδης καὶ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ μετ’ ἀλλήλων· προϋπῆρχον γὰρ ἐν ἔχθρᾳ ὄντες πρὸς αὐτούς.

verses.english: But they all cried out together, "Away with this man, and release to us Barabbas"—
verses.greek: Ἀνέκραγον δὲ παμπληθεὶ λέγοντες· Αἶρε τοῦτον, ἀπόλυσον δὲ ἡμῖν τὸν Βαραββᾶν·

verses.english: a man who had been thrown into prison for an insurrection started in the city and for murder.
verses.greek: ὅστις ἦν διὰ στάσιν τινὰ γενομένην ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ φόνον βληθεὶς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ.

verses.english: Pilate addressed them once more, desiring to release Jesus,
verses.greek: πάλιν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος προσεφώνησεν αὐτοῖς θέλων ἀπολῦσαι τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

verses.english: but they kept shouting, "Crucify, crucify him!"
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἐπεφώνουν λέγοντες· Σταύρου σταύρου αὐτόν.

verses.english: A third time he said to them, "Why? What evil has he done? I have found in him no guilt deserving death. I will therefore punish and release him."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ τρίτον εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν οὗτος; οὐδὲν αἴτιον θανάτου εὗρον ἐν αὐτῷ· παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω.

verses.english: But they were urgent, demanding with loud cries that he should be crucified. And their voices prevailed.
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἐπέκειντο φωναῖς μεγάλαις αἰτούμενοι αὐτὸν σταυρωθῆναι, καὶ κατίσχυον αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν.

verses.english: So Pilate decided that their demand should be granted.
verses.greek: καὶ Πιλᾶτος ἐπέκρινεν γενέσθαι τὸ αἴτημα αὐτῶν·

verses.english: He released the man who had been thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, for whom they asked, but he delivered Jesus over to their will.
verses.greek: ἀπέλυσεν δὲ τὸν διὰ στάσιν καὶ φόνον βεβλημένον εἰς φυλακὴν ὃν ᾐτοῦντο, τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν παρέδωκεν τῷ θελήματι αὐτῶν.

verses.english: Two others, who were criminals, were led away to be put to death with him.
verses.greek: Ἤγοντο δὲ καὶ ἕτεροι κακοῦργοι δύο σὺν αὐτῷ ἀναιρεθῆναι.

verses.english: And when they came to the place that is called The Skull, there they crucified him, and the criminals, one on his right and one on his left.
verses.greek: καὶ ὅτε ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Κρανίον, ἐκεῖ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς κακούργους, ὃν μὲν ἐκ δεξιῶν ὃν δὲ ἐξ ἀριστερῶν.

verses.english: It was now about the sixth hour, and there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour,
verses.greek: Καὶ ἦν ἤδη ὡσεὶ ὥρα ἕκτη καὶ σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης

verses.english: while the sun's light failed. And the curtain of the temple was torn in two.
verses.greek: τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος, ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ μέσον.

verses.english: Then Jesus, calling out with a loud voice, said, "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!" And having said this he breathed his last.
verses.greek: καὶ φωνήσας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Πάτερ, εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθεμαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου. τοῦτο δὲ εἰπὼν ἐξέπνευσεν.

verses.english: Now there was a man named Joseph, a member of the council, a good and righteous man,
verses.greek: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι Ἰωσὴφ βουλευτὴς ὑπάρχων καὶ ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ δίκαιος—

verses.english: who had not consented to their decision and action; he was from Arimathea, a Jewish town, and he was looking for the kingdom of God.
verses.greek: οὗτος οὐκ ἦν συγκατατεθειμένος τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτῶν— ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας πόλεως τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὃς προσεδέχετο τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ,

verses.english: This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
verses.greek: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ,

verses.english: Then he took it down and wrapped it in a linen shroud and laid him in a tomb cut in stone, where no one had ever yet been laid.
verses.greek: καὶ καθελὼν ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι, καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνήματι λαξευτῷ οὗ οὐκ ἦν οὐδεὶς οὔπω κείμενος.

verses.english: It was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was beginning.
verses.greek: καὶ ἡμέρα ἦν παρασκευῆς, καὶ σάββατον ἐπέφωσκεν.

verses.english: The women who had come with him from Galilee followed and saw the tomb and how his body was laid.
verses.greek: κατακολουθήσασαι δὲ αἱ γυναῖκες, αἵτινες ἦσαν συνεληλυθυῖαι ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας αὐτῷ, ἐθεάσαντο τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ ὡς ἐτέθη τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ,

verses.english: Then they returned and prepared spices and ointments. On the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.
verses.greek: ὑποστρέψασαι δὲ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα καὶ μύρα. Καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχασαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν.

notes.explanation: Tertullian (4.42.1) has the council accuse Jesus of calling himself "Christ, a king", and Pilate ask "Are you the Christ?". Epiphanius reports two additions in the charges of 23:2: "and destroying the law and the prophets" (sch. 69) and "and turning away the women and the children" (sch. 70). He answers the first from Matt 5:17 ("I came not to destroy the law and the prophets"), and says that the canonical text reads only "misleading the people". Old Latin manuscripts have the first addition at the same place, and c and e have the second at 23:5, so both readings were known outside Marcion's text. They are printed. 23:4–5 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian (4.42.2–4) reads the trial through Ps 2 and Isaiah: Herod receives Jesus "as a gift" from Pilate (Hos 10:6), is glad to see him and hears no word from him, as the lamb is silent before the shearer (Isa 53:7). Barabbas, "most guilty in life", is released as if good, and Christ, "most just", is demanded for death as a murderer. 23:13–16 form a paragraph that no witness cites and is not printed; NA27 has no 23:17.

Tertullian (4.42.4) attests the two criminals crucified with Jesus "so that he was counted among the lawless", and states that Marcion removed the dividing of his garments because of Ps 22:18; he answers that the whole psalm is Christ's garment. Epiphanius' scholion 71 mentions the dividing, but in a summary of the scene in Matthew's wording; Tertullian's statement is followed. Epiphanius states that "Today you will be with me in paradise" (23:43) was not in the text (sch. 72). Tertullian (4.42.5) attests the darkness at the sixth hour and the torn curtain, and (4.42.6) the loud cry to the Father and "having said this, he breathed his last", from which he argues that what breathes out a spirit is flesh. "Father, forgive them" (23:34a) is not in the NA27 text and is not cited by either witness. Simon of Cyrene, the daughters of Jerusalem, the mockery at the cross, the criminals' exchange, the centurion and the onlookers (23:26–31, 35–42, 47–49) are in paragraphs that no witness cites.

Tertullian (4.42.7–8) argues from the burial: if the body were a phantom, nothing would have been asked of Pilate, taken down from the cross, wrapped in linen or laid in a new tomb; Joseph, "who had not consented to the crime", knew it was a body. Epiphanius quotes Joseph taking down the body, wrapping it in linen and laying it in a rock-cut tomb (sch. 74), and the women returning and resting on the Sabbath "according to the law" (sch. 75). Tertullian (4.43.1) attests the women who came to the tomb with spices.

Interpretation. In this text the charge that Jesus destroys the law and the prophets is made by his accusers before Pilate, beside the charges about tribute and about turning away women and children; the narrative does not endorse it. Irenaeus (Haer. 1.27.2, as cited by Roth, 337 n. 230) reports that Marcion taught that Christ abolished the law and the prophets; that belongs to the reception of the text, not to its wording. The reading itself is old and not confined to Marcion's text, since the Old Latin has it. Epiphanius' charge that Marcion added the words assumes that canonical Luke is the earlier text.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 22
chapters.preamble: The Living One. At early dawn the women come to the tomb with spices and do not find the body. Two men in dazzling clothing say to them: "Why do you seek the Living One among the dead? He has been raised. Remember all that he told you while he was still in Galilee." The women report it, and the disciples do not believe them. On the road to Emmaus Jesus joins two of them, Cleopas and another, who do not recognize him. They say: "We thought that he was the one to redeem Israel." He answers: "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that he spoke to you!" At table he breaks the bread, and their eyes are opened. Then he stands among the disciples. They are afraid and think they see a spirit. He says: "See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself; for a spirit does not have bones as you see that I have." He asks for food. He sends them to proclaim repentance for the forgiveness of sins in his name to all the nations. No witness cites the text beyond this point.

verses.english: But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they went to the tomb, taking the spices they had prepared.
verses.greek: τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ὄρθρου βαθέως ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἦλθον φέρουσαι ἃ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα.

verses.english: And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
verses.greek: εὗρον δὲ τὸν λίθον ἀποκεκυλισμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου,

verses.english: but when they went in they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
verses.greek: εἰσελθοῦσαι δὲ οὐχ εὗρον τὸ σῶμα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.

verses.english: While they were perplexed about this, look, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἀπορεῖσθαι αὐτὰς περὶ τούτου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο ἐπέστησαν αὐταῖς ἐν ἐσθῆτι ἀστραπτούσῃ.

verses.english: And as they were frightened and bowed their faces to the ground, the men said to them, "Why do you seek the Living One among the dead?
verses.greek: ἐμφόβων δὲ γενομένων αὐτῶν καὶ κλινουσῶν τὰ πρόσωπα εἰς τὴν γῆν εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτάς· Τί ζητεῖτε τὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν;

verses.english: He has been raised. Remember all that he told you while he was still in Galilee,
verses.greek: ἠγέρθη. μνήσθητε ὅσα ἐλάλησεν ὑμῖν ἔτι ὢν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ,

verses.english: saying that the son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men and be crucified and on the third day rise."
verses.greek: λέγων τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὅτι δεῖ παραδοθῆναι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ σταυρωθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀναστῆναι.

verses.english: And they remembered his words,
verses.greek: καὶ ἐμνήσθησαν τῶν ῥημάτων αὐτοῦ,

verses.english: and returning from the tomb they told all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
verses.greek: καὶ ὑποστρέψασαι ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπήγγειλαν ταῦτα πάντα τοῖς ἕνδεκα καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς λοιποῖς.

verses.english: Now it was Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary the mother of James and the other women with them who told these things to the apostles,
verses.greek: ἦσαν δὲ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ Μαρία καὶ Ἰωάννα καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ σὺν αὐταῖς· ἔλεγον πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ταῦτα.

verses.english: but these words seemed to them an idle tale, and they did not believe them.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐφάνησαν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λῆρος τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα, καὶ ἠπίστουν αὐταῖς.

verses.english: That very day two of them were going to a village named Emmaus, about sixty stadia from Jerusalem,
verses.greek: Καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἦσαν πορευόμενοι εἰς κώμην ἀπέχουσαν σταδίους ἑξήκοντα ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ᾗ ὄνομα Ἐμμαοῦς,

verses.english: and they were talking with each other about all these things that had happened.
verses.greek: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡμίλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους περὶ πάντων τῶν συμβεβηκότων τούτων.

verses.english: While they were talking and discussing together, Jesus himself drew near and went with them.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὁμιλεῖν αὐτοὺς καὶ συζητεῖν καὶ αὐτὸς Ἰησοῦς ἐγγίσας συνεπορεύετο αὐτοῖς,

verses.english: But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν ἐκρατοῦντο τοῦ μὴ ἐπιγνῶναι αὐτόν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "What is this conversation that you are holding with each other as you walk?" And they stood still, looking sad.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίνες οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι οὓς ἀντιβάλλετε πρὸς ἀλλήλους περιπατοῦντες; καὶ ἐστάθησαν σκυθρωποί.

verses.english: Then one of them, named Cleopas, answered him, "Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in these days?"
verses.greek: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἷς ὀνόματι Κλεοπᾶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σὺ μόνος παροικεῖς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνως τὰ γενόμενα ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις;

verses.english: And he said to them, "What things?" And they said to him, "Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, a man who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ποῖα; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τὰ περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ, ὃς ἐγένετο ἀνὴρ προφήτης δυνατὸς ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ,

verses.english: and how our chief priests and rulers delivered him up to be condemned to death, and crucified him.
verses.greek: ὅπως τε παρέδωκαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν εἰς κρίμα θανάτου καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.

verses.english: But we thought that he was the one to redeem Israel. Yes, and besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
verses.greek: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐνομίζομεν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι τὸν Ἰσραήλ· ἀλλά γε καὶ σὺν πᾶσιν τούτοις τρίτην ταύτην ἡμέραν ἄγει ἀφ’ οὗ ταῦτα ἐγένετο.

verses.english: Moreover, some women of our company amazed us. They were at the tomb early in the morning,
verses.greek: ἀλλὰ καὶ γυναῖκές τινες ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξέστησαν ἡμᾶς, γενόμεναι ὀρθριναὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον

verses.english: and when they did not find his body, they came back saying that they had even seen a vision of angels, who said that he was alive.
verses.greek: καὶ μὴ εὑροῦσαι τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἦλθον λέγουσαι καὶ ὀπτασίαν ἀγγέλων ἑωρακέναι, οἳ λέγουσιν αὐτὸν ζῆν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that he spoke to you!
verses.greek: καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὦ ἀνόητοι καὶ βραδεῖς τῇ καρδίᾳ τοῦ πιστεύειν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐλάλησεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς·

verses.english: Was it not necessary that the Anointed One should suffer these things and enter into his glory?"
verses.greek: οὐχὶ ταῦτα ἔδει παθεῖν τὸν χριστὸν καὶ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ;

verses.english: So they drew near to the village to which they were going. He acted as if he were going farther,
verses.greek: Καὶ ἤγγισαν εἰς τὴν κώμην οὗ ἐπορεύοντο, καὶ αὐτὸς προσεποιήσατο πορρώτερον πορεύεσθαι.

verses.english: but they urged him strongly, saying, "Stay with us, for it is toward evening and the day is now far spent." So he went in to stay with them.
verses.greek: καὶ παρεβιάσαντο αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Μεῖνον μεθ’ ἡμῶν, ὅτι πρὸς ἑσπέραν ἐστὶν καὶ κέκλικεν ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα. καὶ εἰσῆλθεν τοῦ μεῖναι σὺν αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: When he was at table with them, he took the bread and blessed and broke it and gave it to them.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ κατακλιθῆναι αὐτὸν μετ’ αὐτῶν λαβὼν τὸν ἄρτον εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἐπεδίδου αὐτοῖς·

verses.english: And their eyes were opened, and they recognized him. And he vanished from their sight.
verses.greek: αὐτῶν δὲ διηνοίχθησαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν· καὶ αὐτὸς ἄφαντος ἐγένετο ἀπ’ αὐτῶν.

verses.english: As they were talking about these things, he himself stood among them, and said to them, "Peace to you!"
verses.greek: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτῶν λαλούντων αὐτὸς ἔστη ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.

verses.english: But they were startled and frightened and thought they saw a spirit.
verses.greek: πτοηθέντες δὲ καὶ ἔμφοβοι γενόμενοι ἐδόκουν πνεῦμα θεωρεῖν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί τεταραγμένοι ἐστέ, καὶ διὰ τί διαλογισμοὶ ἀναβαίνουσιν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν;

verses.english: See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself; for a spirit does not have bones as you see that I have."
verses.greek: ἴδετε τὰς χεῖράς μου καὶ τοὺς πόδας μου ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτός· ὅτι πνεῦμα ὀστέα οὐκ ἔχει καθὼς ἐμὲ θεωρεῖτε ἔχοντα.

verses.english: And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
verses.greek: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἔδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας.

verses.english: And while they still disbelieved for joy and were marvelling, he said to them, "Have you anything here to eat?"
verses.greek: ἔτι δὲ ἀπιστούντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς καὶ θαυμαζόντων εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἔχετέ τι βρώσιμον ἐνθάδε;

verses.english: They gave him a piece of broiled fish,
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἐπέδωκαν αὐτῷ ἰχθύος ὀπτοῦ μέρος·

verses.english: and he took it and ate before them.
verses.greek: καὶ λαβὼν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ἔφαγεν.

verses.english: … and that repentance for the forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in his name to all the nations.
verses.greek: … καὶ κηρυχθῆναι ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ μετάνοιαν εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη.

notes.explanation: Tertullian (4.43.1–5) follows the women who came "before light" with spices, the body not found, the two "angels", the women's return "from the tomb" and the disciples' persisting unbelief; he quotes the words of the two men: "Remember all that he told you in Galilee, that the son of man must be delivered and crucified and on the third day rise." Epiphanius (sch. 76) quotes "Why do you seek the Living One among the dead? He has been raised. Remember all that he told you while he was still with you." Two readings of this text are printed in 24:6: "all that" (ὅσα, both witnesses) and "he has been raised" without "he is not here, but" (Epiphanius, against his own habit of citation). "Of the Lord Jesus" (24:3) and "into the hands of sinful men" (24:7) are not cited and are printed with NA27.

Tertullian (4.43.3–5): two of them were travelling; the Lord joined them without showing who he was, and even pretended not to know what had happened; they said "we thought that he was the redeemer of Israel", and he rebuked them: "O foolish and slow of heart to believe all that he spoke to you." Epiphanius (sch. 77) names Cleopas and states that the text read "that I spoke to you" where canonical Luke has "that the prophets spoke", and quotes "was it not necessary that he suffer these things?" and the opening of their eyes when he broke the bread. Both witnesses agree that the rebuke was about Jesus' own words, not about the prophets. Tertullian's "we thought" and "he spoke to you" are printed. "A prophet mighty in deed and word" (24:19b) is not cited by either witness; it stands in the text as part of an attested verse.

Tertullian (4.43.6–8) quotes: "Why are you troubled, and why do thoughts arise in your hearts? See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself, for a spirit does not have bones as you see me having", and adds that Jesus asked for food "to show that he had teeth". Epiphanius (sch. 78) quotes the same verse with "bones" only. In this text there is no "handle me and see" and no "flesh and". Tertullian reports how Marcion read the end of the verse: "as you see me having" refers to the spirit, that is, "not having bones, as a spirit has none" (4.43.7). Eznik reports that the Marcionites based their abstinence from fish on Jesus' eating fish after his resurrection (De Deo 407, as quoted by Roth). "Peace to you" (24:36) and the showing of hands and feet (24:40), both lacking in D and the Old Latin, are not cited and are printed in grey.

No witness cites Peter's visit to the tomb (24:12) or the report of it (24:24); both are classed probably absent, since the linen cloths would have served Tertullian's argument and 24:12 is also lacking in D and the Old Latin. The interpretation of "Moses and all the prophets" (24:27), the burning hearts "while he opened to us the scriptures" (24:32) and "everything written about me in the law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms" with the opening of their minds (24:44–46) would have been Tertullian's proof that Jesus is the Christ of the prophets, the thesis with which he ends his book; neither witness cites them, and they are classed probably absent. The return to Jerusalem and the appearance to Simon (24:33–35) form a paragraph with no attested verse. Nothing after 24:47 is cited.

Tertullian ends his commentary on the gospel with Jesus "sending the apostles to preach to all the nations" (4.43.9). Whether the text went on, and how (the parting at Bethany, 24:50–51, or an ending like Acts 1:8–11), is not attested; the text is printed to the last attested verse. In canonical Luke 24:47 is governed by "thus it is written" (24:46); the words that introduced it in this text are not known.

Interpretation. Three layers are kept apart. (a) Text: the two men at the tomb call Jesus "the Living One" and say "he has been raised"; the disciples recognize him in the breaking of the bread; he answers their fear of a spirit by showing hands and feet and saying that a spirit does not have bones "as you see that I have"; he asks for food; he sends them to all the nations; the rebuke on the road is about believing his own words. (b) Canonical Luke has in addition the touch and the flesh (24:39), Peter at the tomb and the appearance to Simon (24:12, 24, 34), and the proof from Moses, the prophets and the psalms with the commissioning of the Eleven (24:27, 32, 44–49). On the Semler model these are a common original's; on the Schwegler model, additions; the witnesses show only that the text attested here lacked them. (c) Reception: the Marcionites read 24:39 as Jesus saying that he had no bones, like a spirit (Tertullian 4.43.7), and kept the meal of fish as the basis of their own practice (Eznik). The text itself holds together the Living One who is not found among the dead and a risen Jesus who can be seen, who eats, and who is recognized at table.
